With reference to the query of the Commissioner
of Police on the attached translation of a report entitled
"Amusement Resorts and the July 7 Anniversary" appearing in
the "Shanghai Daily News" ( 上海日報 ), a mosquito paper, of
July 10, 1938, Mr. Tseu Tsien-han ( 周劍寒 ), publisher of
the paper in question, was interviewed at Police Headquarters
on July 20 when he was warned against publishing untrue
reports.

Mr. Tseu expressed his regrets and stated that he
would publish a correction (translation attached) in his
paper and would exercise greater care in future.

Shanghai Daily News (上海日報) of July 21, 1938:

CORRECTION

On July 10 this paper published a report entitled
"Amusement Resorts and the July 7 Anniversary" in which
mention was made to the effect that the suspension of
stage performances by the Tai Wu Tan and the Carlton
Theatres on July 7 was due to the receipt of a notice
from the Shanghai Municipal Council.

Enquiries made show that the statement is untrue
because the Council adopts an absolutely neutral attitude
when dealing with matters in the Settlement. It had
nothing to do with this affair nor was there any necessity
for it to do so.

This paper hereby publishes a correction for
public information.

1938年7月21日《上海日报》（上海日報）：

更正

本报于7月10日刊登了一篇题为《娱乐场所与“七七”纪念》的报道，其中提及大舞台戏院和卡尔登大戏院于7月7日停止演出，原因是收到了上海工部局的通知。

经查询，该陈述不实，因为工部局在处理租界事务时采取绝对中立的态度。此事与工部局无关，工部局也无必要介入。

本报特此刊登更正，以正视听。

July 11, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Shanghai Daily News :-

AMUSEMENT RESORTS AND THE JULY 7 ANNIVERSARY

In compliance with a notification
received beforehand, all the amusement resorts suspended
business on July 7, the anniversary of the outbreak of
the Sino-Japanese hostilities. The Pekinese theatres
did not receive any notification and made preparations
to carry on business as usual, for they were afraid
that to suspend business on their own initiative under
present conditions might give rise to trouble.
On the day in question, the Kung Wu
Tan (共舞台) Theatre staged a matinee while the Tai
Wu Tan (大舞台) and the Carlton Theatres intended to
put on a night performance only, but in the end no
night performance was staged by any of the three theatres.
This, according to report, was due to the receipt of
a notice from the Shanghai Municipal Council.
It is said that while the matinee
was on at the Kung Wu Tan, the theatre received a
telephone message saying: "What day is it to-day? How
are the audience and the actors feeling?" The Tai Wu
Tan Theatre and the Carlton Theatre also received
telephone messages on July 7 from persons who made
sarcastic remarks about the managements' intention to
stage performances on that day.

《上海日报》:-

娱乐场所与“七七”纪念

根据事先收到的通知，所有娱乐场所在7月7日，即中日敌对行动爆发周年纪念日，暂停营业。京班戏院未收到任何通知，并准备照常营业，因为他们担心在目前形势下主动停业可能会引发麻烦。
当天，共舞台戏院上演了日场，而大舞台戏院和卡尔登大戏院原计划仅上演夜场，但最终这三家戏院均未上演夜场。据报道，这是因为收到了上海工部局的通知。
据说，在共舞台上演日场期间，戏院接到一个电话，问道：“今天是什么日子？观众和演员感觉如何？”大舞台戏院和卡尔登大戏院也在7月7日接到了电话，打电话的人对管理层打算在那天演出进行了讽刺。

Date July 11, 1936.

Subject Resolutions passed by Japanese Military and Civil
following incidents occurring on the "July 7 Anniversary"

Made by D.I. Kuh Tao Hwa Forwarded by C. Gaspard

Some twenty chiefs of the Intelligence Sections
of the Japanese Consulate-General, the Jiji News Agency,
the Japanese Military Police and of the Japanese Military
held a conference in the Japanese Club on Boone Road on
July 8, 1936. Apart from discussing appropriate measures
to be taken against the activities of Chinese secret service
agents
and recurrence of such incidents as those which occurred
during the early hours of July 7, the meeting passed the
following resolutions :-

1. That the Japanese Consulate-General be requested to
open negotiations with the Police Authorities of the
International Settlement and French Concession and
present a time limit for the apprehending of the persons
responsible for the outrages on Japanese Military, civilians
on July 7.

2. That both the Settlement Authorities and the French
Concession Authorities be requested to permit the
establishment of Japanese Special Service organs within
their jurisdiction to facilitate the investigation of
all cases wherein anti-Japanese elements are concerned
as well as Chinese military special service agents.

3. That privileges be granted, within the jurisdiction of
the two settlements to the Japanese Authorities to
exercise free police rights and the investigation and
power of arrest be also granted.

4. That the Police Authorities of the two Settlements be
requested to suppress the Chinese Anti-Japanese and
Traitor-Riddance Association and similar organizations.

5. That officers of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai
Municipal Administrative Office be despatched to the
two Settlements to conduct rigid investigations.

6. That Japanese and Chinese intelligence agents belonging
to various organs be instructed to redouble their efforts.

7. That capital punishment be meted out to members of anti-
Japanese and traitor-riddance associations and similar
organizations if arrested.

1936年7月8日，日本总领事馆、时事新闻社、日本宪兵队和日本军队的情报部门约二十名负责人在布恩路日本俱乐部召开会议。除了讨论针对中国特工活动以及再次发生类似7月7日凌晨事件应采取的适当措施外，会议还通过了以下决议：-

5. 派遣上海特别市行政办公室警察局官员前往两个租界进行严格调查。

Subject Visit to San Sing (三新) Printing Press, 8 Burkill Road.
Made by D.S. Pitts    Forwarded by [手写签名：C. Crawford S.D.]

On July 6, 1938, C.D.C.308 reported having
received information that coloured handbills and posters
were being prepared for distribution on July 7, the
first anniversary of the Lukouchiao Incident, and were
being printed at the San Sing Printing Press, 8 Burkill
Road. A watch was kept over these premises during
July 6 and members of this office accompanied by
detectives from Louza Station visited the address at
5.15 p.m. July 6. A search of the shop failed to reveal
any sign of pamphlets of a political nature whilst an
examination of the accounts books indicated that no
orders for brochures of this type had been placed.
The accountant of the printing shop, named
Doong Jing Nyih (童勤業), was warned regarding the
seriousness of printing anything relating to politics
at the present time and advised to refuse to receive
any such orders. He promised to inform Louza Station
should he at any time be requested to undertake any such
tasks and also stated that not only had he never
indulged in work of this nature but would under no
circumstances do so in the future.

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Gaspar.

It is learned that in observance of the 1st
anniversary of the Outbreak of the War of Resistance,
which falls on July 7, a "Youth's National Salvation
Association." (青年救亡协会) has decided to disseminate
national salvation and anti-Japanese propaganda matter on
that day. A copy of the handbill has been obtained and
is forwarded herewith. A summarized translation is as
follows :-

"An open letter to brethren in various walks of life

"One year has elapsed since the outbreak of the
war of resistance and the Government has designated July 7
as the "Day of the War of Resistance and re-Construction
of the Nation".

"During the past year, although much territory has
been lost, yet the battle line of the enemy has been
lengthened which is most beneficial to us in guerilla
warfare and our people and soldiers will in the end become
united more and more.

"During the past year, the inefficiency of the
enemy has been exposed. The air force of the enemy have
bombarded towns without any military defences. A large
number of people have died because of the barbarous acts
carried out by the enemy. We of course will demand revenge.
There will come a day, when our aeroplanes will fly to
Tokyo and drop bombs and in this way a warning will be given
to the Japanese Emperor and his shameless militarists.
We will employ a "tit for tat" policy towards the mean,
dirty, rash and shameless Japanese in carrying out our **〔此处转录不清〕**
revenge.

据悉，为纪念7月7日到来的抗日战争爆发一周年，“青年救亡协会” (Youth's National Salvation Association) 决定于当日散发救国及抗日宣传材料。已获取传单一份并随文附送。摘要译文如下：-

“致各界同胞的公开信

“自抗战爆发以来已过去一年，政府已将7月7日定为‘抗战建国纪念日’。

“在过去的一年中，虽然丧失了大量领土，但敌人的战线已被拉长，这对我们的游击战最为有利，且我国军民终将日益团结。

“在过去的一年中，敌人的无能已暴露无遗。敌军空军轰炸没有任何军事防御的城镇。因敌人实施的野蛮行径，大量民众死亡。我们当然要求复仇。总有一天，我们的飞机将飞抵东京投掷炸弹，以此向日本天皇及其无耻的军国主义者发出警告。我们将对卑鄙、肮脏、鲁莽且无耻的日本人采取‘以牙还牙’的政策，以实施我们的 **〔此处转录不清〕** 复仇。

"As to the economical condition, everyone knows of
the situation at present in Japan, but our own has not
been affected by the war and we strongly believe that the
final victory will be ours.

"Although Shanghai is in an isolated position,
every one of us will swear not to compromise with the
enemy or submit to the enemy's bayonets. We will exert
every effort to assist in the war of resistance until
such time as the enemy's forces leave Chinese territory.

"Brethren, no matter what kind of pressure is
brought to bear we should do our duty and make the supreme
sacrifice. We should not use the Settlement for enjoyment,
but support the soldiers at the front with our money.

"In order to commemorate the 1st anniversary of
the war of resistance and re-construction of the nation,
all brethren are requested to partake of a vegetable diet
to-day and to donate money thus saved to the "front" or
benevolent societies.

"The spirit of the deceased warriors never dies!

"Long Live the Three People's Principles!
"Long live the Republic of China!
"Long Live Generalissimo Chiang !

Translation of a handbill

The Lukouchiao incident was the cause of the outbreak
of Sino-Japanese hostilities. People who watch developments
in the war situation are daily praying for peace. Ever since
the war of resistance, Chiang Kai-shek has lost a large area
of territory, thereby causing heavy sufferings to millions of
people. However, the majority of the people who are under
the pressure of Chiang Kai-shek dare not utter a word despite
their anger. At present the National Government is propagating
a war of resistance, but the people are ignorant of the cause
of the war. All intelligent people desire peace, but cruel
and ambitious Chiang Kai-shek and the Communist Party are
shedding the blood of the 400 million Chinese people for their
own advantage and are remitting huge amounts of money to
foreign banks under the pretext of purchasing munitions.
They are also conspiring with the Soviet Union to bolshevize
China. It is a suicidal policy.

(批：See also
D 8509)

The dispute between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party,
the internal dissensions, the financial crisis and the
discontent among the people --- all constitute fatal blows
to Chiang Kai-shek's war of resistance. At present the
people of China are anxiously hoping for peace and their
attitude is being supported by

CONFIDENTIAL

Special Branch,
July 6, 1938.

Anniversary of Outbreak of Hostilities at Lukouchiao -
July 7, 1938

So far there are no indications that observance
of this Anniversary will take the form of demonstrations
or processions, although it is anticipated that there will
be dissemination, perhaps surreptitiously, of leaflets
bearing on the occasion. Refugee camps plan to hold short
memorial services, but, taking into consideration the rather
insolent attitude some of the inmates adopt towards the
police, it would not be surprising, were these services to
develop into open anti-Japanese lectures. Responsible
representatives of refugee camps have to-day given assurance
that they will cooperate with the police in the suppression
of any movement likely to result in disorder.

Any further information regarding possible dis-
turbances will be circulated through C.C.R..

Thos Robertson

Date July 5, 1938.
Subject Dan Yuin (大運) Refugee Camp convenes meeting, etc.
Made by D.S. Hide    Forwarded by [此处转录不清]

At about 2.30 p.m. on July 5, 1938, Inspector Trodd
attached to West Hongkew Station interviewed one Chen Ts
Ming (陳子銘), manager of the Dan Yuin Refugee Camp and
warned him that the Shanghai Municipal Police would not
permit the proposed meeting to be convened.

At 3.00 p.m. July 5, Chen Ts Ming was further
interviewed by members of the Special Branch who reiterated
the above warning. He stated the mimeograph with which
the letters were duplicated was borrowed from the Dee Loong
(德隆) Refugee Camp, 568/5, North Shanse Road.

Examination of the premises revealed receipts in
respect of twenty-seven letters dispatched to various
refugee camps and a draft of the points to be brought up
at the proposed meeting.

At the time the members of the Special Branch
arrived on the premises, several representatives of various
camps who had arrived to attend the meeting, were being
informed that it had been abandoned.

REPORT
Date July 5, 19 38.
Subject Dah Yuin Refugee Camp convenes meeting of representatives of refugees at 4 p.m. July 5 to discuss observance of "July 7" Anniversary.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Most of the refugee camps under the control of the Federation of Charity Organizations (35 Yunnan Road) are in possession of copies of a notice which were received on the afternoon of July 4. The notice purports to emanate from the Dah Yuin Refugee Camp of the Federation of Charity Organizations, 467 North Honan Road, and asks that a meeting be convened of representatives of refugees in the Dah Yuin Refugee Camp at 4 p.m. on July 5 to discuss the observance of the "First Anniversary of the War of Resistance" on July 7.
A full translation of the notice (copy attached) is as follows :-

"467 North Honan Road,
July 4.

"Dear Refugee Brethren:

"July 7" is the turning point in Chinese history, whereby the life or death of the Chinese race will be decided. It also marks the foundation for the construction of a new China.

The 1st Anniversary of the War For Racial Emancipation is fast approaching. The enemy has decided to occupy Hankow, which is the economical, political and cultural centre of China. The enemy is endeavouring to annihilate the strength of China in the war of resistance at one stroke.

In order to strengthen the force of resistance and to safeguard Hankow, we must decide to abstain from eating for one day and that on "July 7". The money thus saved will be remitted to the front for the consolation of the heroic warriors there. Should you agree with us, please assign representatives to attend our camp at 4 p.m. to-morrow (July 5) to hold discussions on the matter. The representatives are requested to bring with them this letter.

With a salute for the emancipation of the race,

All the refugees of the
Dah Yuin Refugee Camp (chop).

Kao Yen-ken
D.S.I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

主题：大裕（Dah Yuin）难民营于7月5日下午4时召开难民代表会议，讨论纪念“七七”周年事宜。
制作人：副督察高延根（Kao Yen-ken） 转呈人：**〔此处转录不清〕**

慈善组织联合会（云南路35号）管辖下的大多数难民营都持有7月4日下午收到的一份通知副本。该通知声称发自慈善组织联合会位于河南北路467号的大裕（Dah Yuin）难民营，并要求于7月5日下午4时在大裕难民营召开难民代表会议，讨论7月7日“抗战一周年”的纪念活动。
通知全文翻译如下（附副本）：-

“河南北路467号，
7月4日。

“亲爱的难民同胞们：

“七七”是中国历史的转折点，中华民族之生死存亡将由此决定。这也标志着新中国建设的基础。

种族解放战争一周年纪念日即将来临。敌人已决定占领作为中国经济、政治和文化中心的汉口。敌人正企图一举消灭中国在抗战中的力量。

为了加强抵抗力量并保卫汉口，我们必须决定在“七七”当天绝食一天。省下的钱款将汇往前线，以慰劳那里的英勇战士。如蒙同意，请指派代表于明日（7月5日）下午4时莅临本营，就此事项进行讨论。请各位代表携带此信前来。

谨祝种族解放，

大裕难民营全体难民（盖章）。

高延根
副督察

D. C.（特务科）。

Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by C. Cruickshank S.I.

With reference to the first anniversary of the
Lukouchiao incident of July 7, 1937, which resulted in the
current Sino-Japanese hostilities, a meeting was held at
the Japanese Club, Boone Road, at 2 p.m., June 25, to
discuss the function to be observed on July 7, 1938, in
commemoration of the incident. The meeting was attended
by representatives of various local Japanese organs such
as the Consulate-General, Army, Navy, Residents' Corporation,
Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Federation of Street
Unions etc.. In the course of the meeting, the
following matters were decided:-

1) That representatives of various public organs and
individuals should pay their respects at the "Shokon-
sha Shrine", which was dedicated to the memory of the
officers and men who fell in the action around Shanghai
in 1932, on the site of the Shanghai Shinto Shrine,
Kiangwan Road, at 8 a.m..

2) That a religious ceremony be held at the Shanghai
Shinto Shrine at 9 a.m. to pray for the success of the
Imperial Army.

in honour of officers and men who fell in the current
Sino-Japanese conflict.

4) That all of the local Japanese residents should
offer one minutes' prayer in honour of Japanese victims
of the current hostilities and also pray for the victory
of the Imperial Army, at 11 a.m..

5) That each Japanese family should contribute money

Made by Chief-Inspector Hirai Forwarded by....................................................

Sir,

Commemorating the outbreak of the present Sino-Japanese
hostilities, the following functions will be observed by the
Japanese community on July 7th, 1938.

(1) 8 a.m. At the Shokonsha Shrine, in the Shanghai Jinsha
compound, Kiangwan Road. A ceremony to pay respect
to the spirit of those fallen in the field.

(2) 9 a.m. At the Shanghai Jinshe Shrine, Kiangwan Road.
A prayer for unfoiling military success of those
officers and men in the field.

(3) 10 a.m. At the Chion-In Temple, corner N.Szechuen and
Darroch Roads. A memorial service in Buddhist rite
for the fallen officers and men.

(4) 11 a.m. One minute silent prayer by all individual members
of the Japanese community at the spot, even when
they may be driving a car. Police authorities
are requested to take note of this point.

（印：CITY COMMISSIONER 27 JUNE 1938 (DIVISIONAL)）

(5) 10 a.m. -- 4 p.m. Artificial flowers will be sold in the
street by members of the local Japanese Women's
Association.

At 9 a.m. on August 13th, at the Central Primary School on
Range Road, a memorial service for the fallen Naval and Military
officers and men will be held under the joint auspices of official
and civil personages.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Chief-Inspector.

Date July 19, 1938.

Subject Arrest of the shop master of the Dah Sing Printing Shop on July
5th, 1938,
Made by _______________ and _______________ Forwarded by D.L. Crawford

Li Hwan-tsang (李煥章), shop master of the Dah Sing
(大新) Printing Shop at Lane 134, House 18. Cunningham
Road was taken into custody on July 6th, 1938 by officers of
the Special Branch for printing pamphlets of an anti-
Japanese and national salvation nature. He has been detained
at West Hongkew Station since his arrest. On July 14th,
information was received by the personnel of the Special
Branch that a sum of money had been paid to effect the
release of this person and enquiries were immediately
instituted. It was discovered through the wife of the
prisoner that $100 had been paid to certain persons, who were
alleged to be friendly with certain employees of the
Municipal Police and that through their efforts, the release
of this person could be effected. $100 was only an instal-
ment a further $100 to be paid on his release.

Further discreet enquiries found that an employee of
the Printing office of the S.M.P. named Oo (胡 ) was keenly
interested in this case but although the wife and an
assistant in the prisoner's printing shop were carefully
interrogated no definite statement could be obtained that
the money which had been paid over and returned later had
been actually received by this person Oo.

Statements are attached which were taken from the wife
and assistant of the printing shop as to their part in the
scheme.

D.L.C.
19/7
P.A. to D.C. (S. Br.)

C. Crawford
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

事由 1938年7月5日逮捕大新印刷店店主一案，
由 ___ 和 ___ 制作，经 D.L. Crawford 转呈

大新印刷店店主李焕章（Li Hwan-tsang），店铺位于康宁路18号134弄，于1938年7月6日因印刷具有反日和救国性质的小册子，被特别处警员拘捕。自被捕以来，他一直羁押于虹口西捕房。7月14日，特别处人员获悉有人支付了一笔款项以图释放此人，随即展开调查。经向囚犯妻子查问，得知已向某些人支付了100元，据称这些人与工部局警务处的某些雇员关系友好，并通过他们的努力可以促成此人获释。这100元仅是首付款，在其获释时还需再付100元。

进一步的秘密调查发现，工部局警务处印刷所一名姓胡（Oo）的雇员对此案表现出浓厚兴趣，但尽管对囚犯的妻子及其印刷店的助手进行了仔细讯问，仍未能获得确凿陈述证明这笔已支付并随后退还的款项确实由该胡姓人员收受。

附件为从印刷店妻子和助手处取得的关于其在此阴谋中所扮演角色的供词。

D.L.C.
19/7
致副总监（特别处）私人助理

C. Crawford
督察长

副总监（特别处）

The following is the statement of Yang Wen-ching (楊文欽)

My name is Yang Wen-ching. I am a native of
Wusih, age 32, type setter of the Dah Sing (大新) Printing
Press, Lane 134, 18 Cunningham Rc 1. On July 6, 1938,
Li Hwan-tsang (李煥章), proprietor of the Printing Press,
was arrested by the Municipal Police for accepting orders
for printing handbills of a political nature. On July 8,
I called on one of my friend named Chow vong-yung in the
Chow Yah Kee Electro-Plating Works (周協記電鍍廠), Boundary
Road, to request him to enquire at the Police Station if
there was a possibility of his release. On July 17, Chow visit-
ed me and stated that a payment of $100 as a bribe for the
release of the proprietor by his family had been discovered
by the "Foochow Road" Police Station, and consequently the
prisoner could not be released. He further stated that the
money had been refunded.

About three or four days after his arrest by the
Police, I received a telephone message from the Tsing Nyien
(青年) Printing Press, Newchwang Road, telling me that
arrangements had been made for the release of Li, and that
I could cease my efforts in obtaining assistance to secure
his release.

As far as I know, one named Woo (name unknown)
of the Tsing Nyien Printing Press, Newchwang Road, and
one named Chien (錢), a rubber stamp dealer, who are
friends of Li Hwan-tsang, jointly made arrangements to
effect the release of Li. They paid $100 but to whom they
paid the money I do not know. Following enquiries by

The following is the statement of Li Tsai Sz (李蔡氏)

Li Tsai Sz, age 32, native of Wusieh, residing
at 18 Cunningham Road.

My husband, Li Hwan-tsang (李煥章), is the
proprietor of the Dah Sing Printing Shop (大新印刷所),
which has been established for a period of five years at
18 Cunningham Road. On July 6, 1938, he was arrested
by the Municipal Police for having undertaken the printing
of certain literature.

I immediately consulted with Yang Keng-shing
(楊根兴), type-setter of the Dah Sing Printing Shop,
in connection with the measures to secure the release of
my husband. He informed me that he had a friend (name
unknown) who could assist in this matter as he was
friendly with certain members of the Police Force. Yang
went out on the morning of July 7, and returned at noon
on the same day, when he stated that his friend was unable
to secure the release of my husband. Since then, Yang
Keng-shing has never mentioned the matter again.

On the forenoon of July 9, I went to the Tsing
Nyien (青年) Printing Shop, Newchwang Road and
interviewed Mr. Woo (吴), the proprietor of the shop,
who is a friend of my husband. I told him about the arrest
of my husband, and requested his assistance in dealing with
the matter. Mr. Woo stated that his friend Zien Yuan-
chong (錢元昌), a rubber stamp maker, was an
acquaintance with a Mr. Oo (伍), who would be able to
devise means for the release of my husband. He, however,

以下为李蔡氏（Li Tsai Sz）之供词，由其本人陈述，我，刑事侦缉督察施子良（Sih Tse-liang），于1938年7月13日在特别处录取，并由书记员罗伟公（Loh Wei-kong）翻译。

李蔡氏，现年32岁，籍贯无锡，居住于康宁路18号。

我的丈夫李焕章（Li Hwan-tsang）是大新印刷所（Dah Sing Printing Shop）的业主，该所在康宁路18号已开业五年。1938年7月6日，他因承印某些文献而被工部局警务处逮捕。

我立即与大新印刷所的排字工人杨根兴（Yang Keng-shing）商议，商讨确保我丈夫获释的措施。他告诉我，他有一位朋友（姓名不详）可以在此事上提供协助，因为他与警队某些成员关系友好。杨于7月7日上午外出，同日中午返回，当时他表示他的朋友无法确保我丈夫获释。此后，杨根兴再未提及此事。

7月9日上午，我前往新闸路青年印刷所，会见该所业主吴先生（Mr. Woo），他是我丈夫的朋友。我向他告知了我丈夫被捕的情况，并请求他协助处理此事。吴先生表示，他的朋友、橡皮图章制造商钱元昌（Zien Yuan-chong）认识一位伍先生（Mr. Oo），后者能够想出办法让我丈夫获释。然而，他

did not mention whether Mr. Co was connected with the
Police Force or not. On the following day, July 10,
Mr. Woo came to see me and stated that he had entrusted
the matter to Mr. Co. He further told me that a sum
of about $200.00 would be required to cover expenses
necessary for negotiation. I had no money handy and
told Mr. Woo so when he stated that the money question
could be settled after the release of my husband.

On the forenoon of July 13, a male Chinese came
to see me. He claimed that he was instructed by Mr. Woo
of the Tsing Nyien Printing Shop to inform me that my
husband would be released on Saturday, July 16. This was
found to be untrue.

Consequently I went to see Mr. Woo on July 16 and
asked him when the release of my husband would be effected.
He stated that he had been at the Police Headquarters to
act as guarantor for the release of Li Hwan-tsang, but was
refused by Headquarters and therefore he was unable to
secure my husband's release.

Since then, I have made no other overtures to Mr. Woo
for the release of my husband.

7月13日上午，一名中国男子来见我。他声称受青年印刷所吴先生指示前来通知我，我丈夫将于7月16日星期六获释。后经证实此言不实。

因此，我于7月16日去见吴先生，询问我丈夫何时能获释。他表示他曾去警察总局担任李焕章获释的担保人，但被总局拒绝，因此他无法确保我丈夫获释。

此后，我再未就我丈夫获释一事向吴先生提出其他请求。

Special Branch,
July 8, 1938.

Commissioner.

Sir,

In this instance we have not managed to
apprehend the principals, i.e. the persons responsible
for the order for printing, and I think the case would
be met with a week to ten days' detention plus a warning
of deportation on repetition of the offence and the
furnishing of a bond by some responsible person or
persons. To close the establishments would necessitate
provision of guards and at the moment Stations require
every man they have got. While the literature is
undoubtedly anti-Japanese in character, it lacks sting
and is mild to that appearing in past anti-Japanese
movements.

Establishments coming to notice in this
connection will be visited from time to time by
Special Branch detectives.

（批：Approved）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 8 JULY 1938 / Commissioner of Police / COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

Jho Rubentom
D. C. (Special Branch)

先生：

在此案中，我們未能抓獲主犯，即下達印刷命令的負責人。我認為，此案可通過拘留一至十天，並警告若再犯將予驅逐出境，以及由一名或多名擔保人提供保證金的方式來了結。關閉這些場所需要配備警衛，而目前各捕房人手緊張，需盡用所有警力。雖然該宣傳品無疑具有反日性質，但與過去反日運動中出現的內容相比，其鋒芒較弱，語氣溫和。

特務處偵探將不時視察与此類案件有關的場所。

"July 7" Anniversary - Seizure made by Special Branch.

Made by __________ and Forwarded by __________

Dah Sing Printing Press, Lane 134, 18 Cunningham Road -
1,000 Copies of a Handbill and a Set of Types Seized.

Acting on instructions of the D.C. (Special
Branch), D.S. McKeown, D.S.I. Kao Yen-keng, C.D.S. 156,
C.D.C.s 357 and 360, accompanied by D.S. Rossington of West
Hongkew Station, visited the Dah Sing (大興) Printing
Press, Lane 134, 18 Cunningham Road, at 12 noon on July 6.
As a result of a search, about 1,000 copies of an anti-
Japanese leaflet purporting to emanate from the "Youth's
National Salvation Association" and bearing on the "July 7"
Anniversary (Outbreak of Hostilities at Lukuchiao in 1937)
and a set of type for the handbill were seized. A summarized
translation of the handbill appears in a Special Branch report
made by D.S.I. Kao on the same subject on July 6. A copy
of the seizure is attached as "A".

The proprietor and manager of the shop, Li
Hwei-chwang (李章) was arrested and detained in West
Hongkew Station for investigation, pending instructions.
The person who placed the order, according to the proprietor,
declared that he would come between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. July 6,
and take away the printed handbills. Therefore detectives
were posted on the premises to wait for the arrival of the
man concerned, who, however, failed to visit the shop on
July 6.

Further investigations made from the staff of
the press revealed that the person who placed the order claimed
to be sent by an old customer of the press who is a teacher
of the Tsing Teh Primary School (正德小学), Lane 696, 14 Haining
Road. At 4.10 p.m. a visit was paid to the above-mentioned

根據特務處副處長的指示，麥基恩副督察（D.S. McKeown）、高延庚副督察（D.S.I. Kao Yen-keng）、華籍高級偵探156號、華籍偵探357號和360號，在西虹口捕房羅斯辛頓副督察（D.S. Rossington）的陪同下，於7月6日中午12時前往康寧路18號134弄的大興（大興）印刷廠。經搜查，查獲約1,000份反日傳單，聲稱出自「青年救國會」，內容涉及「七七」紀念日（1937年盧溝橋事變爆發），並查獲該傳單的字模一套。傳單的摘要譯文見高副督察於7月6日就同一主題所作的特務處報告。查獲物品清單副本作為附件「A」。

該店業主兼經理李章（Li Hwei-chwang）被捕，並羈押於西虹口捕房以待進一步指示進行調查。據業主稱，下訂單的人聲明將於7月6日下午3時至4時之間前來取走印好的傳單。因此，偵探在該處守候該人的到來，然而該人於7月6日並未到店。

對印刷廠員工的進一步調查顯示，下訂單的人聲稱是由該印刷廠的一位老顧客派來的，這位顧客是海寧路14號696弄正德小學（Tsing Teh Primary School）的一名教師。下午4時10分，探員前往上述

While the raid was in progress Mr. Tsai arrived
at his office and subsequently he and one Ho Chien Tsung
(何建春), chief cashier of the camp, were brought to
S.M.P. Headquarters and severely cautioned against taking
part in political activities and particularly against printing
propaganda literature.

Mr. W.E. Souter and Mr. T.F. Chu, both members of
the International Relief Committee under whose auspices the
refugee camp in question is conducted, visited S.M.P. Head-
quarters on the afternoon of 7th July and Mr. Chu was cautioned
regarding the folly of permitting political activity in the camps
under the control of his committee.

C. Crawford

Translation of a handbill purporting to have emanated
from the Youth's National Salvation Association
----------
"An open letter to brethren in various walks of life

"One year has elapsed since the outbreak of the
war of resistance and the Government has designated July 7
as the "Day of the War of Resistance and Re-construction
of the Nation."

"During the past year, although much territory has
been lost, yet the battle line of the enemy has been
lengthened which is most beneficial to us in guerilla
warfare and our people and soldiers will in the end become
united more and more.

"During the past year, the inefficiency of the
enemy has been exposed. The air force of the enemy have
bombarded towns without any military defences. A large
number of people have died because of the barbarous acts
carried out by the enemy. We of course will demand revenge.
There will come a day, when our aeroplanes will fly to
Tokyo and drop bombs and in this way a warning will be given
to the Japanese Emperor and his shameless militarists.
We will employ a "tit for tat" policy towards the mean,
dirty, rash and shameless Japanese in carrying out our
revenge.

"As to the economical condition, everyone knows of
the situation at present in Japan, but our own has not
been affected by the war and we strongly believe that the
final victory will be ours.

"Although Shanghai is in an isolated position,
every one of us will swear not to compromise with the enemy
or submit to the enemy's bayonets. We will exert every
effort to assist in the war of resistance until
such time as the enemy's forces leave Chinese territory.

"Brethren, no matter what kind of pressure is
brought to bear we shall do our duty and make the supreme
sacrifice. We should not use the Settlement for enjoyment,
but support the soldiers at the front with our money.

"In order to commemorate the 1st anniversary of
the war of resistance and re-construction of the nation,
all brethren are requested to partake of a vegetable diet
to-day and to donate money thus saved to the "front" or
benevolent societies.

"The spirit of the deceased warriors never dies!

"Down with Japanese Militarists!

"Long Live the Three People's Principles!

"Long live the Republic of China!

"Long live Generalissimo Chiang!

"The Final Victory will be ours!

Youth's National Salvation Association
July 7."

聲稱出自青年救國會的傳單譯文
---
「致各界同胞的公開信

「抗戰爆發至今已滿一年，政府定7月7日為『抗戰建國紀念日』。

「過去一年中，雖然喪失了大量領土，但敵人的戰線拉長，這對我們的游擊戰極為有利，我國人民和士兵終將更加團結。

「過去一年中，敵人的無能暴露無遺。敵軍空襲毫無軍事防禦的城鎮。大量民眾死於敵人的野蠻行徑。我們當然要求復仇。總有一天，我們的飛機將飛抵東京投彈，以此向日本天皇及其無恥的軍閥發出警告。我們將對卑鄙、骯髒、魯莽和無恥的日本人採取『以牙還牙』的政策來實施復仇。

「至於經濟狀況，眾所周知日本目前的局勢，而我國未受戰爭影響，我們堅信最終勝利屬於我們。

「雖然上海處於孤立地位，但我們每個人都誓不與敵人妥協或屈服於敵人的刺刀。我們將竭盡全力協助抗戰，直到敵軍撤出中國領土。

「同胞們，無論面臨何種壓力，我們都將履行職責並做出最大犧牲。我們不應利用租界享受安逸，而應用金錢支援前線將士。

「為紀念抗戰建國一週年，懇請各位同胞今日素食，並將省下的錢款捐贈給『前線』或慈善團體。

「陣亡將士精神不死！

「打倒日本軍閥！

「三民主義萬歲！

「中華民國萬歲！

「蔣委員長萬歲！

「最終勝利屬於我們！

青年救國會
7月7日。」

"July 7" Anniversary - seizure made by Special Branch.

Dah Sing Printing Press, Lane 134, 18 Cunningham Road -
1,000 Copies of a Handbill and a Set of Types Seized.

Acting on instructions of the D.C. (Special
Branch), D.S. McKown, D.S.I. Kao Yen-keng, C.D.C. 156,
C.D.C.s 357 and 360, accompanied by D.S. Rossington of West
Hongkew Station, visited the Dah Sing (大新) Printing
Press, Lane 134, 18 Cunningham Road, at 12 noon on July 6.
As a result of a search, about 1,000 copies of an anti-
Japanese leaflet purporting to emanate from the "Youth's
National Salvation Association" and bearing on the "July 7"
Anniversary (Outbreak of Hostilities at Lukuchiao in 1937)
and a set of types for the handbill were seized. A summarized
translation of the handbill appears in a Special Branch report
made by D.S.I. Kao on the same subject on July 6. A copy
of the seizure is attached as "A".

The proprietor and manager of the shop, Li
Hwei-chwang (李煥章) was arrested and detained in West
Hongkew Station for investigation, pending instructions.

declared that he would come between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. July 6,
and take away the printed handbills. Therefore detectives
were posted on the premises to wait for the arrival of the
man concerned, who, however, failed to visit the shop on
July 6.

Further investigations made from the staff of
the press revealed that the person who placed the order claimed
to be sent by an old customer of the press who is a teacher
of the Tsing Teh Primary School (正德小学), Lane 696, 14 Haining
Road. At 4.10 p.m. a visit was paid to the above-mentioned

康宁路（Cunningham Road）18号134弄大新印刷所——
查扣传单1,000份及铅字一副。

根据特务处副督察长（D.C.）的指示，副督察麦考恩（McKown）、华籍副督察高延庚（Kao Yen-keng，警员编号156）、华籍探目357号和360号，在西区虹口站副督察罗辛顿（Rossington）的陪同下，于7月6日中午12时前往康宁路18号134弄的大新（大新）印刷所。经搜查，查扣了约1,000份据称由“青年救国会”发出的、涉及“七七”纪念日（1937年卢沟桥事变爆发）的反日传单，以及用于印制该传单的铅字一副。传单的摘要译文见于高副督察同日就同一主题提交的特务处报告。查扣物品清单副本作为附件“A”附后。

该店店主兼经理李煥章（Li Hwei-chwang）被捕，并羁押于西区虹口站以待进一步指示并进行调查。据店主称，下单者声称将于7月6日下午3时至4时之间前来取走印好的传单。因此，探员被部署在该处守候相关人员到来，但该人并未于7月6日光顾该店。

通过对印刷所员工的进一步调查得知，下单者声称是由该印刷所的一位老客户派来的，这位客户是海宁路14号696弄正德小学（Tsing Teh Primary School）的一名教师。下午4时10分，有人造访了上述

pages.en:
- 2 -

school, but it was found that the teacher was absent.
Arrangements were made with the headmaster of the school
named Francis Chang (張夢迪) to have the teacher named
Teng Pah-tseng (伯志) to attend West Hongkew Station
on the morning of July 7. Teng, however, called at West
Hongkew Station at 5.30 p.m. He denied having sent or
that he knew the person who placed the order for printing
the handbill.

Observation has been maintained on the
premises.

Zung Vung (人众) Printing Press, Lane 406, 40 Shanhaikwan
Road - 2,000 Copies of Handbill Seized.

At 5 p.m. July 6, D.S. McKeown, D.S.I. Kao
Yen-keng, C.D.S. 156, C.D.C.s 199, 357 and 360 in conjunction
with D.S.I. Watson and C.D.C. 333 of Sinza Station raided
the Zung Vung Printing Press, Lane 406, 40 Shanhaikwan Road.
2,000 copies of the same handbill referred to in the case
of the Dah Sing Printing Press on Cunningham Road, but
printed in a different form (sample attached as "B"),
together with a draft of the handbill, were seized. The
proprietor of the shop named Loh Pah-sung (洛伯成) and
the type-setter named Loh Ling-sung (洛林生), who received
the order for printing, were taken to Sinza Station and are
detained there pending instructions.

According to the statement of the type-setter,
the person who placed the order, claimed to be from the
Woo Shih (核實) Primary School, 248 Shanhaikwan Road. A
pages.zh:
- 2 -

学校，但发现该教师不在。校方安排与名为张梦迪（Francis Chang）的校长协调，让名为邓伯志（Teng Pah-tseng，音译：滕柏增/邓伯志）的教师于7月7日上午前往西区虹口站。然而，邓某于下午5时30分才来到西区虹口站。他否认曾派遣或认识那位下单印制传单的人。

已对该处所保持监视。

据排字工人陈述，下单者声称来自山海关路248号核实（Woo Shih）小学。一名

pages.en:
- 3 -

visit was therefore paid to the school at 6.05 p.m., but
the man concerned could not be located.

A watch by detectives has been kept on the
premises of the printing press with a view to arresting
the person responsible for the handbill.

D. S.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

探员遂于下午6时05分前往该校，但未能找到相关人员。

探员已在印刷所处所进行监视，以期逮捕负责该传单的人员。

D. S.

探员已在印刷所处所进行监视，以期逮捕负责该传单的人员。

Translation of Extracts from literature seized
at the third Refuge Camp of the International
Relief Society, Luzon Road, on July 7:-

(Separate list of seized literature attached).

(1) Translation from Item No. 2 in the list:-
(Chien Ngoo Weekly page 6)

"Go to the front and carry out a desperate struggle
against the enemy. Quickly kill enemy soldiers and
rush into the enemy's defence lines."

(2) Translation from Item No. 3 in the list:-
(Loose sheets of Chien Ngoo Weekly)

Pages 10 and 11

"Of course you are not a combatant. But who have destroyed
your farm, your business and your home? You should
have a clear knowledge of your enemy for he is a merciless
butcher of our countrymen. There is no country in the
world that is in sympathy with our enemy who will be
butchered by some others some day. We expect the approach
of the day of final victory and to redress our humiliations."

Page 13

"A number of insane persons have become traitors following
the fall of Hsuchow and they are shamelessly working for
the enemy. In our endeavours to get rid of traitors, we
must instil political knowledge into those whom we suspect
of being traitors so that they will refrain from becoming
traitors. As regards these who have already become
traitors, we must deal with them severely by actions and
by moral pressure."

Pages/ 9.

" X X are monsters who are disregarding justice and
humanity. They are working for their own destruction
and their end is near."

* July 7 is the day when the X X devils, who **〔此处转录不清〕** spent
sixty years in making preparations, started hostilities
at Loukouchiao at the instigation of their young
militarists. (Here follows an account of the incident.)"

Page 3

"Commemoration of the July 7th Incident.
This is the day when China's anti-Japanese and national
salvation war made a start. Let us commemorate this
day of great significance.
After one year's fighting, we can be sure of getting
a final victory. Although the "barbarous robbers"
are gaining grounds, our resistance has become stronger
and stronger."

Page 14

This page contains an incomplete copy of a story
entitled " The Big Swords Corps bravely kill the enemy."
(Dealing with the Loukouchiao incident.)

7月7日在国际救济协会吕宋路第三难民收容所查扣文献的摘录译文：-

（附查扣文献单独清单）。

(1) 清单第2项译文：-
（《建吴周刊》第6页）

“上前线，与敌人进行殊死搏斗。迅速击杀敌军士兵，冲入敌方防线。”

(2) 清单第3项译文：-
（《建吴周刊》散页）

第10和11页

“当然，你不是战斗人员。但是谁摧毁了你的农场、生意和家园？你应该清楚地了解你的敌人，因为他是对我们同胞无情的屠夫。世界上没有哪个国家会同情我们的敌人，他们总有一天会被其他人屠杀。我们期待最终胜利日的到来，以雪耻辱。”

第13页

“徐州失守后，一些疯子变成了汉奸，他们厚颜无耻地为敌人工作。在铲除汉奸的努力中，我们必须向那些被怀疑是汉奸的人灌输政治知识，使他们不再成为汉奸。至于那些已经成为汉奸的人，我们必须通过行动和道德压力严厉处置他们。”

第9页。

“ X X 是无视正义和人性的怪物。他们正在自取灭亡，末日将近。”

* 7月7日是 X X 魔鬼的日子，他们 **〔此处转录不清〕** 花了六十年时间做准备，在其年轻军国主义者的煽动下，在卢沟桥发动了敌对行动。（此处接着叙述事件经过。）”

第3页

“纪念七七事变。
这是中国反日救国战争开始的日子。让我们纪念这个具有重大意义的日子。
经过一年的战斗，我们可以确信获得最终胜利。虽然‘野蛮强盗’正在取得进展，但我们的抵抗越来越强大。”

第14页

本页包含一篇题为《大刀队英勇杀敌》的故事的不完整副本。
（涉及卢沟桥事变。）

Date July 6th, 19 38

Subject Seizure of Anti-Japanese Pamphlets.

Made by D.J. Rossington Forwarded by [Signature] Inspector,
Officer I/C

Sir,

At 12 noon on the 6-7-38, D.S. McKeown attached to S. I.
together with a number of Chinese detectives, came to the
station and requested assistance to carry out a search at the
Dah Shing (大盛) Printing Works, No. 18/154 Cunningham Road,
where it was suspected that pamphlets of an anti-Japanese nature
were being printed.

Assistance was given by C.D.C. 265 and the undersigned and
on a visit being paid to the aforementioned address, approxima-
tely 1,000 pamphlets and one block of print was seized from a
front downstairs room.

A translation of the pamphlets reads as follows:-

"An open letter to brethren in various walks of life.

"One year has elapsed since the outbreak of the war of
resistance and the Government has designated July 7 as the
"Day of the War of Resistance and Re-construction of the Nation".

"During the past year, although much territory has been
lost, yet the battle line of the enemy has been lengthened
which is most beneficial to us in guerilla warfare and our
people and soldiers will in the end become united more and more.

"During the past year, the inefficiency of the enemy has
been exposed. The air force of the enemy have bombarded towns
without any military defences. A large number of people have
died because of the barbarous acts carried out by the enemy.
We of course will demand revenge. There will come a day, when
our aeroplanes will fly to Tokyo and drop bombs and in this
way a warning will be given to the Japanese Emperor and his
shameless militarists. We will employ a "tit for tat" policy

先生，

1938年7月6日中午12时，附属于特别情报股（S. I.）的警司麦基恩（D.S. McKeown）连同数名华籍侦探来到本捕房，请求协助对位于康宁路（Cunningham Road）18/154号的大盛印刷厂进行搜查，据怀疑该处正在印制具有反日性质的传单。

华籍侦探主任第265号及本人提供了协助，在对上述地址进行查访时，从楼下前间查获约1,000份传单及一块印版。

传单的译文如下：-

“致各界同胞的一封公开信。

“自抗战爆发以来已过去一年，政府指定7月7日为
‘抗战建国纪念日’。

“在过去的一年中，虽然丧失了大量领土，但敌人的战线已被拉长，这对我们的游击战最为有利，且我国军民终将更加团结。

“在过去的一年中，敌人的无能已暴露无遗。敌空军轰炸没有任何军事防御的城镇。大量民众因敌人实施的野蛮行径而死亡。我们当然要求复仇。总有一天，我们的飞机将飞临东京投掷炸弹，以此向日本天皇及其无耻的军国主义者发出警告。我们将采取‘以牙还牙’的政策

towards the mean, dirty, rash and shameless Japanese in carry-
ing out our revenge.
"As to the economic condition, everyone knows of the
situation at present in Japan, but our own has not been affected
by the war and we strongly believe that the final victory will
be ours.
"Although Shanghai is in an isolated position, every one
of us will swear not to compromise with the enemy or submit
to the enemy's bayonets. We will exert every effort to
assist in the war of resistance until such time as the enemy's
forces leave Chinese territory.
"Brethren, no matter what kind of pressure is brought to
bear we shall do our duty and make the supreme sacrifice. We
should not use the Settlement for enjoyment, but support the
soldiers at the front with our money.
"In order to commemorate the 1st anniversary of the war
of resistance and re-construction of the nation, all brethren
are requested to partake of a vegetable diet to-day and to
donate money thus saved to the "front" or benevolent societies.
"The spirit of the deceased warriors never dies!
"Down with Japanese Militarists!
"Long live the Three People's Principles!
"Long Live the Republic of China!.
"Long Live Generalissimo Chiang!
"The Final Victory will be ours!
Youth's National Salvation Association
July 7".

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Assistance to Special Branch re. Pamphlets.

At 7-40pm. on 7/7/38 D. McKeown, S.I. Kao Yen Sen, C.D.C. 156, and C.D.C.s 199, 357 and 360, all attached to S.I., attended this station to obtain assistance to visit the Woo Yung( 人 ) Printing Works, No.70, Lane 240 Chardillon Road, it having been reported to S.I. that pamphlets of an anti-Japanese nature, and in connection with the anniversary of the outbreak of hostilities on July 7th., had been printed there.

C.D.C. 333 and the undersigned accompanied the party to that address, and in a drawer on the upper floor the draft of the pamphlet was found. The type-setter named Loh Ling Sung( 陸林生 ), 26, Changchow, then admitted that at about 3-30pm. on 5/7/38 a male Chinese who gave his name as Wong Yang( 汪楊 ), and his address as the Woo Shih( 務實 ) School, No.243 Shanhaikwan Road, had ordered the pamphlets from him. He had paid $3.00 for two thousand of the pamphlets and had given the above type-setter the seized draft.

The manager named Loh Pah Zung( 陸伯盛 ), 34, Changchow, then produced the 2000 pamphlets, and same were recognized by the detectives from S.I. as similar to others already seized on 6/7/38 in various districts.

华籍侦探主任第333号及本人陪同该组人员前往上述地址，在楼上的一个抽屉里发现了传单草稿。排字工人陆林生（Loh Ling Sung），26岁，常州人，随即承认，1938年7月5日下午3时30分左右，一名自称汪杨（Wong Yang）的中国男子，地址为山海关路243号务实学校（Woo Shih School），向他订购了这些传单。他为两千份传单支付了3.00元，并将被查获的草稿交给了上述排字工人。

经理陆伯盛（Loh Pah Zung），34岁，常州人，随后拿出了2000份传单，特别情报股的侦探认出这些传单与1938年7月6日在各区查获的其他传单相似。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The type-setter stated that the customer was to call for the pamphlets on the evening of 6/7/38, failing which they were to be delivered to the Foo Chih School.

Detectives were accordingly placed in the Printing Factory to arrest this man should he call, and the above School was visited.

The Principal named Feng Dah Fu(馮達夫) stated that no person of the name given is a student there. The type-setter viewed all persons then in the School but did not identify the purchaser.

The type-setter and the manager were then brought to this station, and on the instructions of the D.C.(Special Branch) they will not appear before the Court, but will be detained at this station pending further instructions.

The pamphlets have been removed to the Special Branch, and purport to emanate from the Youth's National Salvation Association, which is a secret organization.

At 8.45 a.m. 7/7/38 one named Koch Wen Lan (郁文煥),
officer i/c. of the Zu Yuen (慈願) refugee camp along
Zong Ai Wan Tang Cemetery, off North Chekiang Road came to
the station and reported that one of the refugees named
Koo Tseng (顧鋒) had attempted to instigate the children
to hold a demonstration in commemoration of the anniversary.

Inquiries made by S.I. and the undersigned brought
to light the following facts. At about 6 a.m. on 7/7/38
the above refugee succeeded in summoning 21 juvenile refugees
(whose ages range from 11 to 15) to gather in the compound
inside the cemetery. He then gave them 20 cents each as
breakfast money and told them to hold a procession along
Nanking Road and to shout the following slogans:-

1) Down with Japanese Imperialism.
2) Kill all Traitors.
3) Support the Government to defend to the end.
4) Long live Chinese Race.
5) Long live China.

Furthermore they were told to throw pebbles at Japanese
pedestrians whom they might have met on the way. After the
departure of the instigator, the children began to whisper
to each other, thus attracting the suspicion of the camp
guard named Wong San Chiu (王三川). An interrogation of
the children disclosed the plot and the Officer i/c. was
informed.

The wanted Koo Tseng was formerly a teacher in the
Zang Kong Refugee Camp, 160 Alabaster Road and resided in
the Zu Yuen Refugee Camp as ordinary refugee since 16/5/38
when the former camp was amalgamated with the latter.
The staff of the camp and the children have been instructed

1938年7月7日上午8时45分，一名名为郁文煥（Koch Wen Lan）的男子前来警署报案。他是位于浙江北路旁宗爱湾塘公墓沿线的慈願（Zu Yuen）难民收容所的负责人。他报告称，一名名为顧鋒（Koo Tseng）的难民企图煽动儿童举行纪念周年活动的示威游行。

经巡官（S.I.）及本报告人调查，查明以下事实。1938年7月7日上午6时许，上述难民成功召集21名少年难民（年龄介于11至15岁之间）在公墓内的院落集合。随后，他发给每人20分作为早餐费，并指示他们沿南京路举行游行，高呼以下口号：-

1) 打倒日本帝国主义。
2) 杀尽汉奸。
3) 拥护政府抗战到底。
4) 中华民族万岁。
5) 中国万岁。

此外，他们还被告知向途中遇到的日本行人投掷石子。煽动者离开后，孩子们开始互相耳语，从而引起了名为王三川（Wong San Chiu）的收容所警卫的怀疑。经对孩子们进行讯问，阴谋败露，随即通知了负责人。

被通缉的顧鋒此前是阿拉巴斯特路160号藏公（Zang Kong）难民收容所的教师，自1938年5月16日前者合并入后者以来，他以普通难民身份居住在慈願难民收容所。收容所工作人员及儿童已接到指令

which place it was extracted. Another bullet entered
the base of the skull but has not been extracted.
Both shots were ascertained to have been fired at close
range.

The bullet, together with the four cartridge
cases found on the scene, were forwarded to the Arms
Identification Section where, on examination, it was
found that the bullet had been fired from the same
weapon which was used in the murder of a male Chinese
in Chengtu Road District on 28-5-38 (F.I.R. 625/35 Ch.
Rd.). Investigations in this direction are therefore
proceeding. The bullet was handed over to the under-
signed on the understanding that same would be returned
to the Japanese Military Authorities when the Police
examination was completed. The bullet has been duly
returned but in view of this development its importance
as an exhibit in a possible future prosecution was
stressed to the Authorities concerned. They were given
to understand that if the bullet was returned to Police
custody it could be at their disposal at any time they

At 5.45 a.m. 7/7/38, a telephone message was
received from J.P.C.147 reporting that a Japanese
had been shot on Markham Road.

The station alarm was rung, and a party of
police under Inspector White immediately attended.
On arrival at Markham and Tonquin Roads corner, a
Japanese was found slumped down in a public riosha
bleeding profusely.

The Emergency Ambulance was called and the
wounded man was removed to the Foo Ming Hospital
where the following certificate was issued:- " A
bullet wound on head (died)". The riosha was resting
at an oblique angle to the North kerb where it was
abandoned by the coolie who absconded after the
shooting took place. Four empty cartridge cases
which appear to be of .32 calibre were found at
the scene, three in the gutter on the South side
of the roadway and the other just beside the
abandoned riosha.

Subsequent enquiries ascertained the deceased
to be Yasujiro Shiraishi, age 53, residing at the
N.W.K.No.1 Mill Quarters, 62 Robison Road O.O.L.
The deceased has for the last four years been
employed in the Finishing Room of the N.W.K. No.9
Mill, Markham Road. During that period, it has
been his daily habit to proceed from his quarters
to his place of employment via Gordon and Markham
Roads by public riosha at about 5.30 a.m. every day.

At 5.40 a.m. to-day, 7/7/38, he was proceed-
ing as usual East along Markham Road by public

1938年7月7日上午5时45分，接到来自J.P.C.147的电话报告，称一名日本人在马克姆路（Markham Road）遭枪击。

警署警报响起，怀特（White）巡官率领一队警员立即赶赴现场。抵达马克姆路与通金路（Tonquin Road）转角处时，发现一名日本人瘫倒在一辆公共人力车中，大量出血。

急救救护车被召来，伤者被送往福民医院（Foo Ming Hospital），院方出具了以下证明：“头部枪伤（死亡）”。该人力车呈斜角停靠在北侧路缘石旁，车夫在枪击发生后弃车潜逃。在现场发现了四枚空弹壳，看似为.32口径，其中三枚位于道路南侧的排水沟内，另一枚就在被遗弃的人力车旁。

后续调查查明，死者名为白石安次郎（Yasujiro Shiraishi），53岁，居住于外白渡桥西北区（N.W.K.）第一纱厂宿舍，罗宾森路（Robison Road）62号，越界筑路区域（O.O.L.）。死者过去四年受雇于马克姆路西北纺织公司（N.W.K.）第九纱厂的整理间。在此期间，他每天早晨约5时30分乘坐公共人力车，经由戈登路（Gordon Road）和马克姆路，从宿舍前往工作地点，这已成为他的日常习惯。

今日，1938年7月7日上午5时40分，他像往常一样乘坐公共

ricsha. On arrival at the intersection of Tonquin

An examination of the ricsha showed that a bullet

The ricsha, S.M.C.License No.8750 was ascer-

Enquiries were made at this address and the
ricsha owner stated that after shooting the ricsha
coolie, who lives at the same address, returned and
explained the case to him. He ( the ricsha owner ) advis-
ed him to report the matter to the police of Gordon
Road Station immediately. The coolie promised to do
so, and left the premises. He has, however, not been
seen since. The ricsha owner was unable to give his
proper name but stated that he was known as Wei Siam

人力车沿马克姆路向东行进。到达通金路交叉口时，四名站在南侧人行道上的中国男子（持械数量不明）突然近距离开火。人力车夫猛拐穿过马路，如前所述，将车把呈角度搁在北侧人行道上。此时，一名刺客跟随穿过马路，向死者补射了最后一枪。

检查人力车显示，一颗子弹穿透左侧并从坐垫穿出。

经查，该人力车牌号为工部局执照第8750号，系刘先送（Lieu Siam Sung）所有，58岁，籍贯广东（Kampo），住址为罗宾森路梅芳里125号。

警方前往该地址进行调查，人力车主表示，枪击发生后，住在同一地址的人力车夫回来向他说明了情况。他（人力车主）建议车夫立即向戈登路巡捕房报案。车夫答应照办并离开了住所。然而，此后便无人再见过他。人力车主无法提供其正式姓名，但称其绰号为惠小老汉（Wei Siam Loh Han），籍贯广东。目前正努力寻找此人。

Extensive enquiries were made amongst residents
in the vicinity, but all were reticent and it was with
difficulty that detectives succeeded in obtaining two
witnesses from whose statements the facts surrounding
the affairs were obtained. These persons are (1) Tsu
Kya Loh( 〔此处转录不清〕 ),age 40, Kompo, Cake shop assistant,
801 Markham Road, and (2) Ts Fung San( 〔此处转录不清〕 ),38,
Tungchow, Pork shop assistant, 795 Markham Road. The
first of these supplied most of the information upon
which the foregoing outline of the crime is based. The
information given by the 2nd named was not so extensive
but he was able to state that he saw two of the assassins
running East along Markham Road after the crime. Several
others who were in a position where they could not
fail to witness the crime were brought to the station,
where, despite intensive interrogation they maintained
that although they heard the shots they were not wit-
nesses to the crime. Enquiries in this direction are,
however, continuing.

The nearest Police to the scene were C.P.C.s
3552 and 3645 who were on patrol duty on the beat cover-
ing the scene of the crime. They, however, were on
Changping Road. a matter of 250 yards away when the
crime took place. The assassins therefore made good
their escape before the arrival of these officers.

警方在附近居民中进行了广泛调查，但所有人都保持沉默，侦探们费尽周折才找到两名证人，从其供词中获得了围绕此案的事实。这两人是：(1) Tsu Kya Loh（〔此处转录不清〕），40岁，籍贯广东（Kompo），蛋糕店店员，住址马克姆路801号；(2) Ts Fung San（〔此处转录不清〕），38岁，籍贯通州（Tungchow），肉铺店员，住址马克姆路795号。前者提供了大部分信息，前述犯罪概况即基于此。后者提供的信息较少，但他能陈述在案发后看到两名刺客沿马克姆路向东奔跑。另有几名处于必然目击犯罪位置的人被带到警署，尽管经过严厉审问，他们仍坚持声称虽然听到了枪声，但并未目击犯罪。然而，这方面的调查仍在继续。

距离现场最近的警员是华捕3552号和3645号，当时他们正在覆盖犯罪现场的巡逻段执行巡逻任务。然而，案发时他们位于昌平路（Changping Road），距离现场250码。因此，刺客在这些警员到达之前成功逃脱。

1.

Arrest of Chinese boy in possession of Anti-Japanese
pamphlets.

At 6.15p.m. 7/7/38 F.S. 236, Skibin brought to
the station a Chinese boy named Tong Vung Piau ( 董文彪 )
age 15, Ningpo, residing at 281, Zing Ying Lee, Hart Road,
for being in possession of anti-Japanese pamphlets.

Enquiries ascertained that a few minutes before
F.S. Skibin was walking past the Bubbling Well Cemetery
in plain clothes when he observed a number of pamphlets
on the road, he proceeded into the cemetery to the private
watchman's hut where he saw the above mentioned boy in
possession of a paper parcel which upon being opened was
found to contain a quantity of pamphlets.

The boy on being questioned stated he had gone for
a walk around the cemetery and had a few minutes before
found the parcel by the side of one of the graves, he pick-
ed same up and showed it to his father Toong Lien Sung
( 董連生 ) who has been a private watchman at B'Well
Cemetery for the past 30 years.

The boy stated that he had not had time to read
the characters on the pamphlets before F.S. Skibin had
found him in possession of same.

Supt. Crouch D.D.C. "B" who was also at B'Well
Station was informed of the facts of this case and later
communicated with D.C. (Crime) who stated that the boy
should be cautioned and released.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 707 / - 8 JULY 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

（批：S 1. / J.B.Q / 8/7 / C.J.G.S.L / E.S. / 88 1/1 / pm 97）

                        1938年7月7日.
1.

逮捕一名持有反日小册子的中国男孩。

1938年7月7日下午6时15分，西捕236号Skibin将一名名为董文彪（Tong Vung Piau）的中国男孩带至巡捕房，该男孩15岁，籍贯宁波，居住在哈同路（Hart Road）景英里281号，因其持有反日小册子。

调查查明，几分钟前，Skibin便衣路过静安寺公墓时，发现路上有一些小册子，他进入公墓来到私人看守棚屋，看见上述男孩持有一个纸包，打开后发现里面装有大量小册子。

经讯问，该男孩称他去公墓散步，几分钟前在一个坟墓旁发现了这个包裹，他将其捡起并展示给他的父亲董连生（Toong Lien Sung）看，其父在过去30年里一直担任静安寺公墓的私人看守。

该男孩称，在Skibin发现他持有小册子之前，他还没来得及阅读上面的文字。

当时也在静安寺路巡捕房的“B”分区副总监克劳奇（Crouch）警司获悉了本案事实，随后与刑事侦缉处长联系，后者表示应对该男孩予以警告后释放。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 707 / - 1938年7月8日 / 特别处）

Rough translation of attached pamphlets.

Dear Bretherns,
How do we commemorate the great and sacred July 7th.
anniversary? We believe that all the bretherns in the nation had
been deeply impressed with the Lukouchiao incident last year, when
the 1st. shot was fired at the cruel enemy - The Japanese
Imperialists and it was spread to a nationwide war of resistance.
During this war, it is not only to fight for the freedom and
Independence for our race of a population of 450,000,000, but also
to give a severe blow to the aggressor in order to protect the
justice and peace for the whole mankind in the world. Therefore
this sacred resistance is not only a programme of the Oriental East
war but also the beginning of a World war.
Dear Bretherns: today, although we are under the enemy's
horse-shoe, as in Shanghai, to commemorate the anniversary we have to
appeal to all those in the world who love justice and peace that we
now hold iron and blood to protect our nation, and fight with enemy
to obtain the independent living, and we do not care to continue the
bloodshed for a longer period. At the same time we have to appeal to
our bretherns that in order to fight for the victory of our struggle,
we have to strengthen the line of our whole race and fortification of
protracted resistance and concentrate ourselves under the leadership
of our only superior Generalissimo Chiang that we would never
negotiate nor influenced. Nevertheless, we would never scare of
any sacrifice, and we will follow up the blood path of our martyrs
to fight with our only enemy and a few traitors to reach our goal of
emancipation. Rush on to the extreme point of enemy's defeat, and
we commemorate the July 7th. with the following slogans:-
(1) Overthrow the Japanese Imperialism!
(2) " " " Militarists!
(3) All the bretherns get up and arm yourselves!
(4) The spirit of the martyrs during the resistance will never die.
(5) Long live the Emancipation of our China race.
(6) Long live the Generalissimo Chiang.

The Chinese Youth Iron and
Blood Anti-Japanese and
Traitors Eradication Party.

-------------------------

Translation of handbills

We want to fight with enemy to the end.
pages.zh:
所附小册子的粗略译文。

亲爱的同胞们：
我们如何纪念伟大而神圣的七月七日周年纪念日？我们相信，全国同胞都对去年的卢沟桥事变印象深刻，当时向残酷的敌人——日本帝国主义者打响了第一枪，并由此蔓延为全国的抗战。在这场战争中，不仅是为了争取我们四亿五千万种族的自由与独立，也是为了给侵略者以沉重打击，从而保护全世界人类的正义与和平。因此，这场神圣的抵抗不仅是东方战争的一部分，也是世界大战的开端。
亲爱的同胞们：今天，虽然我们在上海等地处于敌人的铁蹄之下，但为了纪念这一周年，我们必须呼吁世界上所有热爱正义与和平的人士，我们现在手持铁与血来保卫我们的国家，并与敌人战斗以获得独立的生存，我们不在乎流血持续更长的时间。同时，我们必须呼吁我们的同胞，为了争取斗争的胜利，我们必须加强全民族的阵线和持久抵抗的堡垒，并在我们唯一的最高领袖蒋介石委员长的领导下团结一致，绝不谈判，也不受任何影响。尽管如此，我们绝不畏惧任何牺牲，我们将追随烈士的血迹，与我们唯一的敌人和少数汉奸战斗，以达到我们解放的目标。冲向敌人失败的极点，我们以以下口号纪念七月七日：
(1) 打倒日本帝国主义！
(2) 打倒日本军国主义者！
(3) 全体同胞起来武装自己！
(4) 抗战中烈士的精神永垂不朽。
(5) 中华民族解放万岁。
(6) 蒋委员长万岁。

中国青年铁血抗日锄奸党。

---

传单译文

我们要与敌人战斗到底。

REPORT
Louza Station 897
Date July 8th. 1938.

Subject State of District 7 7-38.

Made by D.I. Bennett Forwarded by ____________________

Sir,

During the 7-7-38, no untoward incidents occurred in
Louza District with the exception of the distributions of Anti-
Japanese pamphlets.

Pamphlets were found to have been scattered on the
roadway on several occasions.

(1) At about 6.10. a.m. 7-7-38, Mr. Fairburn, (A.C. Police)
effected the arrest of four male Chinese who were riding
in a tramcar on Nanking Road near Yu Y Ching Road, they
being suspected of having thrown a number of pamphlets
from this tramcar.

D.S. Henchman, Special Branch attended, insufficient
evidence to definitely ascertain they were responsible
for the distribution of these pamphlets, they were
released after enquiries.

(2) At 11.20. a.m. 7-7-38, pamphlets found at Hankow and
Yunnan Roads Corner, probably thrown from Yangtse Hotel,
detective enquiries however failing to ascertain who was
responsible.

(3) At about the same time, similar pamphlets found at
Foochow and Yu Y Ching Roads Corner.

(4) At 2. p.m. 7-7-38, pamphlets found on the roadway at
Foochow and Chekiang Roads Corner.

(5) At 5.30.p.m. 7-7-38, pamphlets found on roadway at
Nanking and Yu Y Ching Roads Corner.

(6) At 6.25.p.m. 7-7-38, pamphlets found on the roadway at
Nanking and Kweichow Roads Corner.

(7) At 8.p.m. 7-7-38, pamphlets found on the roadway at
Nanking and Chihli Roads Corner.

During the 7-7-38, hourly tours of the District were
made by a foreign detective accompanied by Chinese detectives,
hotels, lodging houses and teashops being visited, whilst
during the progress of these tours 103 male Chinese who were
of the loafer type and others who were observed to be loitering
were brought to the Station for enquiries.

A large number of these were finger printed, four found
to have previous records, these men with the exception of the

主题 1938年7月7日第七区治安状况。

由 警督 Bennett 制作 转呈 ___

先生，

在1938年7月7日当天，除分发抗日小册子外，老闸区未发生其他不良事件。

多次发现小册子被散落在路面上。

(1) 1938年7月7日上午6时10分左右，费尔伯恩先生（代理巡官，警务处）在南京路近虞洽卿路的一辆电车上逮捕了四名中国男子，怀疑他们从该电车上抛撒了大量小册子。

政治部侦探长 Henchman 到场，因证据不足无法确证他们负责分发这些小册子，经讯问后予以释放。

(2) 1938年7月7日上午11时20分，在汉口路与云南路转角处发现小册子，可能是从扬子饭店抛出的，但经侦探调查未能查明责任人。

(3) 大约同一时间，在福州路与虞洽卿路转角处发现类似小册子。

(4) 1938年7月7日下午2时，在福州路与浙江路转角处的路面上发现小册子。

(5) 1938年7月7日下午5时30分，在南京路与虞洽卿路转角处的路面上发现小册子。

(6) 1938年7月7日下午6时25分，在南京路与贵州路转角处的路面上发现小册子。

(7) 1938年7月7日晚上8时，在南京路与直隶路转角处的路面上发现小册子。

1938年7月7日当天，由一名外籍侦探陪同华籍侦探对该区进行每小时一次的巡逻，走访了旅馆、客栈和茶馆，在这些巡逻过程中，将103名具有游民特征的中国男子及其他被观察到徘徊不前的人带至捕房进行讯问。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Pamphlets found on the Nanking Road.

Sir,
At 5.30p.m. on July 7th, S.I. Wilcox brought to the station several pamphlets containing the words "Long Live Chang Kai-Shek" and one of Anti Japanese nature, advocating the continuation of resistance to Japan.
It appears that the said pamphlets had been collected by C.P.C.s 301 and 831 on the south side of Nanking Road east of Shanse Road. C.P.C.s found the pamphlets lying on the road near the footpath. 5 copies of the pamphlets forwarded to the Special Branch, S.M.P.

Misc. No. 677/38.    Central
                      July 7th,       38.

1.

Anti-Japanese pamphlets found at the corner
of Nanking and Honan Roads.

At 5.30a.m. 7/7/38 Mr. Y.H. Short of the River
Police brought to the station 14 Anti-Japanese pamph-
lets which, he found, discarded on the street at the
corner of Nanking and Honan Roads at 5.20a.m. even date.

The pamphlets were found to be of Anti-Japanese
in nature to the effect that Chinese people should
continue their efforts to resist the invasion of the
Japanese militarists for the commemoration of the
July 7th Anniversary.

（批：Special Branch copy）
Enquiries were made by C.I.D. S3 at the scene and
its vicinity, but failed to locate an eye-witness who
might reveal the identity of the distributors of these
pamphlets.

The pamphlets have been forwarded to Special
Branch.

1.

在南京路与河南路转角处发现反日传单。

1938年7月7日上午5时30分，水上警察局 Y.H. Short 先生将14份反日传单带至巡捕房，称其于当日凌晨5时20分在南京路与河南路转角处的街道上发现并被丢弃的这些传单。

经查，这些传单属反日性质，内容为呼吁中国民众为纪念七七事变周年，继续努力抵抗日本军国主义的侵略。

（批注：政治部副本）
刑事侦查处 S3 组在现场及其周边进行了查询，但未能找到可能揭露这些传单分发者身份的目击证人。

传单已送交政治部。

Handbills thrown from the roof of the
Emporium Building.

Sir,
At 7.50p.m. on July 7th C.P.C. 3047 telephoned
to the station stating that several handbills had been
thrown from the roof of the Continental Emporium Bldg.,
377 Nanking Rd. S.I. Wilcox and C.D.C. 194 visited the
place in question and C.P.C.s 3089,3132 handed over to
C.D.C. 194 three anti-government handbills. C.D.C.194
visited the roof of the building with intent to find
the person or persons who threw the said handbills to
the ground but without any result. The copies of
handbills forwarded to the Special Branch S.M.P.

Misc. 288/38.
Memo. July 6th., 38.

1.

Pamphlets found on B'Well Road.

At 9-30pm. on 6/7/38 C.P.C. 2057, when patrolling
B'Well Road near Yu Yah Ching Road, observed several
pamphlets on the pavement and roadway. On examining
one of these he found that it had bearing on July 7th.,
the anniversary of the commencement of hostilities.
He brought same to this station, and the actual
translation is:"Remember July the 7th."
The pamphlets had apparently been thrown from
the roof of the New World Amusement Resort, and
detectives immediately made enquiries there, but were
unable to secure any useful information.
Circulated.
Copy with pamphlet to D.C. (Special Branch).

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 7 JULY 1938）

备忘录。1938年7月6日。

1.

在贝勒路发现传单。

1938年7月6日晚上9时30分，华捕2057号在贝勒路近虞洽卿路巡逻时，观察到人行道和马路上有数份传单。经检查其中一份，发现其与7月7日战事爆发周年纪念日有关。
他将传单带至本巡捕房，实际译文为：“记住七月七日。”
这些传单显然是从新世界游乐场屋顶抛下的，侦探立即前往该处查询，但未能获得任何有用信息。
传阅。

Subject Unauthorised Searching by Members of the Japanese Gendarmerie.

Made by E.A. Bennett Forwarded by

Sir,
At 10.55.p.m. 7-7-38, a telephone message was received from
S.I. Barry (Central) that members of the Japanese Gendarmerie
were conducting a search of motor cars and pedestrians on
Yu Ching Road near Avenue Edward VII.

Inspector Chamberlain immediately attended and found that two motor trucks, licence
plates Nos. 2111 and 2112, belonging to the
Japanese Forces together with 24 members of the Japanese
Gendarmerie (armed) were in this area on Yu Ching Road and
Avenue Edward VII Corner, and that members of the Armoured Car
Section, S.V.C. under Major Loch had taken charge of this
stretch of roadway, thereby preventing members of the Gendarmerie
from continuing the search of cars and pedestrians, this having
been done by diverting the flow of traffic from Yu Ya Ching
Road between Canton Road and Ave. Ed. VII.

J.D.S. Kobayashi (Plain clothes) a Japanese sergeant and
two Japanese constables (Uniform) were with this party of
Japanese Gendarmerie, J.D.S. Kobayashi stating that the search
was being done with the full knowledge and permission of the
Commissioner of Police and Mr. Agnil (Special Deputy Commissioner
of Japanese) and that Central, Louza, and Chengtu Road Stations
had been informed.

No such instructions had been received by Inspector
Chamberlain, officer i/c of Louza, whilst Mr. Robertson, D.C.
who attended escorted the Japanese members of S.M.Police to
Central Station. (Partly in El-S 7-2 sector)

This searching by the Japanese Gendarmerie was carried
out by the instructions of Major Hayashi, in charge of the
Gendarmerie, which had commenced at about 8.30.p.m. in Central

主题 日本宪兵队员的非法搜查行为。

制作人 E.A. Bennett 转呈人

先生，
1938年7月7日晚上10点55分，接到中央捕房巴里 (Barry) 巡官的电话留言，称日本宪兵队员正在爱多亚路 (Avenue Edward VII) 附近的虞洽卿路上对机动车和行人进行搜查。

张伯伦 (Chamberlain) 巡长立即赶赴现场，发现两辆属于日军的卡车（车牌号分别为2111和2112）以及24名武装日本宪兵队员位于虞洽卿路与爱多亚路拐角处的这一区域，且由洛克 (Loch) 少校指挥的上海义勇军 (S.V.C.) 装甲车分队已接管了这段道路，从而阻止了宪兵队员继续搜查车辆和行人，这是通过将广东路与爱多亚路之间虞洽卿路上的车流改道来实现的。

便衣日本军曹小林 (J.D.S. Kobayashi) 和两名制服日本警员与这群日本宪兵在一起，小林声称此次搜查是在警务处处长和日本特别副 commissioner 阿尼尔 (Agnil) 先生完全知情并许可的情况下进行的，且已通知中央捕房、老闸捕房和成都路捕房。

负责老闸捕房的张伯伦巡长未收到此类指令，而到场的 Robertson 副 commissioner 则护送上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本籍成员前往中央捕房。（部分位于 El-S 7-2 防区）

日本宪兵的这次搜查是根据宪兵队负责人林 (Hayashi) 少校的指令进行的，该行动于晚上8点30分左右在中央捕房辖区开始

Subject   N. J. K. No. 9 Mill -- Precautions for Anniversary of the
          Lukouchiao Incident.

Made by   D. S. I. Cunning,    &    Forwarded by    Inspector i/c.

Sir,

      Mr. Kobayashi, Manager of the N. J. K. Mills, came to
Gordon Road Station at 10 a.m. 6/7/38, and stated that he
desired police co-operation against possible attempts at
sabotage inside the N. J. K. No. 9 Mill, Markham Road. He had
no definite information that such acts would be attempted,
but was desirous of taking precautionary measures for the
three days covering the anniversary of the Lukouchiao outbreak
which falls due on 7/7/38.

      The Officer i/c Gordon Road has made the necessary
arrangements for uniform police protection, whilst two
Chinese detectives will be detailed for duty inside the
mill continuously for the next three days.

                                          D. S. I.

D. D. O. "B" Division.

S.M.P., F.M.P. SEEN AT
LOGGERHEADS OVER TERROR ISSUE

TOKYO, JULY 10--(DOMEI)-- ATTEMPTS OF THE BRITISH-
DOMINATED SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE TO FORCE THE FRENCH
MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES TO EXTEND CLOSER AND MORE EFFECTIVE
CO-OPERATION IN CURBING TERRORIST OUTRAGES IN THE INTER-
NATIONAL SETTLEMENT BY CHINESE OPERATIVES ALLEGEDLY BASED
IN THE CONCESSION WERE REFLECTED YESTERDAY IN AN
EDITORIAL OF THE BRITISH-OWNED AND OPERATED NORTH CHINA
DAILY NEWS, DISPATCHES FROM SHANGHAI SAID TODAY. THE
JOURNAL WAS DESCRIBED IN THE REPORTS AS THE "OFFICIAL
MOUTHPIECE" OF THE SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL.

SAID THE EDITORIAL, IN PART,: " BREACHES OF THE
PEACE BY MEN ARMED WITH MILITARY WEAPONS, WHETHER THEY
BOMBS, GRENADES OR PISTOLS SHOULD ENTAIL HANDING THE
CULPRITS OVER TO THE JAPANESE AUTHORITIES. EVEN MERE
POSSESSION OF SUCH WEAPONS SHOULD LEAD TO THE SAME ACTION."

THE POLICE AUTHORITIES OF THE INTER-
NATIONAL SETTLEMENT, THE REPORTS STATED, ARE "EMBARASSED"
BECAUSE THE TERRITORIAL PROPINQUITY OF THE TWO FOREIGN-
CONTROLLED AREAS FACILITATES TERRORISTS TO FLEE INTO
FRENCH-CONTROLLED TERRITORY . (MORE)

第1号。
上海公共租界工部局警务处、法公董局警务处
在恐怖主义问题上陷入僵局

东京，7月10日--(同盟通讯社)-- 据今日来自上海的报道，由英国人主导的上海公共租界工部局警务处试图迫使法国市政当局在遏制由中国特工实施的恐怖暴行方面提供更紧密、更有效的合作，这些特工据称以法租界为基地，这一情况反映在英国拥有并经营的《字林西报》昨日的一篇社论中。据报道，该报被称为上海工部局的“官方喉舌”。

该社论部分指出：“持军用武器（无论是炸弹、手榴弹还是手枪）的人破坏和平，应将罪犯移交给日本当局。甚至仅仅持有此类武器也应导致同样的行动。”

报道指出，国际租界的警察当局感到“尴尬”，因为两个外国控制区域在地理上的邻近便利了恐怖分子逃入法国控制的领土。（续）

Suspect Admits Tossing A
Bomb At City Ferry

Was One Of Terrorists Active On Morning Of
July 7; Other Men Admit Tossing Bombs
On Jinkee Road, Other Locations

Continuing their interrogation of the suspects in custody in connection with the various recent assassinations and bombing outrages, the Homicide Squad of the S.M.P., it is understood, obtained an admission from one of the men that he was the man who tossed a hand grenade at the former City Government Ferry, on the Bund off Peking Road, on the morning of July 7.

It will be recalled that one Japanese member of the Military Water Police, who have their headquarters in the former Floating Restaurant, and three Chinese were injured by this grenade. A Chinese truck driver was arrested near the scene by a Japanese gendarme but released the next day. Another suspect was arrested by the Japanese in Pootung, and was alleged by the military to have admitted knowledge of the crime. He was taken to Hongkew and his fate is not known.

The man in custody of the Homicide Squad, who has confessed to the bombing outrage, is likely to be the second Chinese to be handed over to the Japanese authorities, after a prima facie case against him is established. The first terrorist was handed over to the Japanese authorities on Monday.

Other members of the same terrorist gang rounded-up during the past week have admitted participating in the bombing outrages on the morning of July 7, the anniversary of the outbreak of hostilities in the north. One of the men admitted tossing a bomb at the Japanese sentries at Alabaster Road, near Thibet Road, on the same morning. One terrorist was shot at the time and another wounded. Another man admitted tossing a bomb at 120 Jinkee Road.

The Homicide Squad continued working at full blast for the past few days, following up clues and watching various addresses, but no further arrests have been made.

Pootung Guerrillas

It was revealed yesterday that Li Kwong-zung, 36-year-old terrorist, who had attempted to assassinate Mr. Yih Kyi-vung, Chief of the Pootung Salt Gabelle on Avenue Road on Monday morning, was a Pootung guerrilla. Prior to succumbing to his wounds, inflicted upon him by Detective Sergeant J. Y. Hillhouse, Li, it is understood, admitted that he was attached to a guerrilla unit operating in Pootung and that he was chosen to do away with Mr. Yih.

嫌犯承认向市轮渡投掷炸弹

系7月7日上午活跃的恐怖分子之一；其他人承认在静安寺路及其他地点投掷炸弹

据悉，上海公共租界工部局警务处凶杀组继续审讯近期多起暗杀和爆炸暴行案件的在押嫌疑人，其中一人承认，他就是7月7日上午在外滩北京路口原市政府轮渡码头投掷手榴弹的人。

回想起来，当时有一枚手榴弹炸伤了总部设在原水上餐厅的日本海军水警的一名日籍成员以及三名中国人。一名中国卡车司机在现场附近被日本宪兵逮捕，但次日获释。另一名嫌疑人在浦东被日本人逮捕，军方称其已承认知晓该罪行。他被带往虹口，其下落不明。

这名由凶杀组羁押并已供认参与爆炸暴行的男子，很可能成为继第一名恐怖分子于周一被移交给日本当局后，第二名在初步证据确凿后被移交给日本当局的中国人。

上周被捕的同伙中的其他成员也承认参与了7月7日（华北战事爆发周年纪念日）上午的爆炸暴行。其中一人承认，当天上午在靠近西藏路的阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road，今石门一路）向日本哨兵投掷了一枚炸弹。当时一名恐怖分子被击毙，另一人受伤。还有一人承认在静安寺路120号投掷了一枚炸弹。

过去几天，凶杀组全力工作，追踪线索并监视多处地址，但未再进行逮捕。

浦东游击队

昨日披露，36岁的恐怖分子李光宗（Li Kwong-zung，音译）曾于周一上午在大西路企图刺杀浦东盐务稽核分所主任叶季壮（Yih Kyi-vung，音译），他是一名浦东游击队员。据悉，李光宗在被警佐 J. Y. Hillhouse 击伤致死前，承认自己隶属于一支在浦东活动的游击队，并且是被选中去刺杀叶先生的人。

《上海晚邮报与水星报》. 1938年7月19日

在沪日本人寻求
工部局警务处采取“更好”的行动

随着8月13日的临近——即上海地区中日敌对行动爆发一周年纪念日，据今日当地日文报道称，在沪日本人急于防止重演7月7日夺去其同胞生命的恐怖统治。

日本居留民团对外关系委员会昨日发表声明，严厉抨击上海公共租界工部局警务处未能抓获7月7日暴行的“哪怕一名罪犯”。

报道补充称，居留民团总裁天野真三郎（Masusaburo Amano，音译）将向日高信六郎（Shinrokuro Hidaka）总领事转达一项要求，即工部局警务处应对恐怖分子采取更严厉的措施，并由总领事转呈工部局董事会。

该声明将工部局警务处所谓的效率低下归咎于负责警务官员的“缺乏训练”和“疏忽”。

pages.en:
Sheer Nonsense
Japanese correspondents in Shanghai have been running amok over the leading article which appeared in these columns on Saturday entitled "Thursday's Good Work." Commencing with the wholly unwarrantable and incorrect assumption that this organ is the official mouth-piece of the Shanghai Municipal Council, the Japanese correspondents appear to find in that article proof of attempts by the "British-dominated Shanghai Municipal Police to force the French Municipal Authorities to extend closer and more effective co-operation in curbing terrorist outrages in the International Settlement by Chinese operatives allegedly based in the Concession...." The foregoing and the rest of the report is full of inaccuracies. The "North-China Daily News" is British owned and an entirely "independent" newspaper. It is most certainly not the mouth-piece of the Shanghai Municipal Council nor of any other authority save in so far as certain official announcements appearing in its advertising columns are concerned. There is not, so far as this journal has any knowledge, any attempt on the part of the Shanghai Municipal Police to force the French Municipal Police to take any particular line of action, and in its comment on Saturday this journal extended its compliments alike to both forces on the way in which a day of potential trouble was handled with the greatest efficiency. The statement that the terrorists operate from bases in the French Concession has not been made by this journal. It is a Japanese allegation probably with as much foundation in fact as some of the other hectic stories published by the Japanese press, notably the tale of the two beautiful French women, operating a beauty parlour, which was a meeting place of Chinese spies. That the Japanese Press itself subsequently admitted to be wrong. It is true that this newspaper suggested that Chinese found in unlawful possession of arms should be handed over to the Japanese authorities. That was not inspired by the Shanghai Municipal Council, nor was there, as the Japanese reports suggest, any reference to the Chinese law courts. Domei was perfectly correct in bringing these reports back to Shanghai, though perhaps it has done the Japanese journalists responsible for this farrago of nonsense an ill turn. It is suggested that they should be recalled and others less prone to "language difficulties" should be sent out to take their place, or perhaps those better able to suppress fantasy in favour of fact.

Tokyo's Reaction
To July 7
Attempts of S.M.C. Seen to Get French Assistance;
"N.C.D.N." Quoted

Tokyo, July 10.
Attempts of the British-dominated Shanghai Municipal Police to force the French Municipal authorities to extend closer and more effective co-operation in curbing terrorist outrages in the International Settlement by Chinese allegedly based in the Concession were reflected yesterday in an editorial of the British-owned and operated "North-China Daily News," dispatches from Shanghai said today. The journal was described in the reports as the "official mouth-piece" of the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Said the editorial, in part,: "Breaches of the peace by men armed with military weapons, whether they be bombs, grenades or pistols should entail handing the culprits over to the Japanese authorities. Even mere possession of such weapons should lead to the same action."
The police authorities of the International Settlement, the reports stated, are "embarrassed" because the territorial propinquity of the two foreign-controlled areas facilitates terrorists to flee into French-controlled territory.
The French police, while anxious to curb terrorism, find their hands tied by the alleged dilatory tactics employed by the judges of the Chinese Branch Second Special District Court and the Third Branch High Court of Kiangsu located in the Concession.
These judges are Hankow appointees and are further accused of treating anti-Japanese terrorist suspects with leniency and of frequently interfering with the work of the French police.
The suggestion of the "North-China Daily News," which the press reports say was "inspired" by the S.M.C., would enable the police in both foreign-controlled areas to strike with vigour against terrorists since the authorities would not have to cope with the Chinese law courts.—Domei.
***For editorial comment see Page 4.

纯属胡扯

驻上海的日本记者对周六刊登在本栏题为《周四的良好表现》的社论大肆攻击。日本记者从一开始就基于完全毫无根据且错误的假设，即本报是上海公共租界工部局的官方喉舌，他们似乎在那篇社论中找到了“由英国人主导的上海公共租界工部局警务处试图迫使法公董局当局在遏制由中国特工实施的恐怖暴行方面提供更紧密、更有效的合作”的证据，据称这些特工以法租界为基地____”。上述内容及报告的其余部分充满了不实之处。《字林西报》由英国人拥有，是一份完全“独立”的报纸。它绝非上海公共租界工部局或任何其他当局的喉舌，除非涉及刊登在其广告栏中的某些官方公告。据本刊所知，上海公共租界工部局警务处并未试图强迫法公董局警务处采取任何特定的行动路线，而且本刊在周六的评论中，对两支警力以最高效率处理潜在动荡的一天给予了同样的赞誉。本刊从未发表过恐怖分子以法租界为基地的说法。这是日本方面的指控，其事实依据可能与其他由日本媒体发布的狂热故事一样少，特别是关于两名经营美容院的美丽法国女性的故事，该美容院被指为中国间谍的聚会场所。后来日本媒体自己也承认这是错误的。诚然，本报曾建议应将非法持有武器的中国人移交给日本当局。但这并非受上海公共租界工部局指使，也没有像日本报道所暗示的那样提及中国法院。同盟社将这些报道传回上海是完全正确的，尽管这可能给制造这堆 nonsense（胡言乱语）的日本记者帮了倒忙。建议将他们召回，派遣其他不太容易出现“语言困难”的人接替，或者派遣那些更能抑制幻想、尊重事实的人。

东京对7月7日事件的反应
视工部局试图获取法国援助；引用《字林西报》

东京，7月10日。
据今日来自上海的电讯称，由英国人主导的上海公共租界工部局警务处试图迫使法公董局当局在遏制 allegedly（据称）以法租界为基地的中国人在国际租界实施的恐怖暴行方面提供更紧密、更有效的合作，这一企图反映在英国拥有和经营的《字林西报》昨日的社论中。报道将该报描述为上海公共租界工部局的“官方喉舌”。

该社论部分称：“持军用武器（无论是炸弹、手榴弹还是手枪）的人破坏和平，应将罪犯移交给日本当局。甚至仅仅持有此类武器也应导致同样的行动。”

报道指出，国际租界的警察当局感到“尴尬”，因为两个外国控制区域在地理上的邻近便利了恐怖分子逃入法国控制的领土。

法国警方虽然渴望遏制恐怖主义，但据称其手脚被位于法租界内的江苏高等法院第三分院和中国特区第二地方法院的法官所使用的拖延战术所束缚。

这些法官是汉口方面任命的，并被进一步指责对反日恐怖嫌疑人宽大处理，并经常干涉法国警方的工作。

据报道，《字林西报》的建议是受工部局“指使”的，这将使两个外国控制区域的警方能够有力地打击恐怖分子，因为当局无需再应付中国法院。——同盟社。
***社论评论见第4版。

档案

A Friday Search:
Complaint from Chinese

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—Please allow me a small
space in your valuable paper.
In todays' issue, you published that

the S.M.C. authorities accompany
plain cloth Japanese searchers in
their work throughout the day
(Thursday). Yesterday at late noon I
was stopped and searched by two
plain cloth Japanese at Foochow
Road near the Bund, they even
looked into the contents of my pocket
book.

Apparently satisfied, they nodded
their thanks? and I was allowed to
go on. Now coming from the opposite
direction was a Chinese carrying a
parcel accompanied by a Foreigner.
The Japanese searchers stopped the
pair, and took away the parcel and
commenced to tear away the wrap-
ping to examine the contents, not
being satisfied with the Chinese ex-
planation, they took him by the arm
and requested that he accompany
them. The Foreigner explained but
they completely ignored him.
The Japanese holding the parcel
made a hostile move towards his
back pocket, but the Foreigner had
a large pistol in his hands pointing
at them, something they said about
being police and returned the parcel
to the Chinese, they then turned
away.

In a hurry to avoid the chance of
a stray bullet, I stumbled, fell, broke
my eye glasses and sprained my hand,
the foreigner pointed his pistol at
me, then helped me up.

Now if Guards were compelled by
the S.M.C. to wear uniform, and
plain cloth Japanese police carried
cards or badges; this would not have
occurred. I should not need to spend
the cost of a new pair of eye glasses,
suffer an injury to my hands and
get a bad fright.

C. S. L.
Shanghai, July 9.
