周五的搜查：
来自中国人的投诉

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——请允许我在贵报宝贵的版面上占用一点空间。
在今日的刊物中，你们刊登了工部局当局全天（周四）陪同便衣日本搜查人员执行工作的消息。昨天下午晚些时候，我在靠近外滩的福州路被两名便衣日本人拦下并搜查，他们甚至查看了我钱包里的内容。

他们显然满意了，点头致谢？然后我被允许离开。这时，对面走来一个带着包裹的中国人，旁边伴有一名外国人。日本搜查人员拦住了这两人，拿走了包裹并开始撕开包装检查内容，因对那名中国人的解释不满意，他们抓住他的手臂，要求他随他们走。那名外国人进行解释，但他们完全无视了他。

拿着包裹的日本人对他后口袋做出了敌对举动，但那名外国人手中握着一把大号手枪指着他们，他们说了些关于自己是警察的话，然后将包裹还给了那个中国人，随后转身离开。

为了避开流弹的风险，我匆忙中绊倒，摔碎了眼镜，扭伤了手，那名外国人用枪指着我，然后把我扶了起来。

现在，如果警卫被工部局强制穿着制服，并且便衣日本警察携带证件或徽章；这就不会发生了。我就不需要花费配一副新眼镜的钱，手部受伤，还受到极大的惊吓。

C. S. L.
上海，7月9日。

pages.en:
THURSDAY'S GOOD WORK

This journal has already commented on the futility of the acts of terrorism perpetrated in the International Settlement on the occasion of the first anniversary of the commencement of Sino-Japanese hostilities on Thursday, and there is very little that can be added, save again to emphasize the stupidity of the whole proceedings, and to point out that those responsible for it are not animated by high ideals but by a completely mistaken view of their duty towards their own countrymen. The sum total of what happened appears to be that some eighteen bombs were thrown, three Chinese killed, a number injured, and two Japanese slain. As a contribution toward the establishment of China's military fortunes the whole business was beneath contempt. There is a certain amount of evidence to show that the terrorists who are said to have percolated into Shanghai, generally passing through what should be Japanese controlled territory to do so, acted in concert, and that behind the outburst of early yesterday morning there was at least a plan, if not a directing mind. If not, why were all the bombs thrown around the hours five to six a.m.? It is clear that those responsible for planning the demonstration expected that later in the day the authorities would clamp down such strict control that the only chance to get anything done was to start before the various precautionary measures would be in full working order. It was the only time when the bomb-throwers could hope to do their dastardly work and escape afterwards, and the throwing of missiles practically simultaneously in districts so far apart is convincing proof of the existence of some sort of widespread organization, rather different from the scheme, which, it was originally alleged, consisted of small bands operating in the foreign areas completely unknown to each other. The terrorists having shot their bolt early in the day, the work of the authorities was rendered comparatively simple, though their activities were praiseworthy and strenuous and indicated a complete realization of the situation, and full ability to handle any emergency which arose. It is possible that out of the large number of arrests which were made on Thursday there may be found prisoners who may lead back to those at the head of this movement, and if this proves to be the case much future anxiety will be avoided.

Nothing but the highest praise can be spoken of the arrangements which the various authorities responsible for the maintenance of order in the French Concession and the International Settlement, civil as well as military. It would be invidious to endeavour to allot credit amongst them for one of the most remarkable pieces of efficient work which has been demonstrated for a long while, and to all those, from the men who patiently plodded the streets all day ready for any emergency which might arise, to those higher officials, responsible for the general arrangements, the highest credit is due for the excellent manner in which they carried out their work. It is a striking answer to the charges made by the Japanese authorities some months ago that the administrations of the French Concession and the International Settlement were incapable of maintaining order within their boundaries. The efficiency of the arrangements was testified to by a Japanese military spokesman yesterday morning, according to Domel, when he expressed "appreciation of the most effective policing of the Settlement south of the Creek on Thursday." Questioned whether he meant that the Japanese authorities were satisfied with the policing taken after the two-hour reign of terror early on Thursday the spokesman replied "No, we mean the entire day, July 7, 1938. From 12 midnight to midnight." A generous and highly deserved tribute to the very efficient work done. The mobility of the numerous patrols, and the close liaison maintained between them all is responsible for the manner in which possible further outbreaks during the day were kept down, and it is extremely doubtful, whether, had there been further incidents, the perpetrators would have escaped. That they appear to have recognized, and, if this is indeed the case, it accounts for the cessation of activities immediately after the first outbreak. Fully organized efficiency had made the game too dangerous, and that in itself is sufficient proof of the quality of the men who made arrangements which had such telling effect. That view is emphasized by what happened with regard to the Louza district. Earlier in the day, when it was apparent that the terrorists had for the time being been discouraged, it was expected that as evening fell, Louza, which has been for years the magnet attracting disorderly elements, would be the focus for further activities on the part of the terrorists. This journal learns that special concentrations were made to deal with that area in the case of trouble, and the fact nothing of the kind occurred, is again the best testimony to the adequacy of the arrangements made.

The Municipal Council has already made its attitude plain regard to activities directed against the Japanese forces in Shanghai, committed within its jurisdiction. Persons caught responsible for such acts may be handed over to be dealt with by the Japanese naval or military authorities. It would seem that the scope of that proclamation might with advantage be considerably widened. With the constant talk of continuing guerilla warfare against the Japanese even within the neutral borders of the International Settlement, it is clear that the neutrality, upon which depends the safety not only of the foreigners resident within its borders, but of the hundreds of thousands of Chinese in excess of the normal population, needs to be protected to the utmost. Breaches of the peace by men armed with military weapons, whether they be bombs, grenades, or pistols should entail handing the culprits over to the Japanese authorities. Even mere possession of such weapons should lead to the same action. Quite possibly men so armed, and merely bent upon a little mild armed robbery would fall into the net. Whatever may be their intentions in retaining such weapons against the law of the International Settlement, it is clear that it is no part of the duty of the authorities to endeavour to discover what the possessors may have had in their minds when they procured them. The fact is that such things may be used for the infringement of the neutrality of the Settlement, and if its authorities were to make it plain that such people would have to be handed over, the effect might prove a striking one. The armed robber per se might then completely disappear, leaving the terrorist in splendid isolation; when the fullest application of the doctrine suggested would have the completest results. It is undoubtedly a point worth consideration. The municipal authorities should seek every means to strengthen their own hands, for they have done so splendidly that every possible recognition and assistance should be given them. pages.zh:
周四的良好成效

本报此前已就周四在中日敌对行动爆发一周年之际于公共租界内实施的恐怖主义行为之徒劳无益作了评论，对此几乎无需赘言，唯有再次强调整个事件的愚蠢，并指出那些责任人并非受崇高理想驱动，而是出于对其对本国同胞责任的完全错误认知。事件的全部情况似乎是：共投掷了约十八枚炸弹，三名中国人死亡，多人受伤，两名日本人身亡。作为对中国军事运势的贡献，整件事简直不值一提。有一定证据表明，据称渗透进上海的恐怖分子（通常穿越本应由日本控制的领土进入）是协同行动的，且在昨天清晨的爆发背后，至少有一个计划，即便没有统一的指挥头脑。否则，为何所有炸弹都集中在凌晨五点至六点之间投掷？显然，策划此次示威活动的责任人预计，当天晚些时候当局将实施严厉管控，因此唯一的机会是在各种预防措施全面生效之前动手。这是投弹者希望完成其卑鄙行径并随后逃脱的唯一时机，而在相距甚远的地区几乎同时投掷爆炸物，有力地证明了存在某种广泛的组织，这与最初声称的由互不相识的小团伙在外国区域各自为战的方案大相径庭。由于恐怖分子在清晨便已耗尽手段，当局的工作变得相对简单，尽管他们的行动值得称赞且紧张忙碌，显示出对局势的充分认识以及处理任何突发状况的充分能力。周四进行了大量逮捕，从中可能会找到能追溯至该运动头目的囚犯，如果情况属实，将避免未来的许多忧虑。

对于负责维持法租界和公共租界秩序的各当局（包括文职和军方），其安排只能给予最高赞誉。试图在这一长期以来展示出的最高效工作之一中分配功劳是有失公允的，从整天耐心巡视街道、随时准备应对任何突发事件的普通人员，到负责总体安排的高级官员，所有人都因其出色的工作表现而应获得最高荣誉。这是对几个月前日本当局指责法租界和公共租界行政当局无力在其辖区内维持秩序的有力回击。据多梅尔（Domel）报道，一位日本军方发言人昨天上午证实了这些安排的有效性，他表示“赞赏周四苏州河以南租界极其有效的警务工作”。当被问及这是否意味着日本当局对周四清晨两小时恐怖统治之后采取的警务措施感到满意时，该发言人回答说：“不，我们指的是整整一天，即1938年7月7日。从午夜十二点到次日午夜。”这是对非常高效工作的慷慨且当之无愧的赞扬。众多巡逻队的高机动性以及他们之间保持的紧密联络，使得白天可能发生的进一步骚乱得以平息，而且极难想象，如果发生更多事件，肇事者能够逃脱。他们似乎已经认识到了这一点，如果确实如此，这就解释了为何在第一次爆发后活动立即停止。高度组织的效率使得这种游戏过于危险，这本身就足以证明制定这些产生显著效果之安排的人员素质。关于老闸区（Louza district）发生的情况进一步强调了这一观点。当天早些时候，当明显看出恐怖分子暂时受挫时，人们预计随着夜幕降临，多年来一直吸引不法分子的磁石——老闸区，将成为恐怖分子进一步活动的焦点。本报获悉，针对该地区可能出现的麻烦已做了特别兵力集结，而事实上并未发生此类事件，这再次最好地证明了所做准备措施的充分性。

工部局已明确表明其态度，针对在其管辖范围内发生的针对驻沪日军的行动。抓获的相关责任人可移交给日本海军或军事当局处理。看来，该公告的范围不妨大大拓宽。鉴于不断有关于甚至在公共租界这一中立边界内继续对日进行游击战的言论，显然，不仅关系到居住在其境内的外国人安全，也关系到超出正常人口数量的数十万中国人安全的这种中立地位，需要得到最大程度的保护。凡持军用武器（无论是炸弹、手榴弹还是手枪）破坏和平者，均应将罪犯移交给日本当局。甚至仅仅持有此类武器也应导致同样的处理。完全有可能，一些仅企图进行轻微武装抢劫的持械者也会落入法网。无论他们违反公共租界法律保留这些武器的意图如何，显然，当局并无责任去探究持有者在获取这些武器时的心理动机。事实是，这些物品可能被用于侵犯租界的中立地位，如果当局明确表示此类人员将被移交，其效果可能会非常显著。武装抢劫犯本身可能会完全消失，使恐怖分子陷入彻底的孤立；届时，充分应用上述原则将取得最圆满的结果。这无疑是一个值得考虑的要点。市政当局应寻求一切手段以加强自身力量，因为他们做得如此出色，理应获得一切可能的认可与协助。其中之一是采取一切可能的措施以**〔此处转录不清〕**

pages.en:
Cheap Assassination
Some other name than "terrorism" will have
to be found for the puerile display of violence
which was used yesterday by Chinese bad char-
acters to mark the end of the first year of
hostilities. At the time of writing it was stated
that no fewer than eighteen hand grenades had
been thrown in the International Settlement and
Chapel causing a few deaths and doing slight
damage, while one or two Japanese, apparent'
civilians were shot by Chinese desperadoes. The
military effect of all this, even if more incidents
have to be added to the list before these lines
appear in print, is insignificant and indicates as
complete a lack of psychological knowledge on
the part of the Chinese leaders responsible for
this type of activity as the Japanese bombing
of Canton. If the Chinese think that by such
antics as these they are likely to inspire the
Japanese with fear they are sadly mistaken.
Indignation is the only sentiment which is
likely to be aroused. There is a vast difference
between the prosecution of guerilla activities
behind Japanese lines, where the risk to the
attacker is on a par with the peril to the at-
tacked, but these bombing raids in the Inter-
national Settlement have nothing whatever in
common with that. Taking advantage of the
crowded condition of the Settlement, a few
Chinese throw bombs with a fair margin of
safety and manage to inflict a few deaths and
a small amount of material damage. Nothing
is done in any way likely to have any effect
upon the general military situation. It is more-
over a most cowardly proceeding, for the safety
these bomb throwers seek lies in the fact that
they hope to escape amongst the crowds of
their own countrymen who thus run the risk
of being shot down. The governments of the
Foreign areas of Shanghai by the maintenance
of as strict a neutrality as possible in the cir-
cumstances, have succeeded in offering asylum
to hundreds of thousands of Chinese who
otherwise might have met their deaths outside
Shanghai. That neutrality is being imperilled
by a course of action which can have no pos-
sible effect upon the military fortunes of China,
and amounts only to a programme of cheap
assassination in which their own people suffer
as much as, if not more than, those against
whom their activities have been launched. If
this campaign of "terrorism" has been ordered
by responsible officials of the Chinese Govern-
ment they should be brought to realize the futil-
ity of the whole proceeding, for the murder
of a few innocent civilians of their own
nationality, or one or two Japanese is not only
not worth the effort, but casts a sad reflection
on a government and a people who, it was
believed, had acquired the gift of being able to
suffer with all the dignity of a proud nation.
No nation can be a proud one which resorts to
cheap assassination such as was to be witnessed
in the streets of Shanghai yesterday.
pages.zh:
廉价暗杀

对于昨日中国不良分子为标志敌对行动第一周年结束而上演的幼稚暴力展示，必须找一个除“恐怖主义”以外的其他名称。截稿时据悉，在公共租界和闸北（Chapel，原文疑为Chapei之误）共投掷了不少于十八枚手榴弹，造成数人死亡及轻微损失，同时有一两名看似平民的日本人被中国亡命之徒枪击。即便在这些文字付印前名单上还需增加更多事件，所有这些行为的军事影响也是微不足道的，这表明负责此类活动的中国领导人在心理学知识方面的缺乏，与日本轰炸广州如出一辙。如果中国人认为通过这类滑稽举动可能让日本人感到恐惧，那他们就大错特错了。唯一可能激起的情绪是愤怒。在日军战线后方开展游击活动与在公共租界进行轰炸袭击之间存在巨大差异，前者攻击者承担的风险与被攻击者面临的危险相当，而后者则毫无共同之处。利用租界拥挤的状况，少数中国人以相当高的安全系数投掷炸弹，并设法造成少量死亡和轻微的物质损害。这种做法在任何方面都不可能对整体军事局势产生影响。此外，这是一种极其懦弱的行为，因为这些投弹者寻求的安全感在于他们希望能混入本国同胞的人群中逃脱，从而使这些人面临被射杀的风险。上海各外国区域政府通过在当时情况下维持尽可能严格的中立，成功地为数十万否则可能在上海以外丧生的中国人提供了庇护。然而，一种对中国军事运势不可能产生任何影响、仅构成廉价暗杀计划（其本国人民遭受的痛苦不亚于、甚至超过其行动针对的对象）的行为正在危及这种中立。如果这场“恐怖主义”运动是由中国政府负责任命的官员下令的，应当让他们认识到整个过程的徒劳，因为谋杀几名无辜的本国平民或一两个日本人，不仅不值得付出努力，而且给一个被认为已具备以骄傲民族之尊严承受苦难能力的政府和人民蒙上了悲哀的色彩。任何一个诉诸如昨日上海街头所见之廉价暗杀的国家，都无法成为骄傲的民族。

pages.en:
Dissatisfaction With
Police Measures Shown
By Japanese Consulate

Protest On Terrorism Filed With Council, With
Stress Being Laid On Fact That Repeated
Assurances For Protection Not Upheld

MILITARY SPOKESMAN'S APPRECIATION
OF EFFECTIVE POLICING HERE

Demands that steps be immediately taken to prevent the
recurrence of terroristic outbreaks, such as those witnessed on
Thursday, were made by the Japanese authorities, through their
Consulate-General, upon the Shanghai Municipal Council, a
Japanese Embassy spokesman announced last evening.

The Japanese authorities, the spokesman said, had pointed
out to the Council that terroristic activities in the Settlement
had an unfavourable effect upon the prosperity of the area and
would consequently retard the restoration of the entire Shang-
hai district

Requests had been made to co-operate with the Japanese authori-
ties towards preventing such out-
breaks.

"The Japanese authorities deeply
deplored the fact that Japanese
civilians were made the target of
attacks in the Settlement by ter-
rorist elements," the spokesman
noted.

"In this connection, the fact that
not a single case of terrorism occur-
red in Hongkew yesterday is
significant. We are convinced that
this was achieved through the
efficient control imposed on traffic
at the bridges across Soochow
Creek."

Vigorous Protest

Dissatisfaction with the measures
taken by the Shanghai Municipal
Council in preventing Chinese ter-
roristic activities in the Inter-
national Settlement on Thursday,
the first anniversary of the out-
break of the Sino-Japanese hostili-
ties, was expressed in a vigorous
protest filed by the Japanese Con-
sulate-General with the Council on
Thursday night.

The note recalled the repeated
assurances for the better protection
of Japanese lives and property
made by the Council on previous
occasions in the wake of anti-
Japanese terrorist outrages.

The murder of two Japanese sub-
jects, and the bombing of Japanese
military and civil establishments
in the Settlement on Thursday, the
note was understood to have point-
ed out, did not lend support to the
professions of good intentions made
by the Council, Domel learnt.

A Word Of Appreciation

Meantime, a Japanese military
spokesman yesterday morning ex-
pressed "appreciation of the most
effective policing of the Settlement
south of the Creek" on Thursday.

Two Japanese were shot from the
back and killed and eight bombs
were thrown against Japanese estab-
lishments in the Settlement and
extension roads.

Questioned whether he meant that
the Japanese authorities were satis-
fied with the policing taken after
the two-hour reign of terror early
on Thursday, the spokesman re-
plied: "No, we mean the entire day,
July 7, 1938. From 12 midnight to
12 midnight."

Japanese search parties operat-
ing in the Settlement on Thursday
night, the military spokesman said,
consisted of Japanese military police
dressed in plain clothes "at the ex-
press request of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police."

The parties were operating "joint-
ly and in co-operation with the
Shanghai Municipal Police, whose
heads had given their full ap-
proval."

Friction between minor S.M.P.
officials, apparently uninformed of
their superiors' decisions, and mem-
bers of the search parties occur-
red on Thursday night.

Referring to the reported "oust-
ing" of the Japanese search par-
ties from the American defence
sector, the spokesman declared that
such a situation had arisen because
of interference by minor police
officials and the Shanghai Volun-
teers Corps with the search par-
ties.

"The Japanese search parties
were hemmed in in a part of the
American defence section by the
police," the spokesman said.

The Japanese immediately with-
drew when requested to do so by
the American Marine authorities
represented by a lieutenant.

Taking a serious view of the
allegedly unwarranted interference
by these minor police officials, the
Japanese military, consular and
gendarmerie authorities held a
conference to discuss future steps
yesterday morning, Japanese press
sources indicated.

Agents Of Hankow Blamed

TOKYO, July 8. Terroristic out-
rages in Shanghai on Thursday
were perpetrated by agents of the
Hankow Government, with head-
quarters in the French Concession,
a press message from Shanghai
claimed to-day.

The agents met a few days ago
and arranged the series of bomb-
ings and shootings on Thursday,
the message alleged.

The report predicted that "in
case of necessity Japanese auth-
orities will take action to purge the
International Settlement and French
Concession to prevent a recurrence
of such incidents."

The message said the Reformed
Government of China sent official
notes to the Chairman of the
Municipal Council of the Interna-
tional Settlement and the French
Consul-General, drawing attention
to the frequent outbreaks of ter-
rorism in the Settlement and
French Concession.

Most of the outrages, the notes
said, were aimed at those connect-
ed with the Reformed Govern-
ment. The notes expressed regret
that the authorities of the Settle-
ment and Concession had "failed
to prevent a recurrence of such
untoward incidents or arrest any of
the authors of the outrages."

The notes requested the authori-
ties to take action to suppress ter-
roristic organizations and prevent
such outrages in the future. The
notes enumerated 21 victims of
terroristic outrages, including 12
officials of the Reformed Govern-
ment who were killed and nine
others seriously injured.

Observers predicted that the
Japanese Government may take ac-
tion to prevent terroristic incid-
ents in Shanghai.—Domei.

Gang Under Yang Hu

Terroristic acts perpetrated in
Shanghai on Thursday were com-
mitted by a gang of desperadoes
led by Lieut.-General Yang Hu,
former commander of the head-
quarters of the Shanghai-Woosung
Garrison, the Japanese daily "Nippo"
alleged yesterday.

The paper expressed regret that
the Shanghai Municipal Police had
been unable to prevent the series
of hand-grenade throwings and
shootings on the first anniversary
of the start of hostilities.

Lieut.-General Yang "absconded"
with $2,000,000 collected from Chin-
ese citizens here and fled to Hong-
kong when hostilities started in
Shanghai, the paper alleged. He
returned here recently, the journal
claimed.

The paper predicted that more
terroristic acts will be committed
on the first anniversary of the
start of hostilities in Shanghai on
August 13. The journal warned
the police to be on the watch for
terrorists planning deeds of viol-
ence here on that day.
pages.zh:
日本领事馆对警务措施表示不满

向工部局提出关于恐怖主义的抗议，着重强调反复作出的保护承诺未得到履行

军方发言人对本地有效警务工作的赞赏

据日本大使馆发言人昨晚宣布，日本当局已通过其总领事馆向上海公共租界工部局提出要求，必须立即采取措施，防止再次发生如周四所见的那类恐怖主义爆发事件。

该发言人称，日本当局已向工部局指出，租界内的恐怖主义活动对该地区的繁荣产生了不利影响，因而将阻碍整个上海地区的恢复。

已提出要求与日本当局合作，以防止此类爆发事件。

发言人指出：“日本当局对日本平民在租界内成为恐怖分子袭击目标这一事实深表遗憾。”

“在此方面，昨天虹口未发生一起恐怖主义案件，这一点具有显著意义。我们确信，这是通过对苏州河各桥梁交通实施的有效管制而实现的。”

强烈抗议

日本总领事馆于周四晚间向工部局提交了一份强烈抗议照会，表达了对工部局在周四（即中日敌对行动爆发一周年纪念日）防止中国恐怖主义活动在公共租界蔓延所采取的措施的不满。

该照会回顾了工部局此前在反日恐怖暴行发生后，曾多次保证更好地保护日本人的生命和财产。

据《同盟社》获悉，该照会指出，周四两名日本臣民被谋杀，以及租界内日本军事和民用机构遭到炸弹袭击，这些事实并不支持工部局所宣称的善意。

一句赞赏之词

与此同时，一位日本军方发言人昨天上午对周四“苏州河以南租界地区极其有效的警务工作”表示“赞赏”。

两名日本人从背后被枪杀，八枚炸弹被投掷向租界及越界筑路区域内的日本机构。

当被问及这是否意味着日本当局对周四清晨两小时恐怖统治之后采取的警务行动感到满意时，该发言人回答说：“不，我们指的是整整一天，即1938年7月7日。从午夜12点到次日午夜12点。”

这位军方发言人称，周四晚间在租界内行动的日本搜查队由便衣日本宪兵组成，这是“应上海公共租界警务处的明确要求”而安排的。

这些搜查队“与上海公共租界警务处联合行动并与其合作，警务处高层已给予完全批准。”

周四晚间，一些显然不了解上级决定的公共租界警务处低级官员与搜查队成员之间发生了摩擦。

在提及有关日本搜查队被“驱逐”出美式防区的报道时，该发言人宣称，出现这种情况是因为低级警务官员和上海万国商团干涉了搜查队的行动。

发言人说：“日本搜查队被警察围困在美式防区的一部分区域内。”

当由一名中尉代表的美军海军陆战队当局要求撤离时，日本人立即撤出。

据日本新闻界消息透露，日本军方、领事馆和宪兵队当局鉴于这些低级警务官员涉嫌进行毫无理由的干涉，事态严重，已于昨天上午举行会议，讨论后续步骤。

归咎于汉口政府的特工

东京，7月8日电。据今日来自上海的一则新闻电讯声称，周四在上海发生的恐怖暴行是由以法租界为总部的汉口政府特工所为。

该电讯称，这些特工几天前会面，并安排了周四的一系列爆炸和枪击事件。

该报道预测，“如有必要，日本当局将采取行动，肃清公共租界和法租界，以防止此类事件再次发生。”

该电讯称，中华民国维新政府已向公共租界工部局董事长和法国总领事发出正式照会，提请注意租界和法租界内频繁爆发的恐怖主义事件。

照会称，大多数暴行旨在针对与维新政府有关联的人士。照会对租界和法租界当局“未能防止此类不幸事件再次发生或逮捕任何暴行肇事者”表示遗憾。

照会要求当局采取行动镇压恐怖组织，并防止此类暴行在未来发生。照会列举了21名恐怖暴行的受害者，其中包括12名被杀害的维新政府官员和9名受重伤的其他人员。

观察家预测，日本政府可能会采取行动，以防止上海发生恐怖主义事件。——《同盟社》。

杨虎麾下的帮派

日本日报《日日新闻》昨日声称，周四在上海实施的恐怖行为是由前上海吴淞警备司令部司令杨虎中将领导的一伙亡命之徒所为。

该报对上海公共租界警务处未能在敌对行动开始一周年纪念日防止一系列手榴弹投掷和枪击事件表示遗憾。

该报声称，杨虎中将在上海敌对行动开始时，“卷走”了从此地中国公民那里筹集的200万美元，并逃往香港。该报刊称，他最近回到了这里。

该报预测，在8月13日上海敌对行动开始一周年纪念日，将会发生更多的恐怖行为。该期刊警告警方要警惕计划在那天在此地实施暴力行为的恐怖分子。

pages.en:
“Cheap Assassination”:
Who is Responsible ?

To the Editor of the
“NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS”

SIR.—The anniversary assassina-
tions were “cheap,” you say. Yes,
I agree with you. But I can’t help
feeling that that very editorial
on this subject is likewise “cheap!”
You seem to distrust the integrity
of the Chinese National Government
by your implied indictment of its
officials as if they had aided
and abetted this malicious affair.
The last two sentences of your
leaderette “Cheap Assassination”
are unbecoming for one of your
standing with the Chinese people to
utter. What has led you to suppose
that “this campaign of ‘terrorism’
has been ordered by responsible
officials of the Chinese Government”?
China has never advocated, nor will
she ever advocate, such unstately
acts in order to win a justification
for being proud of herself.

YOUNG CHINESE.
Shanghai, July 8.

* The omission of one very small
word defeats the whole contention of
Young Chinese. This journal wrote
“If this campaign of terrorism has
been ordered by responsible officials
of the Chinese Government.”
The cheapest method of controversy
is by misquotation.—ED.
pages.zh:
“廉价暗杀”：谁该负责？

致《字林西报》编辑

先生——您说周年纪念日的暗杀是“廉价”的。是的，我同意您的看法。但我忍不住觉得，关于这一主题的社论本身也是“廉价”的！您似乎通过暗示指控其官员协助和教唆了这一恶意事件，从而怀疑中国国民政府的诚信。贵报短评《廉价暗杀》的最后两句话，对于一家在中国民众中享有如此声望的报纸来说，是不相宜的。是什么让您认为“这场‘恐怖主义’运动是由中国政府负责任官员下令进行的”？中国从未提倡，也永远不会提倡这种有失体统的行为，以赢得引以为豪的理由。

一位中国青年。
上海，7月8日。

* 漏掉一个非常小的词，就彻底驳倒了这位中国青年的全部论点。本报写道：“如果这场恐怖主义运动是由中国政府负责任官员下令进行的”。最廉价的争论方法就是错误引用。——编者按。

pages.en:
Japanese Protest To
S.M.C. Over Bombings

Dissatisfaction with Precautions Expressed
In Note; Army, However, Pleased with Steps
Taken; Minor Friction with Police

DISSATISFACTION with the measures taken by the Shanghai Municipal Council in preventing Chinese terrorist activities in the International Settlement on Thursday, the first anniversary of the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, was expressed in a vigorous protest filed by the Japanese Consulate-General with the Council on Thursday night.

The note recalled the repeated assurances for the better protection of Japanese lives and property made by the Council on previous occasions in the wake of anti-Japanese terrorist outrages.

The murder of two Japanese subjects, and the bombing of Japanese military and civil establishments in the Settlement on Thursday, the note was understood to have pointed out, did not lend support to the professions of good intentions made by the Council, Domei learned.

Demands that steps be immediately taken to prevent the recurrence of terroristic outbreaks, were made by the Japanese authorities through their Consulate-General upon the Shanghai Municipal Council, a Japanese Embassy spokesman announced yesterday evening.

The Japanese authorities, the spokesman said, had pointed out to the Council that terroristic activities in the Settlement had an unfavourable effect upon the prosperity of the area and would retard consequently restoration of the entire Shanghai district.

Requests had been made to co-operate with the Japanese authorities toward preventing such outbreaks.

"The Japanese authorities deeply deplore the fact that Japanese civilians were made the targets of attacks in the Settlement by terrorist elements," the spokesman noted.

"In this connection, the fact that not a single case of terrorism occurred in Hongkew yesterday is significant. We are convinced that this was achieved through the efficient control imposed on traffic at the bridges across Soochow Creek."

Military Appreciation

In the meantime, a Japanese military spokesman yesterday morning expressed "appreciation of the most effective policing of the Settlement south of the creek" on Thursday.

Two Japanese were shot from the back and killed and eight bombs thrown against Japanese establishments in the Settlement and extension roads.

Questioned whether he meant that Japanese authorities were satisfied with the policing taken after the two-hour reign of terror early on Thursday, the spokesman replied, "No, we mean the entire day, July 7, 1938. From 12 midnight to 12 midnight."

Japanese search parties operating in the Settlement on Thursday night, the military spokesman said, consisted of Japanese military police dressed in plain clothes "at the express request of the Shanghai Municipal Police."

The parties were operating "jointly and in co-operation with the Shanghai Municipal Police whose heads had given their full approval."

Minor Officials Blamed

Friction between minor S.M.P. officials apparently uninformed of their superiors' decisions and members of the search parties occurred on Thursday night.

Referring to the reported resistance of the Japanese search party from the American defence sector, the spokesman declared that such a situation had arisen because of interference by minor police officials and the Shanghai Volunteer Corps with the search parties.

"The Japanese search parties were hemmed in a part of the American defence sector by the police," the spokesman said.

The Japanese immediately withdrew when requested to do so by the American Marine authorities represented by a lieutenant.

Taking a serious view of the alleged unwarranted interference by these minor police officials, the Japanese military, consular and gendarmerie authorities held a conference to discuss future steps yesterday morning, Japanese press sources indicated.

Day Passes Quietly

In striking contrast to Thursday's long series of bombings and shootings yesterday was dead quiet in the International Settlement, with no "incidents" whatever reported either north or south of the Soochow Creek. The French Concession likewise remained undisturbed.

Of the hundreds of suspects arrested in the course of Thursday's countless raids and searches, very few remained in custody yesterday. The Chinese lorry driver who was picked up on The Bund by the Japanese military after the bombings there at 6 a.m. was yesterday turned over by the Japanese Military Police to the Settlement Police, who promptly released him as it had been shown that he had no connection with the attacks. Another Chinese, who was found to have a hand-grenade in his possession when stopped by the French Police, remained in custody.

The strictest vigilance was observed throughout yesterday to prevent new outbreaks of terrorism. Military, S.V.C., Reserve Unit and station police patrols kept operating in the Settlement. Many searches were made in the Central and Louza districts, where alleyways and lodging-houses were entered by the police.

Tailor's Apprentice Held

In their investigation into an abandoned bicycle and long gown in North Soochow Road shortly after the bombing incident in North Tibet Road and Alabaster Road on Thursday morning, the Settlement Police have detained one Nyi Ah-mi, 21-year-old tailor's apprentice. He was remanded by Judge Kiang of the First Special District Court yesterday until next week under a writ of detention.

Detective-Sergeant T. Rossington of the West Hongkew Station, who conducted the investigations, traced the owner of the abandoned bicycle to his shop at 233 Rue Kraetzer. According to the shop proprietor, it was hired by one named Chen with the tailor's apprentice as a guarantee.

The apprentice was found in a house in Zong On Li off Rue de Grouchy in the French Concession. It appeared that the apprentice had hired two bicycles for a friend named Chen in the evening of July 6, but only one was returned to the shop. He did not know the full name of the friend.

Questioned by the Judge, the apprentice denied any knowledge of the bombing in North Tibet Road. He said he was home that morning.
pages.zh:
日本就爆炸事件向工部局提出抗议

照会中表达对防范措施的不满；日军对已采取的步骤表示满意；与警方发生轻微摩擦

周四，正值中日敌对行动爆发一周年之际，日本总领事馆于当晚向上海公共租界工部局提交了一份措辞强烈的抗议书，对工部局在防止中国恐怖分子在公共租界内活动方面所采取的措施表示不满。

该照会回顾了工部局此前在反日恐怖暴行发生后，曾多次保证将更好地保护日本人的生命和财产。

据同盟社获悉，该照会指出，周四两名日本臣民被杀，以及租界内的日本军事和民用机构遭到轰炸，这些事实并不支持工部局所宣称的善意。

日本大使馆发言人昨晚宣布，日本当局已通过其总领事馆要求上海公共租界工部局立即采取措施，防止恐怖事件再次发生。

该发言人称，日本当局已向工部局指出，租界内的恐怖活动对该地区的繁荣产生了不利影响，从而将阻碍整个上海地区的恢复。

日方已提出要求，希望与日本当局合作，以防止此类事件的发生。

“日本当局对日本平民在租界内成为恐怖分子袭击目标的事实深表遗憾，”该发言人指出。

“在此方面，昨天虹口未发生一起恐怖主义案件，这一事实具有重要意义。我们相信，这是通过对苏州河桥梁交通实施有效管制而实现的。”

军方的赞赏

与此同时，一名日本军方发言人昨天上午对周四“苏州河以南租界地区极其有效的警务工作”表示“赞赏”。

两名日本人从背后被枪杀，另有八枚炸弹被投掷向租界及越界筑路区域内的日本机构。

当被问及这是否意味着日本当局对周四清晨两小时恐怖统治之后采取的警务措施感到满意时，该发言人回答说：“不，我们指的是1938年7月7日全天。从午夜12点到次日午夜12点。”

该军方发言人称，周四晚间在租界内行动的日本搜查队由便衣日本宪兵组成，这是“应上海公共租界警务处的明确要求”而安排的。

这些搜查队“与上海公共租界警务处联合行动并予以合作，后者高层已给予充分批准。”

归咎于低级官员

周四晚间，显然未获知上级决定的上海公共租界警务处（S.M.P.）低级官员与搜查队成员之间发生了摩擦。

针对有关来自美防区的日本搜查队遭遇抵抗的报道，该发言人宣称，出现这种情况是因为低级警务官员和上海万国商团干扰了搜查队的行动。

“日本搜查队被警察围困在美防区的一部分，”该发言人说。

当由一名中尉代表的美国海军陆战队当局要求撤离时，日本人立即撤出。

据日本新闻界消息人士透露，鉴于这些低级警务官员涉嫌进行无端干涉，日本军方、领事馆和宪兵队当局于昨天上午举行会议，讨论后续步骤。

平静度过一日

与周四接连不断的爆炸和枪击事件形成鲜明对比的是，昨天公共租界内一片死寂，苏州河南北两岸均未报告任何“事件”。法租界同样保持平静。

在周四无数次的突袭和搜捕中被捕的数百名嫌疑人中，昨天仅有极少数人仍被拘留。早上6点在外滩爆炸案发生后被日军抓获的一名中国卡车司机，昨天由日本宪兵移交给租界警方，警方在查明其与袭击无关后迅速将其释放。另一名中国人在被法国警察拦下时被发现持有手榴弹，目前仍被拘留。

昨天全天保持高度警惕，以防止新的恐怖主义爆发。军队、上海万国商团（S.V.C.）、后备队及各警署巡逻队在租界内持续运作。在中央区和老闸区进行了多次搜查，警察进入了小巷和寄宿房屋。

裁缝学徒被捕

在周四早晨西藏北路和阿尔巴斯特路（Alabaster Road，今海宁路附近）发生爆炸事件后不久，公共租界警方在北苏州路调查一辆被遗弃的自行车和一件长衫时，拘留了一名21岁的裁缝学徒倪阿米（Nyi Ah-mi，音译）。昨天，第一特区地方法院江法官签发拘留令，将其还押至下周。

负责调查的西虹口警署侦探警长T. Rossington追踪到被遗弃自行车的主人位于克勒策尔路（Rue Kraetzer，今新闸路）233号的店铺。据店主称，该车由一名姓陈的人租用，并由该裁缝学徒作为担保。

该学徒在法租界格鲁希路（Rue de Grouchy，今吉安路）宗安里的一处房屋内被发现。据悉，该学徒于7月6日晚为一名姓陈的朋友租了两辆自行车，但只有一辆归还给店铺。他不知道这位朋友的全名。

在接受法官讯问时，该学徒否认知晓西藏北路的爆炸案。他说那天早上他在家。

pages.en:
Clash Of Police
Officers Denied

Dispute Over Japanese
Search Parties Said
Regarded Closed

Terming as "utterly ridiculous"
a Japanese report concerning an
alleged friction among minor
Police officials on Thursday or at
any other time a high official of
the S.M.P. this morning confirmed
however that there had been a
misunderstanding with regard to
the plain-clothed Japanese search
parties that had come into the
settlement on that day. This mis-
understanding, it is understood,
has been cleared by the parties
concerned and the matter is con-
sidered satisfactorily closed.

In the meantime, Shanghai's
"homicide squad," a unit of
special detectives especially creat-
ed on Thursday to investigate all
terrorist acts and assassinations,
was busy going into the dif-
ferent bombing and shooting af-
fairs of the hectic anniversary
day. The unit is attached to
Louza Police Station and the best
men from the detective staffs of
the different stations, have been
drawn upon, for this service.

The Fingerprinting Department
of the S.M.P. examined 616 prints
in 14 hours, ever since the rain of
bombs descended on Shanghai
Thursday morning. They have
thus established, what is believed
to be a world record, with regard
to speed and the number of
examinations made.

All the terrorist acts perpetrat-
ed day before yesterday, were
committed by a gang of des-
peradoes led by Lieutenant-Gen-
eral Yang Hu, former commander
of the headquarters of the Shang-
hai-Woosung garrison, the Japan-
ese daily Nippo alleged yesterday.
Yang Hu is alleged by the paper
to have departed from Shanghai
with $2,000,000 collected from
Chinese Citizens here, at the be-
ginning of the hostilities. He is
said to have been in Hongkong
and returned here recently the
journal alleged.

（批注：There was no misunderstanding...）
pages.zh:
否认警官冲突

称关于日本搜查队的争议已解决

上海公共租界警务处（S.M.P.）一名高级官员今晨称，有关周四或任何其他时间低级警务官员之间 alleged（涉嫌）发生摩擦的日本报道“完全荒谬”，但他同时确认，当天进入租界的便衣日本搜查队确实存在误会。据悉，相关各方已消除这一误会，此事被认为已圆满解决。

与此同时，上海“凶杀组”——一个为调查所有恐怖主义行为和暗杀事件而于周四特别组建的特遣侦探小组——正忙于调查这个动荡的周年纪念日内发生的各类爆炸和枪击事件。该小组隶属于老闸警署，并从各警署的侦探队伍中抽调了最优秀的人员参与此项工作。

自周四上午炸弹如雨点般降落在上海以来，上海公共租界警务处指纹科在14小时内检验了616枚指纹。他们在速度和检验数量方面 thus（因此）确立了被认为是世界纪录的成绩。

日本日报《日日新闻》昨天声称，前天发生的所有恐怖主义行为均由前上海吴淞警备司令部司令杨虎中将领导的一群亡命之徒所为。该报称，杨虎在敌对行动开始时携带从上海中国市民那里筹集的200万美元离开上海。该报刊称，据说他曾在香港，最近返回上海。

（批注：There was no misunderstanding...）

pages.en:
New Section
Of Police Dept.
Starts Work

To Stamp Out Local
Terrorist Moves
Is Goal

The special section of the Shang-
hai Municipal Police, organized
Thursday afternoon, for the pur-
pose of investigating terrorist out-
breaks in the International Settle-
ment commenced functioning from
the Louza Police Station yesterday
morning.

This new unit of the police will
for the time being, devote its entire
time to making inquiries into the
recent acts of terrorism here with
the aim of rounding up the culprits.

The new section's goal is to
stamp out terrorism in the Settle-
ment, or, at least, to make an effort
in that direction. Some of the best
detectives on the force have been
taken from their jobs at police
stations and assigned to the new
unit.

Actually, the section will function
more or less as a "homicide squad."
Its creation will centralize the
handling of investigations into as-
sassinations and other acts of ter-
rorism, and, because of this, it is
hoped that quick and definite results
can be obtained.

In the meantime, Shanghai police
officers and men of the British
and American services in the city
were recovering from a heavy day
on Thursday, July 7, when no less
than 18 bombs and three shooting
affairs took place within the short
space of two hours.

Both yesterday morning and
afternoon were quiet with no in-
cidents of any kind. Nevertheless,
heavy police patrols remained on
the job. Search parties were work-
ing in accordance with the new
schedule outlined last week—name-
ly, from 4 a.m. until midnight.

The 1,000 or more loafers and
questionable characters rounded up
and taken to police stations Thurs-
day afternoon and evening, were
released yesterday morning after
interrogation.

The roundup of these people was
carried out, the police explained, as
a preventative action.

About 1,000 loafers were put under
lock and key for the night as a
means of preventing any possible
spread of the terrorism that ac-
companied the observance of the

pages.zh:
警务处新部门
开始工作

目标是铲除本地
恐怖主义活动

上海公共租界警务处于周四下午组建的特别部门，旨在调查公共租界内的恐怖主义爆发事件，已于昨天上午从老闸警署开始运作。

这个新的警务部门暂时将全部时间用于调查近期在此发生的恐怖主义行为，目的是缉拿罪犯。

新部门的目标是铲除租界内的恐怖主义，或者至少朝这个方向努力。警队中一些最优秀的侦探已从各警署的岗位上抽调出来，分配到新部门。

实际上，该部门的功能或多或少类似于“凶杀组”。它的成立将集中处理对暗杀和其他恐怖主义行为的调查，因此，希望能以此获得快速且确凿的结果。

与此同时，上海的警务人员以及驻沪英美部队官兵正从7月7日周四那沉重的一天中恢复过来，当时在短短两小时内发生了不少于18起爆炸案和三起枪击事件。

昨天上午和下午都很平静，没有任何类型的事件发生。尽管如此，大量的警察巡逻队仍在执勤。搜查队按照上周制定的新时间表工作——即从凌晨4点到午夜。

周四下午和晚上被围捕并带往各警署的1000多名闲散人员和可疑分子，在经过审讯后于昨天上午获释。

警方解释称，对这些人的围捕是作为一种预防性行动进行的。

约1000名闲散人员被关押过夜，以此作为防止伴随纪念活动而可能蔓延的恐怖主义的手段。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 上海公共租界警务处特别科）

pages.en:
1,000 Suspicious Characters Arrested
More than 1,000 suspicious char-
acters were arrested yesterday by
the Shanghai Municipal Police as
a prelude to the cleaning up of
terroristic activities in the Settle-
ment. Although bombings and
shootings occurred only between 5
and 7 a.m., the police, along with
foreign military detachments and
the Shanghai Volunteer Corps, were
busy the rest of the day and far
into the night searching suspects
and arresting all those under
suspicion. No outrages took place
in the French Concession, but police
there were busy too, and the streets
were patrolled by armoured car
units.
pages.zh:
逮捕1000名可疑人物

上海公共租界警务处昨天逮捕了1000多名可疑人物，作为清理租界内恐怖主义活动的前奏。虽然爆炸和枪击事件仅发生在凌晨5点至7点之间，但警方连同外国分遣队和上海万国商团在当天剩余时间及深夜一直忙于搜查嫌疑人并逮捕所有受怀疑者。法租界内未发生暴行，但那里的警方也很忙碌，街道上有装甲车部队巡逻。

pages.en:
Eighteen Bombs Hurled
Here on Anniversary

Four Known Dead, Many Wounded During
Reign of Terror Starting at Daybreak: Two
Japanese Killed; S.V.C. Called Out

IN a day of rampant terrorism unequalled in the history of
Shanghai the first anniversary of the "Lukouchiao incident"
was observed here yesterday, creating an emergency situation
reminiscent of the early days of the war whose beginning it com-
memorated. Eighteen hand-grenades were thrown in various
parts of the International Settlement, both north and south of
the Soochow Creek. Many shots were fired by terrorists and by
Japanese military. Altogether, the known dead were two Japanese
and two Chinese, while the wounded were an Indian watchman at
a Japanese cotton mill and at least a dozen Chinese. Some of
these were in a serious condition last night.

Most of the bombings occurred at
about 6 a.m., chiefly on or close to
the Bund, where the violent explo-
sions were heard—and felt—while
sporadic machine-gun fire in Pootung
furnished a raucous obligato.

The throwers of the bombs escaped,
but one Chinese was arrested by the
French Police with a hand-grenade in
his possession.

The Settlement and French Police
were mobilized in full, the S.M.P.
Specials were called out, the S.V.C.
operated armoured cars and foot
patrols up to a late hour, and in-
numerable searches were made.

Members of the Fourth Regiment,
the United States Marines, turned out
from their barracks to patrol the
American sector, and both lorries and
foot patrols were operating at a late
hour in that area, in Bubbling Well
Road and elsewhere.

One of the most astounding features
of the day was the searching of
houses in the Central and Louza dis-
trict by a party of about 22 members
of the Japanese Military Police, with
drawn pistols, last night. This search
started at about 8.15 o'clock at
Avenue Edward VII and The Bund
and the men, some of whom were
in civilian clothes, slowly "worked
their way" west in Avenue Edward
VII, halting vehicles and pedestrians
on the Settlement side and entering
houses.

British Military Notified

The British Military Headquarters
were notified about this activity in
their sector. It was understood,
further, that representations were
made to the Japanese early in the
evening by high officials of the
Municipal Police and that a party of
policemen went to the scene of the
search from the Louza Station short-
ly before midnight. It was doubted
that the Japanese Military Police
would attempt to extend their opera-
tions to the American sector, which
starts at Yu Ya Ching Road.

The absence of the usual Japanese
military truck convoys on The Bund
and the French Bund was notice-
able throughout the day.

At midnight, while the situation
appeared to be under control, con-
siderable tension remained. At that
time the S.V.C. armoured cars were
deploying in the area between Nan-
king Road and Avenue Edward VII.
The Louza district, where the cus-
tomary amusements—dancing and
roof-garden entertainments—had been
called off, was strangely quiet, but
the atmosphere was nevertheless
electric. The French Concession
appeared to be calm.

The series of well-organized bomb-
ings and shootings started at 5 o'clock
yesterday morning when three hand-

grenades were thrown simultaneously
at a Japanese Naval Landing Party
post off North Tibet Road, at Alab-
aster Road, near the famous bank
godown where the so-called "Lost
Battalion" of Chinese soldiers held
out against the Japanese last autumn.
The bombs did not injure anyone, but
the sentries opened fire and killed
one Chinese and wounded three
others. The body of the Chinese was
later claimed by the Japanese.

The Seaforth Highlanders, who
occupy the West Hongkew sector,
turned out in force immediately after
the bombing and shooting and closed
all the boundary gates. The British
troops started patrolling all the im-
portant thoroughfares in the district,
while the police made a thorough
search of alleyways and houses and
arrested about 150 suspects. A tense
situation prevailed near the boundary
throughout the day.

Two bombs were hurled at the
Japanese Kung Dah Mill, Jessfield
Road at 5.15, causing some damage
but no injury to persons. The Police
Reserve Unit turned out to the scene
from their Gordon Road quarters and
searched the neighbourhood. The
two divisions of the Reserve Unit, led
by Mr. W. E. Fairbairn, Assistant
Commissioner, were kept "on the go"
throughout the day and evening, from
then on, one section being stationed
in the heart of the turbulent Louza
district all day.

Another Mill Bombed

Five minutes after the Jessfield
Road outrage, a similar incident
occurred at the Japan-China Cotton
Mill quarters, 250 Penang Road, into
which two grenades were hurled
from Penang Road. Again, no-one
was injured although the explosions
caused a temporary panic within the
walls.

Simultaneously with this attack, a
Japanese engineer, Mr. Kozaburo
Kano, about 50 years old and em-
ployed by the N.K.W. No. 1 Mill, was
shot several times from behind as he
was riding a bicycle along Robison
Road on his way to work. He was
removed to the Foo Ming Hospital,
North Szechuen, Road, where he later
died.

Twenty minutes afterwards, another
Japanese civilian, Mr. Yasujiro
Shiraishi, employed by the same cot-
ton mill, was fired upon while he
was riding in a public rickshaw at
Tonquin and Markham Roads. He
was shot with a small-calibre pistol
and he likewise succumbed to his
wounds in hospital. Owing to the
proximity to one of their barracks,
members of the Fourth United States
Marine regiment turned out to the
scene of the attack and helped the
police in conducting searches.

At 5.30 three bombs were thrown
into the grounds of the N.W.K. Cotton
Mill quarters, in Gordon Road near
Penang Road, where they exploded.
While the damage was not consider-
able, there was one casualty—that of
an Indian watchman who was wound-
ed slightly.

Bund Shaken by Outbreaks

The scene then shifted to The Bund
north of Nanking Road, where at 6
o'clock two desperate attacks took
place, spreading death and destruc-
tion. These attacks caused the
Japanese Naval Landing Party to post
steel-helmeted sentries along The
Bund and to conduct searches of
Chinese vehicles and pedestrians
simultaneously with the police
searches.

At exactly 6 o'clock two small
bombs of the "Mills" type were
smashed against the wall of the
Yokohama Specie Bank, in whose
building the offices of the Japanese-
sponsored Chinese Civic Association
are situated. One of the missiles ex-
ploded, injuring several Chinese, one
fatally. The dying man was later
picked up near the former City Gov-
ernment Ferry pontoon, foot of
Peking Road, where another bomb
was exploded at 6 o'clock. He had
been so terribly mangled that nothing
could be done to save his life, and
he died almost instantly.

The Yokohama Specie Bank Build-
ing was not badly damaged.

The hand-grenade thrown at the
ferry pontoon which for weeks past
has housed a post of the Japanese
Military Police, again injured some
Chinese pedestrians. The explosion
caused general consternation at the
jetty, and on the ferry pontoon soldi-
ers manned a machine-gun and took
up positions with levelled rifles. Sen-
tries with fixed bayonets were posted
on the Bund foreshore in front of the
former "Floating Restaurant." The
Japanese seized the Chinese driver
of a truck which was passing at the
time and kept him at the ferry pon-
toon post.

Two More Blasts at 6 a.m.

At 6 o'clock also, another bomb
was exploded in the compound of the
Shanghai Land Investment Company,
100 Jinkee Road, causing a crashing
of windows and general panic. No-
one was injured here, however, and
order was soon restored.

A fourth bomb outrage almost at
the stroke of 6 was the hurling of a
hand-grenade, over the barbed-wire,
at a Japanese sentry near the crown
of the Szechuen Road Bridge. The
bomb, which landed close to its target,
did not explode. As a result of this
act the bridge was closed almost im-
mediately by the Japanese military
and no traffic was allowed to pass for
about an hour.

Activity on The Bund after these
attacks assumed a feverish aspect as
police including the "Red Marias" of
the Reserve Unit arrived and started
searching houses, motor-cars and
rickshaws and pedestrians. Beside
the members of the Russian Regiment
S.V.C., who patrol The Bund at all
hours, the Seaforth Highlanders and
the Japanese Naval Landing Party
posted sentries at close intervals,
giving The Bund the appearance of
an armed camp. On the footpath
there were more military than
civilians for some time.

"Ta Tao" Tries a Hand

The main searches were made by
the Reserve Unit personnel and the
Russian Regiment, but it was observed
that five members of the "Ta Tao"
administration police, with yellow
hat-bands, attempted to do some
searching of—and on—their own,
especially near the Peking Road
Jetty. These constables, who carry
no firearms, did not succeed, how-
ever, in functioning and searching on
the Bund yesterday, being promptly
displaced by the lawful authorities
engaged in that work.
pages.zh:
周年纪念日此地遭投掷十八枚炸弹

恐怖统治自黎明开始，已知四人死亡，多人受伤：两名日本人遇害；商团武装被召集出动

昨日在此度过了上海历史上前所未有的恐怖猖獗之日，正值“卢沟桥事变”一周年纪念日，造成了令人想起战争初期（即该事件所纪念的战争开端）的紧急局势。在苏州河南北两岸的国际租界各处，共投掷了十八枚手榴弹。恐怖分子和日军发射了许多子弹。总计已知死者为两名日本人和两名中国人，伤者包括一名在日本棉厂工作的印度守夜人以及至少十二名中国人。其中一些人在昨晚情况危急。

大多数爆炸发生在上午6点左右，主要在外滩或其附近，那里听到了——并感受到了——剧烈的爆炸声，而浦东 sporadic 的机枪射击则提供了嘈杂的背景伴奏。

投掷炸弹者逃脱，但一名携带手榴弹的中国人被法国警察逮捕。

租界警察和法国警察全面动员，上海公共租界警务处（S.M.P.）后备警员被召集出动，上海志愿军（S.V.C.）操作装甲车并进行徒步巡逻直至深夜，并进行了无数次搜查。

美国海军陆战队第四团的成员从营房出动，巡逻美籍居民区，卡车和徒步巡逻队在该区域、静安寺路及其他地方运作至深夜。

当天最令人震惊的事件之一，是昨晚约有22名日本宪兵组成的队伍，手持出鞘手枪，对中区及老闸区房屋进行搜查。这次搜查始于晚上8点15分左右，地点在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）和外滩，这些人员中有些身着便衣，沿着爱多亚路缓慢向西“推进”，拦截租界一侧的车辆和行人，并进入房屋。

英军已获通知

英国军事司令部已获知在其防区内发生的这一活动。此外，据悉，工部局警务处高级官员在傍晚早些时候向日方提出了交涉，且一队警察在午夜前不久从老闸捕房前往搜查现场。人们怀疑日本宪兵是否会试图将其行动扩展到始于虞洽卿路的美籍居民区。

全天值得注意的是，外滩和法外滩通常可见的日本军用卡车车队不见踪影。

午夜时分，虽然局势似乎已得到控制，但紧张气氛依然浓厚。当时，上海志愿军的装甲车正部署在南京路与爱多亚路之间的区域。老闸区往常的娱乐活动——跳舞和屋顶花园表演——已被取消，该地区异常安静，但气氛仍然十分紧张。法租界显得平静。

这一系列组织严密的爆炸和枪击事件始于昨天凌晨5点，当时三枚手

榴弹同时被投向北西藏路、阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）附近的一个日本海军陆战队哨所，靠近著名的银行仓库，去年秋天所谓中国士兵的“孤军营”曾在此抵抗日军。炸弹未造成任何人受伤，但哨兵开火，打死一名中国人，打伤另外三人。该中国人的尸体后来被日方领走。

驻守西虹口地区的 Seaforth Highlanders（海福斯高地团）在爆炸和枪击发生后立即大规模出动，关闭了所有边界大门。英军开始巡逻该地区所有主要干道，而警察则对弄堂和房屋进行了彻底搜查，逮捕了约150名嫌疑人。全天边界附近局势紧张。

5点15分，两枚炸弹被投向杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road，今万航渡路/长寿路一带）的日本公大纱厂，造成一定破坏，但未造成人员伤亡。警察后备队从其戈登路（Gordon Road，今江宁路）驻地出动前往现场，并搜查了周边地区。由副督察 W. E. Fairbairn 先生率领的后备队两个分队从那时起整天和整晚都保持“待命行动”状态，其中一个分队全天驻守在动荡的老闸区中心。

另一家纱厂遭炸

杰斯菲尔德路暴行发生五分钟后，类似事件发生在槟榔路250号的日华棉厂宿舍，两枚手榴弹从槟榔路被投掷进去。再次无人受伤，尽管爆炸在围墙内引起了暂时的恐慌。

与此同时，在这次袭击中，受雇于 N.K.W. 第一纱厂、约50岁的日本工程师加纳幸三郎（Kozaburo Kano，音译）先生在骑自行车沿罗宾森路（Robison Road，今圆明园路）去上班时，从背后被数次射击。他被送往北四川路的福明医院，后在那里死亡。

二十分钟后，另一名受雇于同一家棉厂的日本平民白石康次郎（Yasujiro Shiraishi，音译）先生，在东京路（Tonquin Road，今大名路）和马克姆路（Markham Road，今塘沽路）乘坐公共人力车时遭到枪击。他被一支小口径手枪击中，同样因伤势过重在医院身亡。由于靠近他们的一个营房，美国海军陆战队第四团的成员出动前往袭击现场，协助警察进行搜查。

5点30分，三枚炸弹被投进位于戈登路近槟榔路的 N.W.K. 棉厂宿舍院内，并在那里爆炸。虽然损失不大，但有一人伤亡——一名印度守夜人受轻伤。

外滩因突发事端而震动

随后场景转移到南京路以北的外滩，6点钟发生了两次绝望的袭击，散布死亡和破坏。这些袭击导致日本海军陆战队在外滩部署戴钢盔的哨兵，并与警察搜查同时对中国车辆和行人进行搜查。

正好6点钟，两枚小型“米尔斯”式炸弹被砸向横滨正金银行的墙壁，该建筑内设有日本扶植的上海市市民协会办事处。其中一枚导弹爆炸，炸伤数名中国人，一人致命。这名垂死之人后来在北京路底原市政府轮渡浮码头附近被拾起，另一枚炸弹也在6点钟在那里爆炸。他受伤极其严重，无法挽救生命，几乎立即死亡。

横滨正金银行大楼受损不重。

投向轮渡浮码头的手榴弹再次炸伤了一些中国行人，该浮码头在过去几周内一直驻扎着一个日本宪兵哨所。爆炸在码头引起普遍惊恐，在轮渡浮码头上，士兵们操作一挺机枪，并举起步枪瞄准。在前“浮水餐厅”前的外滩滩地上，部署了装有刺刀的哨兵。日本人扣留了一辆当时经过的卡车的中国司机，并将其关押在轮渡浮码头哨所。

上午6点又发生两起爆炸

同样在6点钟，另一枚炸弹在江西路100号上海地产公司院内爆炸，导致窗户震碎和普遍恐慌。然而此处无人受伤，秩序很快恢复。

第四起近乎在6点整发生的炸弹暴行是，一枚手榴弹被越过铁丝网，投向四川路桥顶附近的一名日本哨兵。炸弹落在目标附近，但未爆炸。作为这一行为的结果，日军几乎立即封闭了桥梁，交通中断约一小时。

在这些袭击之后，外滩的活动呈现出狂热的景象，包括后备队的“红玛丽亚”（Red Marias，指俄籍警员）在内的警察抵达，并开始搜查房屋、汽车、人力车和行人。除了全天候巡逻外滩的俄罗斯团上海志愿军成员外，海福斯高地团和日本海军陆战队也密集部署哨兵，使外滩看起来像一个武装营地。在人行道上，军人在一段时间内多于平民。

“大道”尝试插手

主要搜查工作由后备队人员和俄罗斯团进行，但有人观察到，五名头戴黄色帽带的“大道”政府警察试图自行进行一些搜查，特别是在北京路码头附近。然而，这些不携带枪支的巡捕未能成功在外滩执行职能和进行搜查，很快被从事该项工作的合法当局取代。

pages.en:
Throughout the day Japanese
buildings on The Bund and elsewhere
in the downtown district were care-
fully guarded by the authorities.
Also at 6 a.m. two bombs were
exploded in the compound of the
Kung Dah No 3 Mill, Singapore
Road, without, however, causing
injury to anyone.
At 6:05 a.m. only five minutes
after the series of downtown bomb-
ings - a hand-grenade was hurled at
a Japanese dwelling-house in Macao
Road, near Seymour Road in the
Japanese mill district. No-one was
injured.
Throughout the day, in widely
separated parts of the Settlement and
French Concession, pamphlets and
leaflets were thrown and posters and
slogans placed on walls. The printed
slips and the chalked notices general-
ly urged the cause of the Nationalist
government and assailed the policies
of Japan. The police were active all
day long seizing inflammatory hand-
bills and tearing down political
posters.

Arrested with Grenade

A Chinese carrying a hand-grenade
in his pocket was arrested at about
7 a.m. as he was attempting to elude
a French Police search party in
Avenue Edward VII, opposite Fokier
Road. The man had acted suspicious-
ly in trying to cross from the Con-
cession into the Settlement and the
French policemen halted him. A
search of his person revealed the
bomb, in an inside pocket. He was
later turned over to the Settlement
Police.
It was understood that this suspect
told a story of having come down the
Yangtze River with five other Chi-
nese, all members of a terrorist
organization. A search was conse-
quently started for the alleged other
members of the desperate band.
Arrests of suspects ran into the
hundreds in the two foreign controlled
areas. In the Central and Louza dis-
tricts alone 300 men and women had
been taken into custody up to an
early hour yesterday afternoon. The
West Hongkew police had 150 persons
under arrest as a result of the early
morning outrage there. The French
Police, who searched thousands of
vehicles and pedestrians throughout
the day, also detained many sus-
picious characters.

Special Precautions

Special precautions were taken to
guard the frequently disturbed Louza
district yesterday. Since early morn-
ing, police, S.V.C. and British military
patrols operated in that district and
in the Central district. Mr. H. D. M.
Robertson, Assistant Commissioner of
Police, arranged for further measures
to be taken in the afternoon and eve-
ning. These included patrols by the
Armoured Car Company, S.V.C., be-
ginning at 2.30 p.m., and turning out
the Police Special to do emergency
duty in the area between 6 p.m. and
8 p.m. Further precautions included
the placing of barbed-wire barriers
by the P.W.D. at the entrance to
alleyways opening on Avenue Edward
VII.
Since early morning, searches were
made of hotels and lodging-houses in
the Louza district, where Inspector
A. H. Chamberlain and his men ar-
rested many suspects. Altogether, the
various police station cells were
groaning with prisoners already at an
early hour of the day. Some were
released after they had given satis-
factory accounts of their movements.
In other cases, weapons were seized.
pages.zh:
全天，当局对外滩及市中心其他地区的日本建筑物进行了严密守卫。此外，上午6时，新加坡路（Singapore Road）公大第三纱厂（Kung Dah No 3 Mill）厂区内发生两起炸弹爆炸事件，但未造成任何人员伤亡。

上午6时05分，即市中心系列炸弹爆炸案发生仅五分钟后，一枚手榴弹被投掷向日资工厂区西摩路（Seymour Road）附近澳门路（Macao Road）的一处日本住宅。无人受伤。

全天，在公共租界和法租界相隔甚远的各个区域，有人抛撒传单和小册子，并在墙上张贴海报和标语。这些印刷品和粉笔书写的告示通常宣扬国民政府的主张，并抨击日本的政策。警方全天积极行动，收缴煽动性传单并撕除政治海报。

携带手榴弹被捕

一名中国男子口袋中藏有一枚手榴弹，于上午7时许在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）福开森路（Fokier Road）对面试图躲避法国警察搜查队时被捕。该男子在试图从法租界进入公共租界时行为可疑，被法国警察拦下。对其人身搜查在内袋中发现了炸弹。随后他被移交给公共租界警方。

据悉，这名嫌疑人供称，他与另外五名中国人一同沿长江而下，这些人均为一个恐怖组织的成员。因此，警方开始搜捕这名亡命团伙的其他所谓成员。

在两个外国管辖区域内，被捕嫌疑人数以百计。仅在中央区和老闸区，截至昨天下午早些时候，已有300名男女被拘留。由于清晨在那里发生的暴行，虹口西区警方逮捕了150人。法国警察全天搜查了数千辆车辆和行人，也扣留了许多可疑人物。

特别预防措施

昨天采取了特别预防措施，以保卫经常发生骚乱的老闸区。自清晨以来，警察、上海义勇军（S.V.C.）和英国军队巡逻队在该区及中央区开展行动。警务处副总监 H. D. M. Robertson 先生安排于下午和晚间采取进一步措施。这些措施包括装甲车连和上海义勇军自下午2时30分开始的巡逻，以及调动警察特别队（Police Special）在傍晚6时至8时之间在该区域执行紧急任务。进一步的预防措施还包括由工务处（P.W.D.）在通往爱多亚路的弄堂入口处设置铁丝网障碍。

自清晨以来，警方对老闸区的旅馆和寄宿房屋进行了搜查，督察 A. H. Chamberlain 及其手下逮捕了许多嫌疑人。总之，早在当天清晨，各警察局的牢房就已人满为患。部分人在对其行踪作出令人满意的解释后被释放。在其他案件中，则缴获了武器。

pages.en:
Lone Terrorist
Suspect Faces
District Court

Writ Of Detention Is
Asked Against
Apprentice

Suspected of being implicated in
the hand-grenade tossing Thursday
morning on North Thibet Road near
Alabaster Road because the bicycle
he rented was found abandoned
near the scene of the incident,
Nyi Ah-mi, 21-year-old unemployed
tailor's apprentice, was yesterday
brought before the First Special
District Court for a writ of deten-
tion.

Nyi was the only suspect out of
some 1,000 people rounded up by
the Settlement police after the
terroristic outbreak Thursday who
was taken to the court yesterday
morning. Practically all of the
other arrested persons had been re-
leased after questioning.

Another Under Questioning
Another Chinese, who was arrest-
ed by the French Police on Rue du
Consulat Thursday when he was
found to be carrying two hand-
grenades, is understood to have been
turned over to the Settlement police,
who were yesterday questioning the
man. If evidence is found against
him, he will be taken to the court
this morning.

Municipal Advocate T. Y. Chang,
who asked the writ of detention
against Nyi, told Judge Kiang that
an abandoned bicycle, bearing li-
cense plate 4213 was found near
the scene of the North Thibet Road
bombing. Detective Sergeant T.
Rossington, of the West Hongkew
station, who was investigating the
case traced the vehicle to a bicycle
renting shop on Rue Kraetzer.

Bicycle Rented
The owner of the shop told the
police that Nyi had rented the
bicycle on Wednesday evening, pro-
mising to return it on the following
day. Nyi, however, only brought
back one bicycle Thursday, explain-
ing the other machine would be
returned that afternoon.

Acting on this information, Nyi
was arrested at his home at Zong
On Li, off Rue de Grouchy. Brought
to the court yesterday, Nyi told the
judge that a casual acquaintance of
his, named Chen, had asked him to
rent the bicycles. He could not give
the full name of the man, neither
could he say where the fellow lived.

Nyi told the judge that he was
home early Thursday morning and
that he knows nothing about the
bombing. The case was adjourned
for one week during which time
Nyi was placed in the custody of
the police.
pages.zh:
单独恐怖分子
嫌疑人面临
特区法院审理

针对一名学徒
申请拘留令

21岁的失业裁缝学徒倪阿咪（Nyi Ah-mi，音译）因涉嫌卷入周四早晨在北西藏路（North Thibet Road）靠近阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）处投掷手榴弹一案——因为他租赁的自行车在事发地点附近被发现遗弃——于昨天被提至第一特区法院，当局对其申请拘留令。

倪是周四恐怖爆发后公共租界警方拘捕的约1000人中，唯一于昨天上午被带至法院的嫌疑人。几乎所有其他被捕者在接受讯问后已被释放。

另一人受审

另一名中国男子于周四在领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）被法国警察逮捕，当时发现他携带两枚手榴弹。据悉，他已被移交给公共租界警方，警方昨天正在对该男子进行讯问。如果找到对他不利的证据，他将于今天上午被带上法庭。

市政检察官 T. Y. Chang 向江法官（Judge Kiang）申请对倪发出拘留令，他告诉法官，在北西藏路炸弹案现场附近发现了一辆车牌号为4213的遗弃自行车。负责调查此案的虹口西区警局侦探警长 T. Rossington 追踪该车辆至克勒策尔路（Rue Kraetzer）的一家自行车租赁店。

租赁自行车

店主告诉警方，倪于周三晚上租赁了该自行车，承诺次日归还。然而，倪周四只归还了一辆自行车，并解释说另一辆将在当天下午归还。

根据这一信息，倪在格罗希路（Rue de Grouchy）旁的宗安里（Zong On Li，音译）家中被捕。昨天被带上法庭时，倪告诉法官，是他的一位名叫陈（Chen）的泛泛之交让他去租赁自行车的。他无法提供此人的全名，也无法说明此人住在哪里。

倪告诉法官，他周四清晨一直在家，对炸弹案一无所知。案件休庭一周，在此期间倪由警方羁押。

pages.en:
Demand To
S.M.C. Made
By Japanese

Body Urged To Prevent
Recurrence Of Terror-
ist Outbreak

“REFORMERS” ALSO
PRESENT NOTE

Council Denies Asking
Aid Of Nipponese
Search Parties

A demand that the Shanghai
Municipal Council take immediate
steps to prevent a recurrence of
Thursday’s terroristic outbreak was
made yesterday through the Japan-
ese Consulate General, a Japanese
Embassy spokesman stated last
night.

The spokesman continued that
the terroristic activities in the Set-
tlement had an unfavorable effect
upon the prosperity of this area
and would consequently retard the
restoration of the entire Shanghai
district.

“The Japanese authorities,” the
spokesman said, “deeply deplore
the fact that Japanese civilians
were made the target of attacks in
the Settlement by terrorist ele-
ments. In this connection, the
fact that not a single case of ter-
rorism occurred in Hongkew yes-
terday is significant. We are con-
vinced that this was achieved
through efficient control imposed
on traffic at the bridges across
Soochow Creek.”

While the Japanese military
spokesman yesterday morning ex-
pressed his “appreciation of the
most effective policing of the Set-
tlement south of the Creek,” on
Thursday, the Nipponese Consulate-
General, in a vigorous protest to
the Shanghai Municipal Council,
expressed dissatisfaction with the
measures taken by the S.M.C. to
prevent Chinese terroristic activi-
ties.

The Consul-General’s note which
was presented to the Council
Thursday night, recalled the re-
peated assurances for the better
protection of Japanese lives and
property made by the Council. It
pointed out that the killing of two
Japanese subjects and the bomb-
ing of Nipponese civil and military
establishments failed to lend sup-
port to the assurances.

“Reformers” Protest

At the same time, the Japanese-
sponsored Nanking “Reformed Gov-
ernment,” also sent a protest to
the Council. This protest stated
that the Chinese patriotic activities
were mostly directed against offi-
cials of the Nanking regime.

The Japanese military spokesman,
who expressed appreciation for
effective policing, was asked if he
meant that the Japanese authori-
ties were satisfied with the policing
measures taken after the terroristic
outbreak. He replied: “No, we
mean the entire day, July 7, 1938.
From 12 midnight to 12 mid-
night.”

Request Denied

Meantime, the Japanese military
authorities claimed that the Jap-
anese search parties, consisting of
military police in plain clothes,
were sent to the Settlement at the
request of the Shanghai Municipal
Police.

THE CHINA PRESS was given
to understand yesterday by the
Council that no such request was
made by the S.M.P. to the Japan-
ese.

Nippon Version Given

The Domei news agency report
on this phase of the question fol-
lows:

“The parties were operating
jointly and in co-operation with
the Shanghai Municipal Police
whose heads had given their full
approval.”

“Friction between minor S.M.P.
officials, apparently uninformed of
their superiors’ decisions and mem-
bers of the search parties occurred
on Thursday night.”

“Referring to the reported ‘oust-
ing’ of the Japanese search par-
ties from the American defense
sector, the spokesman declared that
such a situation had arisen because
of interference by minor police offi-
cials and the Shanghai Volunteer
Corps with the search parties.”

“The Japanese search parties
were hemmed in a part of the
American defense sector by the
police,” the spokesman said.

“The Japanese immediately with-
drew when requested to do so by
the American Marine authorities
represented by a lieutenant.”

“Taking a serious view of the
allegedly unwarranted interference
by these minor police officials, the
Japanese military, consular and
gendarmerie authorities held a
conference to discuss future steps
yesterday morning, Japanese press
sources indicated.”

Tokyo Hears Outbreaks

TOKYO, July 8.—(Domei).—Ter-
roristic outrages in Shanghai on
Thursday were perpetrated by
agents of the Hankow Government
with headquarters in the French
Concession, a press message from
Shanghai claimed today.

The agents met a few days ago
and arranged the series of bomb-
ings and shootings on Thursday,
the message alleged.

The report predicted that “in
case of necessity Japanese authori-
ties will take action to purge
the International Settlement and
French Concession to prevent a re-
currence of such incidents.”

Nanking Irritant

The message said the “Reformed
Government” of China sent official
notes to the Chairman of the
Municipal Council of the Interna-
tional Settlement and the French
Consul-General, drawing attention
to the frequent outbreaks of ter-
rorism in the Settlement and
French Concession.

Most of the outrages, the notes
said, were aimed at those connected
with the “Reformed Government.”
The notes expressed regret that the
authorities of the Settlement and
Concession had “failed to prevent
a recurrence of such untoward inci-
dents or arrest any of the authors
of the outrages.”

Action Asked

The notes requested the authori-
ties to take action to suppress ter-
roristic organizations and prevent
such outrages in the future. The
notes enumerated 21 victims of ter-
roristic outrages, including 12 offi-
cials of the “Reformed Government”
who were killed and nine others
seriously injured.

Observers predicted that the Jap-
anese Government may take action
to prevent terroristic incidents in
Shanghai.
pages.zh:
日本向
工部局提出
要求

敦促该机构防止
恐怖爆发再次发生

“维新派”亦
提交照会

公董局否认曾请求
日本搜查队援助

日本大使馆发言人昨晚表示，昨日通过日本总领事馆提出要求，希望上海工部局立即采取措施，防止周四的恐怖爆发再次发生。

该发言人继续指出，公共租界内的恐怖活动对该地区的繁荣产生了不利影响，因而将阻碍整个上海地区的恢复。

这位发言人说：“日本当局对日本平民在公共租界成为恐怖分子袭击目标的事实深表遗憾。在此方面，昨天虹口未发生一起恐怖主义案件，这一事实具有重要意义。我们确信，这是通过对苏州河桥梁交通实施有效管制而实现的。”

虽然日本军方发言人昨天上午对“苏州河以南公共租界极其有效的警务工作”表示“赞赏”，但周四日本总领事馆在向上海工部局提出的强烈抗议中，对工部局为防止中国恐怖活动所采取的措施表示不满。

周四晚提交给公董局的总领事照会回顾了公董局此前就更好地保护日本人生命和财产所作的反复保证。照会指出，两名日本臣民被杀以及日本民用和军事设施遭轰炸的事实，未能佐证这些保证。

“维新派”抗议

与此同时，日本支持的南京“维新政府”也向公董局提交了抗议书。该抗议书称，中国人的爱国活动主要针对南京政权的官员。

当被问及那位对有效警务工作表示赞赏的日本军方发言人是否意味着日本当局对恐怖爆发后采取的警务措施感到满意时，他回答说：“不，我们的意思是指整整一天，即1938年7月7日。从午夜12点到午夜12点。”

请求被拒

与此同时，日本军方声称，由便衣宪兵组成的日本搜查队是应上海公共租界警务处的请求派遣至公共租界的。

《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）昨天从公董局获悉，上海公共租界警务处并未向日本方面提出此类请求。

日方版本

同盟通讯社关于这一问题方面的报道如下：

“各方联合行动，并与上海公共租界警务处合作，其高层已给予充分批准。”

“周四晚间，不知情的下级警务人员与搜查队成员之间发生了摩擦，这些下级人员显然不了解其上级的决定。”

“关于据报道日本搜查队被‘驱逐’出美防区一事，发言人宣称，出现这种情况是因为下级警官和上海义勇队干涉了搜查队的行动。”

发言人说：“日本搜查队被警察围困在美防区的一部分。”

“当由一名中尉代表的美国海军陆战队当局要求撤离时，日本人立即撤出。”

据日本新闻界消息人士透露，鉴于这些下级警官所谓的无理干涉性质严重，日本军方、领事馆和宪兵当局于昨天上午举行会议，讨论后续步骤。

东京获悉爆发事件

东京，7月8日——（同盟社）。——据上海今日发出的一则新闻消息称，周四在上海发生的恐怖暴行是由总部设在法租界的汉口政府特工所为。

该消息称，这些特工几天前会面，安排了周四的一系列炸弹爆炸和枪击事件。

该报道预测，“如有必要，日本当局将采取行动，肃清国际公共租界和法租界，以防止此类事件再次发生。”

南京方面的刺激因素

该消息称，中国“维新政府”向国际公共租界工部局主席和法国总领事发送了正式照会，提请注意公共租界和法租界内频繁发生的恐怖主义爆发事件。

照会称，大多数暴行旨在针对与“维新政府”有关联的人士。照会对公共租界和法租界当局“未能防止此类不幸事件再次发生或逮捕任何暴行肇事者”表示遗憾。

要求采取行动

照会要求当局采取行动，镇压恐怖组织并防止此类暴行在未来发生。照会列举了21名恐怖暴行的受害者，其中包括12名被杀的“维新政府”官员和9名受重伤者。

观察家预测，日本政府可能会采取行动，以防止上海发生恐怖主义事件。

pages.en:
Police Round
Up Hundreds
In Big Drive

Finger Print Bureau Is
Swamped With Total
Of 616 Records

NEW MACHINERY HERE
TO CURB TERROR

Careful Watch Maintained
Yesterday Following
Recent Outbreak

The Shanghai Municipal
Police were yesterday winding
up one of the busiest periods
seen here in many a day in
connection with the first
anniversary of the outbreak of
the hostilities. It was learnt by
"The Shanghai Times" that
over 600 arrests had been made
in the International Settlement
up to an early hour yesterday
morning.

The Settlement and Concession
were comparatively quiet yesterday
following the intensive outbreak the
day before, but a careful watch was
still being maintained in all sections
of the city. It was also learnt that
special machinery has been instituted
for the study and handling of
terroristic activities in the Settlement, but the police stated that they
preferred not to divulge details of
this at the moment.

One terrorist suspect was brought
before the First Special District
Court yesterday morning, when the
police sought to link a tailor's young
apprentice with the bombing at the
corner of North Tibet and Alabaster
Roads. It was also understood that
the Settlement authorities were
holding a Chinese arrested by the
French Police with a hand grenade
in his possession.

Finger Print Bureau

Indicative of the work done by
the police during the emergency is
the record activity which took place
in the Finger Print Bureau. It was
learnt here yesterday that the
Bureau was just winding up work
upon what is probably an all-time
record for finger print identification
in a municipal organization of this
kind.

Under the direction of Sub-
Inspector J. C. Dickson, from 7
o'clock in the morning on Thursday until 2 o'clock yesterday morning, the 21 members of the Finger
Print Bureau staff worked ceaselessly to handle 616 sets of prints
sent in from the 14 stations in the
International Settlement. It is interesting to note that 143 of these
fingerprints were of suspects who
had previous police records.

During the course of a visit to
the Finger Print Bureau yesterday
afternoon, a representative of "The
Shanghai Times" had an opportunity to see how the work is carried out in this essential branch of
the police. The task of examining
over 600 fingerprints during the
course of a few hours assumes very
formidable proportions when the
workings of the Bureau are explained.

Important Role

There are 1,024 primary subdivisions for the fingerprints and a
total of 100,000 subdivisions. At the
present time there are over 300,000
prints recorded in the Settlement
Bureau, including those received in
exchange from the French Police
and from outports. During the
course of a normal year, 30,000
fingerprints are added to the records. The Bureau also has the
photographs and fingerprints of 7,000
criminals arrested in connection
with armed robberies and house-breaking.

It is thus evident that during
the coming months, when a relentless campaign against terrorists will
be inaugurated, the Finger Print
Bureau will play an increasingly
important part on the local crime
front.
pages.zh:
警方大规模搜捕
数百人落网

指纹局被
616份记录
淹没

新设机制在此
以遏制恐怖活动

继近期爆发事件后
昨日保持严密监视

上海公共租界工部局警务处（Shanghai Municipal Police）昨日正结束连日来最为繁忙的时期之一，这与战事爆发一周年有关。据《字林西报》（The Shanghai Times）获悉，截至昨日清晨，公共租界内已有超过600人被捕。

继前一日激烈爆发事件后，租界与法租界昨日相对平静，但全市各区仍保持着严密的监视。另据悉，租界当局已设立专门机制，用于研究和处理恐怖活动，但警方表示目前不愿透露细节。

昨日早晨，一名恐怖嫌疑犯被提审至第一特区法院，警方试图将一名年轻的裁缝学徒与西藏北路和阿尔巴斯特路（Alabaster Roads，今白石路）拐角处的爆炸案联系起来。另悉，租界当局正羁押一名被法国巡捕逮捕的中国男子，该男子被捕时随身携带一枚手榴弹。

指纹局

指纹局在紧急状态期间的工作量之大，从其创纪录的活动可见一斑。昨日获悉，该局刚刚完成了一项工作，其指纹识别数量可能创下了此类市政机构的历史最高纪录。

在副督察 J. C. Dickson 的指挥下，从周四早上7点到昨日凌晨2点，指纹局的21名工作人员不间断地处理了来自公共租界14个警察分局送来的616套指纹。值得注意的是，其中有143枚指纹属于有警方前科的嫌疑犯。

昨日下午，《字林西报》记者走访指纹局时，有机会目睹了这一警察重要部门的工作流程。当了解该局的运作方式后，便会明白在几小时内检查600多枚指纹的任务是多么艰巨。

重要作用

指纹有一级分类1,024种，细分种类共计100,000种。目前，租界指纹局记录的指纹超过300,000枚，其中包括从法国巡捕房和外埠交换获得的指纹。在正常年份，档案中会增加30,000枚指纹。该局还存有7,000名因武装抢劫和入室盗窃被捕的罪犯的照片和指纹。

因此显而易见，在未来几个月即将展开对恐怖分子的无情打击行动时，指纹局将在本地犯罪防治战线上发挥日益重要的作用。

pages.en:
Nipponese Rap
SMP Protection
On Anniversary

Council Sent Protest
By Nippon Consulate
On Terrorism

SMP INTERFERE,
JAPANESE STATE

Terrorist Suspect Up
In Court; Shanghai
Tension Eases

Dissatisfaction with the measures taken by the Shanghai Municipal Council in preventing Chinese terroristic activities in the International Settlement yesterday, the first anniversary of the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, was expressed in a protest filed by the Japanese Consulate-General with the Council last night.

The note recalled the repeated guarantees for the better protection of Japanese lives and property made by the Council on previous occasions in the wake of anti-Japanese terrorist outrages.

Murders Stressed

The murder of two Japanese subjects, and the bombing of Japanese military and civil establishments in the Settlement yesterday, the note was understood to have pointed out, did not lend support to the professions of good intention made by the Council, Domei reported.

Meantime, a Japanese military spokesman this morning expressed "appreciation of the most effective policing of the Settlement south of the creek" yesterday.

Two Japanese were shot from the back and killed and eight bombs thrown against Japanese establishments in the Settlement and extension roads.

The Entire Day

Questioned whether he meant that the Japanese authorities were satisfied with the policing taken after the two-hour reign of terror early yesterday, the spokesman replied: "No, we mean the entire day, July 7, 1938. From 12 midnight to 12 midnight."

Japanese search parties operating in the Settlement last night, the military spokesman said, consisted of Japanese military police dressed in plain clothes at the express request of the Shanghai Municipal Police."

The parties were operating jointly and in co-operation with the Shanghai Municipal Police whose heads had given their full approval."

Friction Reported

Friction between minor S.M.P. officials apparently uninformed of their superiors' decisions and members of the search parties occurred last night, Japanese reports said.

Referring to the reported "ousting" of the Japanese search parties from the American defense sector, the spokesman declared that such a situation had arisen because of interference by minor police officials and the Shanghai Volunteer Corps with the search parties.

Japanese Withdrew

"The Japanese search parties were hemmed in a part of the American defense sector by the police," the spokesman said.

The Japanese immediately withdrew when requested to do so by the American Marine authorities, represented by a Lieutenant.

Taking a serious view of the allegedly unwarranted interference by these minor police officials, the Japanese military, consular and gendarmerie authorities held a conference to discuss future steps this morning, Japanese sources indicated.

Suspect In Court

Out of more than 1000 suspicious characters rounded up by the Settlement police throughout yesterday in connection with the terrorist activities, only one was brought to the First Special District Court this morning when a writ for his detention for a week was granted by Judge Kiang, upon request by Mr. T. Y. Chang municipal prosecutor.

The discovery of an abandoned bicycle, License No. 4213, near the scene of the bombing at the corner of North Tibet and Alabaster Roads led to the arrest of the suspect, one Nyi Ah-mi, 21-year-old tailor-apprentice, in Zong On Li off Rue de Grouchy in the Concession late yesterday afternoon.

Found Bike Shop

Detective-Sergeant T. Rossington of the West Hongkew Station investigating the case, traced the owner of the bicycle to a native bicycle hire shop 233 Rue Krantz. The owner of the shop identified this machine as one of two bicycles hired by the apprentice on the night of July 6. He said that the apprentice brought back only one bicycle yesterday afternoon. The prisoner is said to have promised to bring the other machine later in the evening.

With this information, Detective-Sergeant Rossington with the assistance of the French police located the apprentice at his home on Rue de Grouchy.

Denies Charge

Facing Judge Kiang today, Nyi denied that he was at the scene of the bombing on North Tibet Road yesterday morning. He told the court that he hired the two bicycles on behalf of one Chen, whom he met some time ago. He stated that he did not know the full name of the mysterious Chen. The latter, according to his story, came to him on Wednesday night and asked him to do a favor by hiring two bicycles. The other machine was returned to him early yesterday and since that time, he hadn't seen Chen. The prisoner said that at the time of the bombing he was at home. He was not questioned further by the judge and the case was adjourned for a week. No incriminating evidence against th prisoner has been dug up by the police so far.

Meanwhile, it is understood that the lone Chinese arrested by the French police while carrying a handgrenade yesterday morning shortly after the bombing outrages is still being detained by the S.M. Police for investigation. Most all the suspicious characters nabbed at various lodging houses, teashops, and alleyways, were released, it is learned.

City Quiet

Nothing untoward has since the bombing ended day morning, according information from police at noon.

The different units of the, as well as the two divisions S.M.P. Specials that had called out to assist the regular forces yesterday, have been on duty since late last night, while of the 600 loiterers arrested during yesterday's clearing-up, only some 107, mostly former convicts, are still being detained by the police.

While international police authorities were relieved at the absence of any untoward incident since yesterday morning, they assured the Post that all necessary measures had been taken to cope with any unexpected eventuality that may come up.

No Japanese Seen

No arrests where made today in connection with past terrorist activities, and trouble was experienced, after the last search party left this side of the settlement, shortly after 1 a.m. today.

In the last of these incidents two truck-loads of armed Japanese ronins appeared at the intersection of Yu Ya Ching and Avenue Edward VII shortly after 10 p.m. last night but did not bother to descend from their vehicles, seeing that their proposed task of searching pedestrians and all side streets and alleyways was unattainable insofar as that all side-streets all alleyways had been locked up, no pedestrians were on the streets and strong detachments of U.S. Marines and the Armored Car Company of the S.V.C. kept a close watch on the proceedings.
pages.zh:
日本人指责
工部局警务处在
周年纪念日的保护工作

日本领事馆
就恐怖主义问题
向公董局提出抗议

日本人称
工部局警务处进行干涉

恐怖嫌疑犯出庭；
上海紧张局势缓和

日本总领事馆昨晚向公董局提交了一份抗议书，表达了对上海公共租界工部局在昨日——即中日敌对行动爆发一周年纪念日——防止中国人在公共租界内进行恐怖活动所采取措施的不满。

照会回顾了公董局此前在反日恐怖暴行发生后，多次承诺更好地保护日本人的生命和财产。

强调谋杀案

据同盟社（Domei）报道，据悉该照会指出，昨日两名日本臣民被谋杀，以及租界内的日本军事和民用机构遭到轰炸，这些事实并不支持公董局所宣称的良好意愿。

与此同时，一位日本军方发言人今早表示，“赞赏”昨日“苏州河以南租界地区”的高效警务工作。

两名日本人从背后被枪杀，另有八枚炸弹被投掷向租界及越界筑路区域的日本机构。

整整一天

当被问及他是否意指日本当局对昨日清晨两小时恐怖统治之后采取的警务措施感到满意时，该发言人回答说：“不，我们指的是1938年7月7日整整一天。从午夜12点到次日午夜12点。”

这位军方发言人称，昨晚在租界内行动的日本搜索队由便衣日本宪兵组成，这是应上海公共租界工部局警务处的明确要求安排的。

这些搜索队与上海公共租界工部局警务处联合行动并相互合作，后者高层已给予充分批准。

据报道发生摩擦

日方报告称，昨晚，一些显然未获知上级决定的工部局警务处低级官员与搜索队成员之间发生了摩擦。

在提及据报道日本搜索队被“驱逐”出美式防区一事时，该发言人宣称，出现这种情况是因为低级警官和上海万国商团（Shanghai Volunteer Corps）对搜索队进行了干涉。

日本人撤离

发言人说：“日本搜索队被警察围困在美式防区的一部分。”

当代表美军当局的一名中尉要求日本人撤离时，他们立即撤出。

日方消息人士暗示，鉴于这些低级警官涉嫌无理干涉，日本军方、领事馆和宪兵队当局今早举行会议，讨论后续步骤。

嫌疑犯出庭

在昨日全天因恐怖活动被租界警方搜捕的1000多名可疑人物中，仅有一人于今晨被提审至第一特区法院。应市政检察官 T. Y. Chang 先生请求，江法官（Judge Kiang）批准将其拘留一周。

在西藏北路和阿尔巴斯特路拐角处的爆炸现场附近发现一辆被遗弃的自行车，牌照号为4213，这导致了一名嫌疑人的被捕。该嫌疑人名为倪阿米（Nyi Ah-mi，音译），21岁，是一名裁缝学徒，昨日下午晚些时候在法租界格鲁希路（Rue de Grouchy，今吉安路）附近的宗恩里（Zong On Li，音译）被捕。

找到车行

负责调查此案的西虹口捕房警佐 T. Rossington 追踪到该自行车的主人位于克兰茨路（Rue Krantz，今康定路）233号的一家本地自行车租赁行。店主指认该车是这名学徒在7月6日晚租用的两辆自行车中的一辆。他说，这名学徒昨日下午只归还了一辆自行车。据称，囚犯曾答应当晚晚些时候归还另一辆车。

凭借这一信息，Rossington 警佐在法国巡捕的协助下，在格鲁希路的住所找到了这名学徒。

否认指控

今日面对江法官，倪某否认昨日早晨曾在西藏北路爆炸现场。他告诉法庭，他是替一个姓陈的人租的两辆自行车，此人是他不久前认识的。他表示不知道这位神秘的陈某的全名。据他陈述，陈某在周三晚上找到他，请他帮个忙，租两辆自行车。另一辆车在昨日清晨还给了他，自那以后他就没见过陈某。囚犯称爆炸发生时他正在家中。法官未再对他进行讯问，案件延期一周审理。截至目前，警方尚未挖掘出针对该囚犯的任何定罪证据。

与此同时，据悉，昨日早晨爆炸暴行发生后不久，被法国巡捕逮捕的那名随身携带手榴弹的唯一一名中国男子，仍被上海公共租界工部局警务处羁押调查。据了解，在各旅馆、茶馆和弄堂里抓获的几乎所有可疑人物均已被释放。

城市平静

据中午警方提供的信息，自昨日早晨爆炸结束以来，未发生任何异常事件。

各分队以及昨日被召出协助正规军的两个连队的工部局警务处特务队（S.M.P. Specials），自昨夜深夜起一直执勤。而在昨日清理行动中逮捕的600名闲散人员中，仅有约107人（大多为前科犯）仍被警方拘留。

虽然国际警察当局对自昨日早晨以来未发生任何意外事件感到宽慰，但他们向《邮报》保证，已采取一切必要措施，以应对可能出现的任何突发状况。

未见日本人

今日未因过去的恐怖活动进行任何逮捕，且在最后一支搜索队于今日凌晨1点后离开租界这一侧后，也未遇到麻烦。

在这些事件的最后一起中，昨晚10点后不久，两卡车武装日本浪人出现在虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road，今六合路）和爱德华七世大道（Avenue Edward VII，今延安东路）的交叉口，但看到他们搜查行人及所有支路和弄堂的预定任务无法实现——因为所有支路和弄堂都已锁闭，街上没有行人，且美国海军陆战队分队和上海万国商团装甲车队严密监视着事态发展——他们便懒得下车。
