BOMBS EXPLODE OVER CITY

**Mobilization Here To Curb Terror Wave**
Armoured Cars Rumble Through Streets Of Settlement

**SEARCH PARTIES ON AVE. EDWARD VII**

The most rigid precautions since the termination of the hostilities in the Shanghai area were taken here yesterday by the Settlement Police, the French Police, the Shanghai Volunteer Corps and the several military forces on the occasion of the first anniversary of the Marco Polo bridge incident.

During the latter part of the day several platoons from the civilian section of the Shanghai Volunteer Corps were turned out for patrol duty, and until 11 o'clock armoured cars rumbled through the Settlement streets. These worked on two hour shifts in Louza, Sinza, Central and Babbling Well districts at all 16 cars in all being put on patrol duty.

The duties of the Russian Regiment were confined to patrolling the Bund and Avenue Edward VII as far out as Moulmein Road, while during the course of the day members of this unit were also sent along Yu Ya Ching and Peking Roads.

The Seaforth Highlanders also patrolled the Bund and marched along Nanking Road throughout the day. The Fourth Marines did patrol work all day in their sector and the Italian troops were also on duty all the time.

**French Concession**

An added precaution was taken by the police in placing search parties of Chinese constables under foreign sergeants at all the road intersections along Avenue Edward VII. Throughout the day thousands of pedestrians coming in from the French Concession were searched for guns or hand-grenades.

The French police also did very good work during the day, and everywhere throughout the Concession the usual police guards were reinforced. The new light armoured cars recently purchased by the Concession were also seen patrolling along the streets to maintain order and let it be known that emergency measures were in force.

At about 8.30 o'clock last night, a party of 34 plainclothes Japanese gendarmes alighted from two trucks at the corner of the Bund and Avenue Edward VII and conducted a search of all Chinese male pedestrians remaining in the area for about three-quarters of an hour before proceeding to the Kiangse Road junction where they continued operations. Two S.V.C. Armoured Car units, who were passing by at the time, remained on the spot, as did several members of the Russian Regiment, until the Japanese made their departure.

**Terrorists Assassinate Two Japanese, Marking First War Anniversary**
GUNMEN, BOMB THROWERS STRIKE BEFORE DEVISED PRECAUTIONS ARE BROUGHT INTO OPERATION AFTER DAWN

**THREE CHINESE KILLED, EIGHT HURT AND TWO JAPANESE WOUNDED**

**One Suspected Terrorist Seized By Japanese On Bund, One Arrested In Concession; Volunteers, Seaforths On Patrols**

Striking immediately after the lifting of curfew at five o'clock yesterday morning, and before the bringing into operation of the widespread precautionary measures devised for the day by the various authorities, Chinese bomb-throwers, and terrorist gunmen staged an unprecedented reign of terror in the International Settlement, for a period of one hour.

Eighteen hand-grenades, several of which did not explode, were thrown in the International Settlement and vicinity in the early morning, and two assassinations of Japanese mill employees were carried out in the same time—as a part of the observance of the first anniversary of the outbreak of hostilities at Lukouchiao, near Peking, on July 7, 1937.

When the excitement had died down a little and the police telephones stopped ringing, announcing with every fresh call another bombing outrage or assassination, it was ascertained that two Japanese and two Chinese had paid with their lives, while three other Japanese, eight Chinese and one Sikh were wounded during the short-lived terroristic overture to the day of the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities.

A Chinese truck driver, alleged to be a terrorist, was arrested by Japanese military on the Bund, shortly after the bombing of the City Government Ferry. A grenade was found in the truck he was driving.

Another alleged terrorist was arrested by a French Police search party on Rue du Consulat. A grenade was found in his possession.

**First Burst**

The first burst of the morning took place at 5.05 a.m. when the sound of gun-fire was heard at Alabaster Road, near Thibet Road. There Japanese sentries had opened fire on four Chinese, who had thrown hand-grenades at them. One of the Chinese was killed and his body was removed by the Japanese to Chapei, while the three wounded Chinese were taken to the Lester Chinese Hospital in an ambulance for treatment for bullet wounds. The grenades thrown at the Japanese sentries did not explode.

Seven minutes later, two bombs were thrown at the Japanese-owned Kung Dah Cotton Mill, at 138 Jessfield Road. A number of windows was broken, but there were no casualties. Eight minutes after this, at 5.20 a.m., the staff quarters of the Japan-China Cotton Mill, also Japanese owned, at 250 Penang Road was the subject of attack. Two bombs were thrown, but damage was only slight.

**Japanese Killed**

At about the same time as the bombs were thrown at the Japan-China Cotton Mill, Mr. Kozaburo Kano, employee of the No. 1 Mill of the Nagai Wata Kaisha, was shot and killed by an unidentified assailant, while riding on a bicycle along Robison Road, near Ferry Road.

Twenty minutes later, at 5.40 a.m., the second Japanese victim, Mr. Yusujiro Shiraishi, an employee of the No. 9 Mill of the same Company, was brutally killed, being shot from behind, while riding to work in a ricksha along Markham Road near Tongqin Road. He was rushed in an ambulance to the Foo Min Hospital on North Szechuen Road but was pronounced dead on arrival. Two gunmen were reported to have made the attack on Mr. Shiraishi, firing four shots in all.

**Sikh Hurt**

At 5.30 a.m. three bombs were thrown into the compound of the Nagai Wata Kaisha Cotton Mill, at Gordon and Penang Roads. An Indian watchman was slightly injured and taken to hospital.

There was quiet for half-an-hour and then a series of bombing outrages were staged in the Central district. Five bombs were thrown at four different locations, all at 6 o'clock in the morning.

The first bomb was thrown into the compound of the Shanghai Land Investment Company, at 120 Jinkee Road. Slight damage was done. At about the same time another bomb

炸弹在全市爆炸

**本地动员以遏制恐怖浪潮**
装甲车在租界街道上隆隆驶过

**爱德华七世大道上的搜查队**

昨日，适逢卢沟桥事变一周年之际，租界巡捕房、法国巡捕房、上海万国商团以及各军事部队采取了自上海地区战事结束以来最为严密的预防措施。

当日下午晚些时候，上海万国商团平民部队的数个排被派出执行巡逻任务，直至晚上11点，装甲车一直在租界街道上隆隆行驶。这些车辆在老闸、新闸、中央和大世界（Babbling Well）地区分两班轮流执勤，共计16辆装甲车全部投入巡逻任务。

俄国团的职责限于在外滩及爱德华七世大道（Avenue Edward VII）巡逻，远至莫尔尼路（Moulmein Road），而在当天期间，该部成员也被派往虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）和北京路。

苏格兰海福斯高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）也在全天巡逻外滩，并沿南京路行进。美国海军陆战队第四团在其防区内全天执行巡逻任务，意大利军队也始终处于执勤状态。

**法租界**

警方采取了一项额外预防措施，即在爱德华七世大道沿线的所有路口，由外籍警长率领华籍巡捕组成搜查队。全天内，成千上万从法租界进入的行人均被搜查是否携带枪支或手榴弹。

法国巡捕房在当天的工作也非常出色，法租界各处的常规警力守卫均得到加强。法租界最近购置的新型轻型装甲车也被看到在街道上巡逻，以维持秩序并显示紧急措施正在实施中。

昨晚约8时30分，一队34名便衣日本宪兵在两辆卡车抵达外滩与爱德华七世大道拐角处下车，对该区域剩余的所有男性华人行人进行了约四十五分钟的搜查，随后前往江西路路口继续行动。当时路过的两支上海万国商团装甲车分队，以及数名俄国团成员，一直留在现场，直到日本人离开。

**恐怖分子刺杀两名日本人，标志战争一周年**
**枪手、投弹者在黎明后、既定预防措施生效前发动袭击**

**三名中国人死亡，八人受伤，两名日本人受伤**

**一名嫌疑恐怖分子在外滩被日军抓获，一人在法租界被捕；商团、海福斯高地团参与巡逻**

昨日清晨五时宵禁解除后，在各当局为当日制定的广泛预防措施尚未完全生效之前，中国投弹者和恐怖主义枪手立即发动袭击，在国际租界制造了长达一小时的空前恐怖统治。

清晨，在国际租界及周边地区投掷了十八枚手榴弹，其中数枚未爆炸；与此同时，发生了两起针对日本纱厂员工的暗杀事件——这是为了纪念1937年7月7日北平附近卢沟桥战事爆发一周年。

当骚动稍息，报警电话不再响个不停、不再每次来电都报告新的炸弹暴行或暗杀事件时，经查明，两名日本人和两名中国人丧生，另有三名日本人、八名中国人和一名锡克教徒在这短暂的、作为中日战事爆发日序幕的恐怖活动中受伤。

一名据称是恐怖分子的中国卡车司机，在上海市政府轮渡遭炸弹袭击后不久，在外滩被日军逮捕。在他驾驶的卡车中发现了一枚手榴弹。

另一名据称是恐怖分子的人，在领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）被法国巡捕房的搜查队逮捕。在他身上发现了一枚手榴弹。

**第一波袭击**

清晨的第一波袭击发生在上午5时05分，当时在西藏路附近的阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）听到枪声。日本哨兵向四名向他们投掷手榴弹的中国人开火。其中一名中国人被打死，其尸体被日本人运往闸北，另外三名受伤的中国人则由救护车送往莱斯特长老会医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）治疗枪伤。投向日本哨兵的手榴弹并未爆炸。

七分钟后，两枚炸弹被投掷位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）138号的日资公大纱厂（Kung Dah Cotton Mill）。多扇窗户被打破，但无人伤亡。八分钟后，即上午5时20分，同样为日资的中日纱厂（Japan-China Cotton Mill）位于槟榔路（Penang Road）250号的职员宿舍遭到袭击。两枚炸弹被投掷，但损失轻微。

**日本人遇害**

大约在中日纱厂遭投弹的同时，永泰纱厂（Nagai Wata Kaisha）第一厂的雇员加纳小三郎先生（Mr. Kozaburo Kano）在靠近斐伦路（Ferry Road）的罗宾森路（Robison Road）骑自行车时，被一名身份不明的袭击者枪杀。

二十分钟后，即上午5时40分，第二名日本受害者，同公司第九厂的雇员白石勇次郎先生（Mr. Yusujiro Shiraishi），在靠近通勤路（Tongqin Road）的马克姆路（Markham Road）乘人力车上班途中，被人从背后开枪残忍杀害。他被救护车紧急送往北四川路的福民医院（Foo Min Hospital），但到达时已被宣布死亡。据报道，两名枪手对白石先生发动了袭击，共开了四枪。

**锡克教徒受伤**

上午5时30分，三枚炸弹被投进位于戈登路（Gordon Road）和槟榔路交汇处的永泰纱厂厂区。一名印度看守受轻伤并被送往医院。

随后平静了半小时，接着在中央区上演了一系列炸弹暴行。上午6时整，在四个不同地点共投掷了五枚炸弹。

第一枚炸弹被投进位于静安寺路（Jinkee Road）120号的上海地产投资公司（Shanghai Land Investment Company）厂区。造成轻微损失。大约同时，另一枚炸弹

所有在傍晚早些时候动员的上海万国商团平民部队于昨晚11时解散。警察后备队待命至午夜，此时大多数全天执勤的人员得到了应有的休息。然而，警方维持了异常严密的监视，直至今日凌晨早些时候，违反宵禁者受到严厉处置。

警方在整个白天对闲逛者和嫌疑人进行了围捕，到夜幕降临时，大多数租界捕房的牢房都已人满为患。据报道，有数百人被捕。

被投向北四川路广场的日本海军陆战队哨兵。手榴弹未能爆炸。据信是从北苏州路（North Szechow Road）、邮政总局附近投掷的。
外滩暴行
大约在同一时间，外滩发生了两起暴行。一枚手榴弹被投向前上海市政府轮渡，致使一名日本人和三名中国人受伤；紧随其后，一名被认为是恐怖分子的卡车司机在外滩被日军抓获，当时在他驾驶的卡车中发现了一枚手榴弹。
几乎就在市政府轮渡爆炸之后，两枚手榴弹在横滨正金银行（Yokohama Specie Bank）附近爆炸，炸死一名中国路人，炸伤另外两人。上午6时05分，一枚炸弹被投向西摩路（Seymour Road）附近澳门路（Macao Road）的一处中国住宅。造成轻微损失。
至此，国际租界上午的暴行结束。后来从日军控制的闸北地区传来报告称，一名身份不明的人据称从界路（Boundary Road）向北站投掷了一枚手榴弹。据报道无伤亡。另一枚炸弹在闸北海宁北路（North Haining Road）附近投掷，炸伤两名日本人。
警方行动
从上午5时起，国际租界各捕房的警察一直处于警戒状态，迅速赶赴接连发生的炸弹袭击和暗杀现场。后备队在约两小时内被紧急调往各处，而上海万国商团俄国分队和苏格兰海福斯高地团的重兵巡逻队也被派往外滩，协助警方维持和平与秩序。炸弹暴行发生后，日本人也立即派遣大量部队沿外滩部署。
日本海军陆战队也被紧急派往西区受袭的各纱厂厂区，但这些部队在当天晚些时候撤出。
外国军事巡逻增加。海福斯高地团驻守在外滩与南京路交汇处以及外滩与北京路交汇处。额外的高地团巡逻队在南京路上来回行进。美国海军陆战队第四团、意大利军队和英国军队在其防区内警惕 disturbances（骚乱）。
商团俄国分队的巡逻范围从外滩沿爱德华七世大道延伸。日本宪兵哨兵被部署在外滩靠近南京路的地方。
警察搜查队在路口和繁忙街道上积极活动。在警察检查卡车和汽车时，某些地方的交通被迫中断。

pages.en:
YESTERDAY'S TERRORISM
Worst fears were realized yesterday
when a whole series of terroristic acts
was staged, doubtless to mark the
anniversary of the outbreak of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities. Details of the
serious incidents will be found fully
recorded in our news columns, and the
reaction in any intelligent person's mind
must be the entirely negative and
destructive result of the outrages. Noth-
ing at all worthwhile is accomplished by
the throwing of bombs or the assassina-
tion of Chinese whose work brings them
into contact with Japanese interests.
China's war against Japan is not helped
in the slightest way. When questions are
asked in the House of Common regard-
ing the non-running of tramcars over the
Garden Bridge, or the keeping closed of
certain local areas, how can hopeful
answers be given in the face of Chinese-
staged terrorism? If yesterday's happen-
ings in Shanghai are fully reported in
the London press, as they doubtless will
be, Members of Parliament must surely
understand for themselves the extremely
difficult position in which the Japanese
authorities here are placed. Shanghai's
greatest enemies are those who carry out
these terroristic acts, for all sections of
the community suffer thereby. High
tribute must be paid to the police forces
of both the Settlement and the Concession
for the splendid work done yesterday,
and also to those military units which
helped them in that work. In such an
organized orgy of secretly planned
terrorism it is impossible for any police
force to forestall those committed to such
dire work, but the promptitude with
which action was taken, the maintenance
of heavy patrols during the busy periods
of the day, and the vigilance shown was
a further piece of creditable work on
the part of men who have already earned
so well of the community.
pages.zh:
昨日的恐怖主义
昨日，一系列恐怖主义行为上演，无疑是为了纪念中日战事爆发周年，人们最担心的情况成为了现实。严重事件的详情已在我们的新闻栏目中充分记录，任何理智之人的反应必然是这些暴行带来的完全负面和破坏性的结果。投掷炸弹或暗杀那些因工作而与日本利益发生接触的中国人，根本不能成就任何有价值的事情。这对中国的对日战争毫无助益。当下议院就花园桥电车停运或某些局部地区封闭提出问题时，面对中国人制造的恐怖主义，怎能给出充满希望的回答？如果昨日上海的事件像毫无疑问会发生的那样在伦敦报刊上得到充分报道，议员们必定会自行理解日本当局在此地所处的极其困难的境地。上海最大的敌人是那些实施这些恐怖主义行为的人，因为社会各阶层都因此受苦。必须对租界和法租界的警察部队昨日所做的出色工作，以及对协助他们工作的军事单位致以崇高的敬意。在这种有组织、秘密策划的恐怖主义狂欢中，任何警察部队都不可能预防那些致力于此类可怕罪行的人，但采取行动之迅速、在日间繁忙时段维持重兵巡逻以及所表现出的警惕性，是这些已为社区赢得良好声誉的人士又一值得称赞的工作。

pages.en:
1,000 Suspects
Said Nabbed By
Local Police

Biggest Raid In History
Carried Out To Curb
Terrorism

The arrest of more than 1,000
suspicious characters and the tenta-
tive formation of a special section
to carry investigations into recent
terroristic activities were among
the major achievements of the
Shanghai Municipal Police force
yesterday.

The arrests were made in scores
of raids, and after almost endless
searches of alleyways, sidestreets,
tea-houses and other gathering
places of loafer and gangster
bands.

Commencing shortly before 9
a.m., about two hours after the
last bomb was thrown in the wave
of terror that spread over this city
during the early morning, police
raiding parties were active through-
out the city.

150 Nabbed In West Hongkew

In the West Hongkew district
alone, more than 100 men of the
loafer class were nabbed and
thrown into detention cells for the
night.

Raids and the arrest of suspi-
cious characters in the Central
District netted an increase in the
Central Jail population for the
night of more than 60 tough-
looking boys.

Even Crime Branch Headquarters
detectives, busy solving other
crimes, joined in the work and
rounded up more than a dozen
men who appeared as though they
might be capable of throwing a
bomb, or shooting a pistol.

From the Louza Police Station,
both foreign and Chinese detectives
were busy throughout the day
roping in suspicious characters.
Patrols and squads of plainclothes
men from all other police stations
in the Settlement were busy doing
the same thing and late last night,
it was roughly estimated that more
than 1,000 persons, allegedly of the
loafer class, were being kept at
police stations for the night.

Biggest Raid In History

The roundup of these suspicious
individuals was perhaps the biggest
in Shanghai's long and colorful
history. The action was not taken,
so much in an effort to locate the
terrorists responsible for yesterday's
bombings and killings, but rather
with the idea of removing 1,000 or
more potential gunmen and bomb-
tossers from the streets and alley-
ways of the city.

Scores of suspicious looking men,
unable to explain their reasons for
being on the street, or wherever
they happened to be at the time
they were approached by the
police, were slapped in handcuffs
and marched to the police station.
Men who gave evasive answers to
questions of the police were treat-
ed likewise.

It was not an uncommon sight to
see detectives marching a gang of
seven or eight men, all linked toge-
ther with handcuffs, down a street
in the busy Central district toward
the police station. And raiding
vans were filled with suspicious act-
ing individuals.

It is quite likely that a large
number of these people will be re-
leased this morning. Others, who
may have been found with weapons
or bombs, in their possession, will
naturally be held for further in-
vestigation. It could not be con-
firmed last night as to whether or
not pistols and bombs had been
found on the persons of pedes-
trians, but the raids were still
continuing at a late hour last
night. Weapons may turn up be-
fore the searches and raids have
been concluded.

New Police Section

Although not officially announced
last night, a CHINA PRESS re-
porter learned that a special section
of the Shanghai Municipal Police
is now in the process of creation
for the express purpose of handling
investigations of terrorist cases.

Some of the best detectives on
the police force are to be assigned
to this special section and will
probably commence their investiga-
tion work this morning.
pages.zh:
据称本地警方
逮捕一千名嫌疑犯

为遏制恐怖主义
实施史上最大规模搜捕

上海公共租界工部局警务处昨日取得重大成果，其中包括逮捕了一千多名可疑分子，并初步组建了一个特别部门，以对近期的恐怖活动展开调查。

逮捕行动是在数十次突击搜查中进行的，警方对小巷、支路、茶馆以及其他游民和帮派团伙的聚集场所进行了近乎无休止的搜查。

清晨时分，这座城市笼罩在一波恐怖浪潮之中，最后一枚炸弹被投掷后约两小时，即上午9点前不久，警方的突击小队便在全市范围内展开行动。

虹口西区逮捕150人

仅在虹口西区，就有超过一百名游民阶级男子被捕，并被关入拘留所过夜。

在中央区的突击搜查和对可疑分子的逮捕，使得中央监狱当晚的在押人数增加了六十多名看起来不好惹的青年。

甚至刑事科总部的侦探们，尽管正忙于侦破其他案件，也加入了此次行动，围捕了十多名看似有能力投掷炸弹或开枪射击的男子。

来自老闸捕房的中外侦探整天都在忙着拘捕可疑分子。租界内所有其他捕房的巡逻队和便衣小队也在忙于做同样的事情。昨晚深夜，粗略估计有一千多名据称属于游民阶级的人被留在各捕房过夜。

史上最大规模搜捕

对这些可疑人员的围捕，或许是上海漫长而多彩的历史中规模最大的一次。采取这一行动，并非主要为了找出负责昨日爆炸和杀人事件的恐怖分子，而是旨在将一千名或更多潜在的枪手和炸弹投掷者从城市的街道和小巷中清除出去。

数十名形迹可疑的男子，因无法解释为何出现在街头，或在警察接近时身处何地，而被戴上手铐，押往捕房。那些对警察提问给出含糊其辞回答的人，也受到了同样的对待。

在繁忙的中央区，看见侦探们押解着一群七八名全部用手铐连在一起的男子沿街道走向捕房，已非罕见景象。突击搜查的车辆里也挤满了行为可疑的人。

这些人中的很大一部分很可能将于今早获释。其他可能被发现持有武器或炸弹的人，自然会被扣留以作进一步调查。昨晚尚无法确认是否在行人身上搜出手枪和炸弹，但直到昨晚深夜，搜捕行动仍在继续。在搜查和突击行动结束之前，可能会有武器被发现。

新设警务部门

虽然昨晚尚未正式宣布，但《字林西报》（China Press）记者获悉，上海公共租界工部局警务处正在组建一个特别部门，专门负责处理恐怖主义案件的调查工作。

警务处中最优秀的一些侦探将被指派到该特别部门，他们可能会于今早开始调查工作。

pages.en:
Parties Busy
In Settlement

Japanese Civilians With
Guns Search Trams,
Pedestrians

The International Settlement of
Shanghai was an armed camp last
night with police, units of the
Shanghai Volunteer Corps, and
patrols from the U. S. 4th Marines,
and the Seaforth Highlanders still
on the job at a late hour in the
downtown and western districts.
Units of Italian servicemen also
were active.

They were out to prevent another
outbreak of terrorism and, ap-
parently, their presence on the
street, and accompanying display of
armed force, had the desired effect.

On the bund unit of the Amer-
ican Company, S.V.C., the Russian
Regiment and Seaforth Highlanders
were kept on duty until a late hour.

Along side-streets running off the
Bund toward the west, Russian
Regiment and police units, as well
as S.V.C. armored cars kept up con-
stant patrols. In the American de-
fense sector, the leathernecks were
on the job most of the day and
most of the night.

And, south of Soochow Creek, the
appearance of Japanese in civilian
clothes armed with pistols, and
engaged in stopping pedestrians
and searching crowded tram-cars
and buses, added to the tension.

The Japanese search parties, with
no authorization to appear south
of the creek, caused the Settlement
authorities considerable concern.

In several instances, it was re-
ported last night, American Marines
turned back Japanese search parties
at the intersection of Yu Ya Ching
and Nanking Roads.

These search parties, however,
remained in the Central and Louza
districts for a good many hours
during the evening. In fact, there
were reports that some of them
were about after midnight this
morning.

On one occasion, an argument
developed between units of the
S.V.C. Armored Car Section and the
Japanese searching groups. Trucks
containing 34 Japanese, in civilian
dress, and armed with pistols, drove
along the Bund to the corner of
Avenue Edward VII.

Passersby Searched

Here, they stopped and commenc-
ed searching passersby as well as
trams and buses; searching people
who had just been searched by the
Shanghai Municipal Police. Later,
they left this area and proceeded
to the corner of Avenue Edward
VII and Kiangse Road.

At this point, they encountered
two S.V.C. armored cars. Officers in
command of this unit stopped the
Japanese and asked to see their
search warrants. The Japanese had
none but insisted that they intend-
ed to keep right on searching.

After some discussion, the Jap-
anese took their leave but instead
of returning to areas north of Soo-
chow Creek, proceeded into the
Louza District. It was reported
last night that they were turned
back along Nanking Road by the
American Marines.

Other search parties of a similar
nature filtered into areas south of
Soochow Creek, thereby increasing
the tension, which was at a high
pitch throughout the day.

Japanese military forces were ac-
tive along the Bund during the
morning following the bombings in
front of the Yokohama Specie Bank
and the Floating Restaurant. They
remained in that area a good part
of the day.

In the western district, around
the Japanese cotton mills, Japanese
forces also were in evidence.
pages.zh:
各方在租界内
忙碌不已

持枪日本平民
搜查电车及行人

昨晚，上海公共租界宛如一座武装营地，警察、上海万国商团（Shanghai Volunteer Corps）分队、美国海军陆战队第四团以及海福尔高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）的巡逻队，直至深夜仍在市中心和西区执勤。意大利军人分队也在积极活动。

他们的目的是防止恐怖主义再次爆发，显然，他们在街头的存在以及随之展示的武力，起到了预期的效果。

在外滩一带，美国连队、上海万国商团的俄罗斯团和海福尔高地团一直执勤至深夜。

在从外滩向西延伸的各条支路上，俄罗斯团和警察分队，以及上海万国商团的装甲车保持着持续的巡逻。在美国防区，海军陆战队士兵（leathernecks）在白天和夜间的大部分时间都在执勤。

此外，在苏州河以南，身穿便服、手持手枪的日本人的出现，以及他们拦截行人、搜查拥挤的电车和公共汽车的行为，加剧了紧张局势。

这些日本搜查小组无权出现在苏州河以南，这引起了租界当局的极大担忧。

据昨晚报道，在几起事件中，美国海军陆战队在虞洽卿路与南京路的交叉口拦回了日本搜查小组。

然而，这些搜查小组在晚间于中央区和老闸区停留了相当长的时间。事实上，有报告称，其中一些小组直到今天凌晨午夜过后仍在活动。

有一次，上海万国商团装甲车分队与日本搜查小组之间发生了争执。载有三十四名身穿便服、手持手枪的日本人的卡车，沿着外滩行驶至爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）转角处。

搜查路人

在此处，他们停下并开始搜查路人以及电车和公共汽车；甚至搜查刚刚被上海公共租界工部局警务处搜查过的人。随后，他们离开该区域，前往爱多亚路与江西路（Kiangse Road）的转角处。

在那里，他们遇到了两辆上海万国商团的装甲车。该部队指挥官拦下日本人，要求查看他们的搜查令。日本人没有搜查令，但坚持表示他们打算继续搜查。

经过一番讨论，日本人离开了，但他们没有返回苏州河以北的区域，而是进入了老闸区。昨晚有报告称，他们在南京路被美国海军陆战队拦回。

其他类似的搜查小组渗透到了苏州河以南的地区，从而加剧了全天都处于高度紧张状态的局势。

在横滨正金银行和浮水餐厅发生爆炸事件后的早晨，日本军队在外滩一带活动频繁。他们在该区域停留了大半天。

在西区，围绕日本棉纺厂一带，也有日本军队活动的迹象。

pages.en:
Two Japanese, Three
Chinese Killed As
Terrorists Run Wild

11 Bombings, 2 Shootings Greet 1st Anniversary
Of Outbreak Of Hostilities; Japanese, 1 Sikh,
7 Chinese Wounded In Series Of Incidents

POLICE AND MILITARY PATROLS KEEP
RIGID CONTROL FOLLOWING OUTBURST

Terror, in an unadulterated form, swept over the International
Settlement for a brief two hours yesterday morning and left this war-
shocked city with a severe case of jitters that lasted the rest of the
day and far into the night.
Bombings and shooting affairs, commencing at dawn, ushered in
the first anniversary of the China war.

Although the explosions of the
bombings and the smoke of the
shooting episodes had cleared away
by 7 a.m., no less than 13 incidents
in various sections of the city, from
the western district to the very
Bund itself, had occurred.
The official score last night was
11 bombings and two shootings.
Two Japanese civilians, both mill
workers, had been shot and killed
while on their way to work in the
western areas.
Two Japanese, reported to have
been sentries, stationed in Chapei,
across the boundary from North
Honan Road, were wounded.
Three Chinese, one pedestrian and
two alleged terrorists, were dead.
Seven Chinese were wounded.
One Sikh police watchman, a
Japanese cotton mill employee, was
the only foreign casualty reported
during the day.

**Outburst Stops Suddenly**
The outburst of enthusiasm, on
the part of the terrorist gangs,
stopped as suddenly as it started.
The last bomb was thrown at 7
a.m. and from that moment, until
late at night, no other episodes of
a similar nature had been reported
to the police.
The huge display of armed forces
presented during the day by the
Shanghai Municipal police, the
United States 4th Marines, the Sea-
forth Highlanders, the Russian
Regiment of the Shanghai Volun-
teer Corps, and various other Volun-
teer Corps units, including the
Armored Car Section and the
American Company, is believed to
have had a sobering effect on the
terrorists.
Police and military patrols func-
tioned throughout the city and
scores of buildings, alleyways and
literally thousands of pedestrians
were stopped and searched. Vari-
ous alleys and lanes that might be
used as avenues of escape by terror-
ist mobs, were barricaded with bar-
bed wire while several side streets
were closed to traffic.
After 7 a.m., the authorities were
taking no more chances of having
another outbreak of terror in the
city. And fortunately, the city re-
mained fairly quiet but confronted
with a situation that was decidedly
tense.
The wounded interpreter's name
last night was given as Hang Pao-
tsai. Fragments of the hand-
grenade has struck his right thigh.
Two other Chinese also were
wounded in the same incident. One
of these was a policeman of the
"Reformed Government of the
Shanghai Municipality," while the
other was a boatman.

**Reports Denied**
Reports circulated yesterday after-
noon to the effect that Japanese
sentries had shot two of the terror-
ists were denied by the Japanese
last night. The score for this in-
cident was three Chinese wounded.
Other bombing cases yesterday
including the throwing of a hand-
grenade in front of a Japanese
house at the corner of Macao and
Seymour Roads.
In the French Concession, no in-
cidents of any kind occurred during
the day although the police of that
area were constantly on the job. It
was reported last night that one
Chinese terrorist suspect was seized
on Rue du Consulat by French
police patrols. The man had a
hand-grenade in his possession, it
was stated.

**Anti-Nippon Leaflets**
Anti-Japanese leaflets were scat-
tered on Nanking Road and Rue
Montauban.
In Chapei, on Haining Road west
of Chekiang Road, one bomb was
thrown about 7 a.m. The target,
according to reports, was a Japanese
sentry post in Chapei and two
Japanese are said to have been
scratched.
Another bomb was thrown at the
North Station but did no damage.
Thirteen incidents, in just five
minutes less than two hours, was
the score for the morning. The
first one occurred at 5:05 a.m., one
hour after heavy police patrols had
started making their rounds. The
last of the 13 happened at 7 a.m.
sharp.
It was a big day for the police
and by 6 a.m., almost every avail-
able man was either on patrol duty
or engaged in investigation work.
Patrols of members of the Russian
Regiment of the Shanghai Volun-
teer Corps were on the job in the
Central and Louza districts as the
first streak of dawn made its ap-
pearance over the eastern horizon.
Seaforth Highlanders were called
out early and their patrols went to
work with the milkman. In the
American defense sector, patrols of
the United States 4th Marines also
were out with the dawn.
The International Settlement took
on a war-like appearance, and it
probably was due to this precaution
that the activities of terrorists yes-
terday morning ended before the
average man had left his home for
his place of business.

**Bombs In West Hongkew**
The first incident of the day was
perhaps one of the boldest. It oc-
curred in West Hongkew, at the
northern end of the Yu Ya Ching
Road Bridge, not far from the scene
where the Chinese "doomed battal-
lion" held out in the Joint Saving
Society Godown last October, four
days after other Chinese forces had
withdrawn from Chapei. The time
was 5:05 a.m.
Here, from the corner of Tibet
and Alabaster Roads, Chinese ter-
rorists, believed to be seven or eight
in number, heaved three bombs at
a Japanese Naval Landing Party
post just across the boundary line
in Chapei.
The bombs exploded but the sen-
try post escaped serious damage,
while none of the occupants were
hurt. Japanese bluejackets opened
fire on the bomb tossers, killing one
Chinese outright and wounding
three others. One of the wounded
Chinese died at the Lester Chinese
Hospital later in the day. The
other two were still alive last night
and are expected to live. If they
do live, they will either be prosecu-
ted for terroristic acts inside the
Settlement or handed over to the
Japanese authorities.

**Cotton Mills Bombed**
Just seven minutes after the
bombing near the Yu Ya Ching
Road Bridge, terrorists operating in
the western district, commenced
tossing hand-grenades, some "po-
tato-mashers," others of the "Mills"
type at Japanese owned cotton
mills.
Thrown at a Japanese naval sentry
post in Chapei. Two Chinese killed,
two wounded when Japanese sen-
tries opened fire.
5:12 a.m.—Two bombs thrown at
the Kung Dah Cotton Mill, Jess-
field Road, no casualties.
5:20 a.m.—Two bombs thrown at
the China-Japan Cotton Mill, 250
Penang Road, no casualties.
5:30 a.m.—One Japanese cotton
mill worker shot to death near
Robison and Ferry Roads.
5:30 a.m.—Three bombs thrown
into the staff quarters of the Nagai
Wata Kaisha Cotton Mill at Gordon
and Penang Roads. One Sikh
watchman wounded.
5:45 a.m.—One Japanese mill
worker, shot and killed, at the
corner of Markham and Tonquin
Roads. One ricsha coolie wounded.
6 a.m.—Two bombs thrown at
120 Jinkee Road.
6 a.m.—Two bombs, thrown at the
Yokohama Specie Bank, one Chi-
nese pedestrian dead, one wounded.
6 a.m.—One bomb thrown at the
Floating Restaurant off the Bund.
Three Chinese wounded.
6:10 a.m.—One bomb thrown at
the Szechuen Road bridge, no one
injured. Bomb failed to explode.
7 a.m.—One bomb thrown in
Chapei on Haining Road near
North Chekiang Road. Two Japan-
ese sentries reported slightly wound-
ed.
7 a.m.—One bomb thrown at the
North Station. No one injured.

（手写批注：Life）
pages.zh:
两名日本人、三名
中国人遇害，恐怖分子猖獗

敌对行动爆发一周年之际，发生11起爆炸案、2起枪击案；一系列事件中，一名日本人、一名锡克教徒、七名中国人受伤

暴乱发生后，警察与军队巡逻队实施严密管控

昨天上午，纯粹的恐怖活动在短短两小时内席卷公共租界，令这座饱受战争冲击的城市陷入严重的恐慌之中，这种紧张情绪持续了一整天并延续至深夜。
黎明时分开始的爆炸和枪击事件，迎来了中国战争（指中日战争）爆发的第一个周年纪念日。

尽管到早上7点时，爆炸的声响和枪击事件的硝烟已经消散，但在全市各个区域，从西区一直到外滩本身，已发生了不少于13起事件。
昨晚的官方统计数据显示，共有11起爆炸案和2起枪击案。
两名日本平民（均为纺织厂工人）在前往西区上班途中被枪杀。
据报道，两名驻守在闸北、位于河南北路边界对面的日本哨兵受伤。
三名中国人死亡，其中一人为路人，另两人为涉嫌恐怖分子。
七名中国人受伤。
一名锡克族警署更夫（系日本棉纺厂雇员）是当天报告的唯一外籍伤亡人员。

**暴乱突然停止**
恐怖团伙的狂热活动如同其开始时那样突然停止。
最后一枚炸弹投掷于早上7点，从那一刻起直到深夜，警方未再收到其他类似性质的事件报告。
白天，上海公共租界工部局警务处、美国海军陆战队第四团、海福斯高地兵团（Seaforth Highlanders）、上海万国商团俄国军团以及其他各类万国商团单位（包括装甲车分队和美国连）展示了庞大的武装力量，据信这对恐怖分子起到了震慑作用。
警察和军事巡逻队在全城范围内执行任务，数十座建筑物、弄堂以及成千上万的行人被拦截搜查。可能被恐怖暴徒用作逃生通道的各种弄堂和小巷被铁丝网封锁，几条支路则禁止交通通行。
早上7点后，当局不再冒险让城市再次发生恐怖暴乱。幸运的是，城市保持了相对平静，但面临的局势显然十分紧张。
昨晚公布的受伤翻译姓名为 Hang Pao-tsai（音译：杭宝才）。手榴弹碎片击中了他的右大腿。
另有两名中国人在同一事件中受伤。其中一人是“上海市政府改组政府”的一名警察，另一人是一名船夫。

**否认相关报道**
昨天下午流传着一种说法，称日本哨兵射杀了两名恐怖分子，但日方昨晚对此予以否认。该事件造成的后果是三名中国人受伤。
昨天的其他爆炸案件包括在澳门路与西摩路转角处的一栋日本房屋前投掷手榴弹。
在法租界，尽管该地区警察全天严阵以待，但白天未发生任何类型的事件。昨晚据报道，法国警察巡逻队在领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）抓获了一名中国恐怖嫌疑犯。据悉，该男子随身携带一枚手榴弹。

**反日传单**
南京路和蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）上散落着反日传单。
在闸北海宁路浙江路以西，约早上7点投掷了一枚炸弹。据报道，目标是闸北的一个日本哨所，据说两名日本人受轻伤。
另一枚炸弹被投向北站，但未造成损害。
在不到两小时的五分钟内，共发生了13起事件。第一起发生在凌晨5:05，即在大规模警察巡逻开始一小时后。第13起事件恰好发生在早上7点。
这对警方来说是忙碌的一天，到早上6点，几乎所有可用警力要么在执行巡逻任务，要么从事调查工作。
当第一缕曙光出现在东方地平线上时，上海万国商团俄国军团的巡逻队已在中央区和老闸区上岗执勤。
海福斯高地兵团早早被召集，其巡逻队随送奶工一同出动。在美国防区，美国海军陆战队第四团的巡逻队也在黎明时分出动。
公共租界呈现出战时景象，或许正是由于这种预防措施，昨天上午恐怖分子的活动在普通人离家去上班之前就结束了。

**虹口西区的炸弹**
当天的第一起事件可能是最大胆的一次。它发生在虹口西区，御驾桥（Yu Ya Ching Road）北端，距离去年10月中国“敢死队”在其他中国军队撤离闸北四天后坚守四行仓库（Joint Saving Society Godown）的地点不远。时间是凌晨5:05。
在此处，来自西藏路与阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）转角的七八名中国恐怖分子，向仅隔着边界线位于闸北的一个日本海军陆战队哨所投掷了三枚炸弹。
炸弹爆炸，但哨所未受严重损坏，内部人员无人受伤。日本水兵向投弹者开火，当场打死一名中国人，打伤另外三人。其中一名受伤的中国人在当天晚些时候死于莱斯忒华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。另外两人在昨晚仍存活，预计能够幸存。如果他们活下来，将因在租界内实施恐怖行为而被起诉，或被移交给日本当局。

**棉纺厂遭炸**
在御驾桥附近爆炸案发生仅七分钟后，在西区活动的恐怖分子开始向日本拥有的棉纺厂投掷手榴弹，有些是“土豆捣碎器”式（德制柄式手榴弹），有些是“米尔斯”式（英制米尔斯手榴弹）。
投掷在闸北的一个日本海军哨所。日本哨兵开火，两名中国人死亡，两人受伤。
5:12 a.m. — 两枚炸弹投掷在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的公大纱厂（Kung Dah Cotton Mill），无伤亡。
5:20 a.m. — 两枚炸弹投掷在彭南路250号的中日纱厂（China-Japan Cotton Mill），无伤亡。
5:30 a.m. — 一名日本棉纺厂工人在罗宾森路（Robison Road）和斐伦路（Ferry Road）附近被枪杀。
5:30 a.m. — 三枚炸弹投掷进戈登路（Gordon Road）和彭南路交界处的长崎棉业株式会社（Nagai Wata Kaisha）棉纺厂职员宿舍。一名锡克族更夫受伤。
5:45 a.m. — 一名日本工厂工人在马克姆路（Markham Road）和东京路（Tonquin Road）转角处被枪杀。一名人力车夫受伤。
6 a.m. — 两枚炸弹投掷在金利源路（Jinkee Road）120号。
6 a.m. — 两枚炸弹投掷在横滨正金银行（Yokohama Specie Bank），一名中国路人死亡，一人受伤。
6 a.m. — 一枚炸弹投掷在外滩附近的“浮游餐厅”。三名中国人受伤。
6:10 a.m. — 一枚炸弹投掷在四川路桥，无人受伤。炸弹未爆炸。
7 a.m. — 一枚炸弹投掷在闸北海宁路近浙江北路处。据报道两名日本哨兵受轻伤。
7 a.m. — 一枚炸弹投掷在北站。无人受伤。

（手写批注：Life）

pages.en:
FIRST of these bombings was
staged at 5:12 a.m. at the Kung
Dah Cotton Mill, on Jessfield Road.
Here two bombs were thrown and
both exploded. No casualties result-
ed, however, although one slight
damage was caused to the mill pre-
mises.
Next on the list of mill bombings
happened at 5:20 a.m. The scene
was the premises of the China-
Japan Cotton Mill at 250 Penang
Road. Here, two more hand-gre-
nades were thrown with no casual-
ties resulting and only minor dam-
age.

Japanese Civilian Killed

The first Japanese casualty of the
morning's activities was Kozaburo
Kano, an employee of the Nagai
Wata Kaisha No 1 Mill, located at
the corner of Gordon and Penang
Roads. Mr Kano was shot and
killed by unknown assailants while
walking along Robison Road, near
Ferry Road, on his way to work.
More than eight shots were fired
at Mr Kano from behind. Six of
the bullets struck him in the head
and back. He died immediately.
Japanese authorities took charge of
the body.
At almost the same moment that
Mr Kano was shot down, terrorists
hurled three bombs at the Nagai
Wata Kaisha No 1 Mill, causing
some damage to outbuildings, and
wounding a Sikh police watchman.
The watchman had just left his
bed and stepped outside his quar-
ters for a breath of fresh air when
a grenade came over the fence and
landed about 15 feet in front of
him. Flying splinters struck him
about the body. The man's condi-
tion however is not regarded as
being serious. He is now being
cared for at the police hospital and
is expected to be back on the job
in a few days.

Second Japanese Slain

The second Japanese to meet
death during the morning at the
hand of terrorists was Yasujiro
Shiraishi, an employee of the Na-
gai Wata Kaisha No. 9 Mill, locat-
ed on Gordon Road.
Shiraishi was riding in a ricksha,
on his way to work, when he was
shot down from behind. The hour
was 5:45 a.m. and the exact spot
where the killing occurred was the
intersection of Tonquin and Robi-
son Roads.
The man was struck in the head
by a single bullet from the killer's
gun. He was taken to the Foomin
Hospital on North Szechuen Road
by an emergency ambulance of the
Shanghai Fire Brigade and died on
the way. The killer made good his
escape.

Bombings On The Bund

From the western district, the
terrorists gave police headquarters
the jitters by moving into the
crowded business district along the
Bund. The first two bombs in this
zone were thrown in front of 120
Jinkee Road, not far from the offices
of the Shanghai Land Investment
Company, a British concern. No
one was injured. It was later as-
certained that the bombs were in-
tended for the offices of the Furu-
kawa Electric Company, on the
same street.
Within a matter of seconds after
the Jinkee Road affair, two hand-
grenades were tossed at the Yoko-
hama Specie Bank. One exploded,
one proved to be a dud. A Chin-
ese pedestrian was fatally wounded
and died before he could be moved
to a hospital. The man had not
been identified up to a late hour
last night. Another Chinese was
slightly wounded. Slight damage
was caused to the bank.
At almost the same time as the
bank bombing, terrorists tossed a
bomb onto the outside deck around
the former Chinese National
Government "Floating Restaurant"
and Ferry building, just off the
Peking Road Jetty. The place is
now being used as a Japanese
military police station. One police
interpreter, a Chinese, was slightly
wounded.
pages.zh:
第一次爆炸发生在凌晨5:12，地点是极司菲尔路的公大纱厂。此处投掷了两枚炸弹并均发生爆炸。然而，除厂房设施受到轻微损坏外，未造成人员伤亡。
接下来列表中的棉纺厂爆炸案发生在5:20。地点是彭南路250号的中日纱厂厂区。此处又投掷了两枚手榴弹，未造成伤亡，仅造成轻微损坏。

**日本平民遇害**

上午活动中的第一名日本伤亡者是加纳幸三郎（Kozaburo Kano），他是位于戈登路和彭南路转角的长崎棉业株式会社第一厂的雇员。加纳先生在前往上班途中，行至罗宾森路靠近斐伦路处时，被不明袭击者枪杀。
有人从背后向加纳先生开了八枪以上。六颗子弹击中他的头部和背部。他立即死亡。
日本当局接管了尸体。
就在加纳先生被枪倒下的几乎同一时刻，恐怖分子向长崎棉业株式会社第一厂投掷了三枚炸弹，造成附属建筑一些损坏，并致一名锡克族警署更夫受伤。
这名更夫刚起床，走出宿舍呼吸新鲜空气，此时一枚手榴弹越过围墙，落在他前方约15英尺处。飞溅的碎片击中他的身体。不过，该男子的状况被认为并不严重。他目前正在警署医院接受治疗，预计几天后可重返岗位。

**第二名日本人遇害**

上午在恐怖分子手中遇害的第二名日本人是白石安次郎（Yasujiro Shiraishi），他是位于戈登路的长崎棉业株式会社第九厂的雇员。
白石在乘坐人力车前往上班途中，从背后被枪击。时间是5:45，确切遇害地点是东京路与罗宾森路的交叉口。
凶手的一颗子弹击中了他的头部。他被上海救火会（Shanghai Fire Brigade）的急救救护车送往北四川路的福民医院（Foomin Hospital），途中死亡。凶手成功逃脱。

**外滩的爆炸案**

恐怖分子从西区转移到外滩拥挤的商业区，让警察总局感到紧张。该区域的前两枚炸弹投掷在金利源路120号门前，离英国企业上海地产投资公司（Shanghai Land Investment Company）的办公室不远。无人受伤。后来查明，炸弹的目标是同一条街道上的古河电气公司（Furukawa Electric Company）办公室。
在金利源路事件发生几秒后，两枚手榴弹被投掷向横滨正金银行。一枚爆炸，另一枚是哑弹。一名中国路人受致命伤，在被送往医院前死亡。直到昨晚很晚时候，该男子身份尚未确认。另一名中国人受轻伤。银行受到轻微损坏。
几乎在银行爆炸的同时，恐怖分子向原国民政府“浮游餐厅”及码头建筑（位于北京路码头附近）的外部甲板投掷了一枚炸弹。该地现被用作日本宪兵队驻地。一名中国籍警察翻译受轻伤。

pages.en:
Terrorism Breaks Loose On First
Anniversary Of July 7th Incident,
Exacting Big List Of Casualties

Two Japanese Killed; Indian
Watchman, Many Chinese Injured

Two Grenades Thrown At
Yokohama Specie Bank

Other Japanese Commercial
Concerns Also Bombed

Throwing a pall of gloom over the observance of the first anniversary of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, no less than 10 bombing and shooting incidents occurred within the Settlement this morning. Two Japanese were shot and killed an Indian watchman wounded, and several Chinese either killed or injured.

Most of the bombing and shooting incidents occurred between the hours of 5 and 6 this morning. Several subjects were held in custody by the police for investigation.

At 5.30 o'clock this morning, a bomb was tossed on Jinkee Road, in the vicinity of the Shanghai Land Investment Company, No. 110, but no one was injured. The windows of the company, however, were shattered. Following in the wake of the first bomb explosion, terrorist gangs shifted the scene of their activities to the Yokohama Specie Bank, where they threw two more bombs, killing the Chinese occupant of a ricksha, and wounding the puller and a boy pedestrian.

Two more bombs were thrown into the Floating Restaurant at the Bund, facing Peking Road, but by this time, the previous explosions had attracted considerable attention from Settlement police and Japanese consular police. The latter opened fire, killing two alleged bomb tossers, as they were fleeing from the scene.

Other sections of the International Settlement also had their share of the terrorist disturbances which occurred almost simultaneously.

The residential quarters for the staff of the Nalga Witta Kalsha, 881 Gordon Road, was also the scene of two bomb explosions followed by shooting. Naran Singh, the Indian watchman was in a lavatory when, unobserved by anyone within the compound, three or four men scaled the walls and immediately fired about five shots at the lavatory.

Three bullets pierced the door, two of them striking the back of Naran Sign's head and wounding him, although slightly. Two bombs were tossed first into the compound, both exploding, one of them shattering the windows of House No. 3, where a Mr. Kowa, staff member of the Cotton Mills was residing. Pa Singh, a friend of Naran Singh who had gone there to pass the night, hurriedly rose up after hearing the shots, but the men had already fled before he could catch a glimpse of them. Naran Singh told the Echo that he had no personal enemy, and neither had he had any quarrel with some other Indians.

Two other bombs, both failing to explode, were also thrown at the mills quarters of the N.W.K., at No. 250 Penang Road, near Robertson Road, a few minutes later. The neighbourhood was just beginning to hum with activities but none of the workers who were proceeding to work saw the bomb tosser or tossers.

Ambushed by four men, a Mr. Kobayashi, employee of the No. 9 Cotton Mills of the N. W. K. was shot and killed instantly while he was riding to office in his private ricksha licence No. 8750 along Markham Road about 5.30 a.m. today. The ricksha was held up, and the four assassins thrust their deadly weapons into his head, and within a split second, had done their job.

According to information gathered by police from the employees of a Chinese shop at 801, Markham Road, they said they heard a shot fired, the sound resembling that of a motor car tyre explosion. The next thing they remembered after hearing a succession of shots, was that they saw four men running away at a distance, but their backs were turned against them, and they could only say that two of the men were unshod. A rough description of the four men was also made to the police, who later found four blank cartridges in the vicinity of the shooting.

Another Japanese victim, K. Kano, age 48, and also employee of the N. W. K. cotton mills, was fatally shot by unknown assassin who fired twice at him while he was riding to work on a bicycle, about 5.20 o'clock this morning, and just as he as turning at the corner of Perry and Robertson Roads. The assassin or assassins fled and joined the large crowd of early factory workers.

The police also found a quantity of handbills scattered about the place. The handbills urged the Chinese public to "Fight to the bitter end," and reminded them that the "Final victory shall be ours."

Two other bombs were also tossed near the mills quarters of the N.W.K. at the corner of Macao and Seymour Roads about the same time, but only one of them exploded, without, however, injuring anyone. Quantities of handbills and posters were also found in the neighbourhood.

The Sih Ching Guild, on North Tibet Road, near Alabaster Road, was the scene of shooting by Japanese military sentries who fired at three alleged bomb tossers. Three bombs had exploded in the vicinity, whereupon, the Japanese stated, the Japanese sentries gave chase, and brought down three Chinese, killing two of them and wounding the other.

The Kung Dah Cotton Mills on Jessfield Road was also the scene of two bomb explosions about the same time, but no one was injured or killed.

Anticipating a resurgence of terrorist activities today, Settlement and Concession police made preparations yesterday to keep a strict watch over their areas. Squads of search parties were sent out last night and this morning, and suspicious pedestrians were being carefully searched. Japanese consular police were also detailed to work in co-operation with the Settlement police.

Following the series of shootings and bombings, Settlement police threw a cordon around the scenes of terrorist activities, and Jinkee Road, Nanking Road, and other parts of the Settlement were placed under martial law.

（批：Fic 2/7）
pages.zh:
七七事变一周年之际恐怖活动猖獗，
造成重大伤亡

两名日本人被杀；一名印度巡夜人受伤，
多名中国人受伤

两颗手榴弹掷向
横滨正金银行

其他日本商号亦遭炸弹袭击

在今晨纪念中日敌对行动一周年之际，笼罩在一片阴郁气氛中的是，租界内发生了不下10起爆炸和枪击事件。两名日本人被枪杀，一名印度巡夜人受伤，数名中国人死伤。

大多数爆炸和枪击事件发生在今晨5时至6时之间。警方拘留了数名嫌疑人以供调查。

今晨5时30分，一颗炸弹被掷于静安寺路（Jinkee Road）上海业广地产公司（Shanghai Land Investment Company）110号附近，无人受伤。但该公司的窗户被震碎。继第一颗炸弹爆炸之后，恐怖团伙将活动场景转移至横滨正金银行（Yokohama Specie Bank），在那里又投掷了两颗炸弹，炸死一名黄包车上的中国乘客，并炸伤车夫和一名男童行人。

另有两颗炸弹被掷入外滩面对北京路的浮游餐厅（Floating Restaurant），但此时之前的爆炸已引起租界巡捕和日本领事馆警察的极大关注。后者开火射击，击毙两名据称正在逃离现场的投弹者。

国际租界的其他区域也几乎同时遭受了恐怖骚乱的波及。

戈登路（Gordon Road）881号日华纺织株式会社（Nalga Witta Kalsha，音译：Nagai Wata Kaisha）职员宿舍区也发生了两起炸弹爆炸及随后的枪击事件。印度巡夜人纳兰·辛格（Naran Singh）当时正在厕所内，compound（大院）内无人察觉，三四名男子翻墙而入，立即向厕所开了约五枪。

三颗子弹穿透门板，其中两颗击中纳兰·辛格的后脑，致其轻伤。两颗炸弹先被掷入大院内，均发生爆炸，其中一颗震碎了3号房屋的窗户，居住在该处的是棉纺厂职员科瓦先生（Mr. Kowa）。纳兰·辛格的朋友帕·辛格（Pa Singh）此前去那里过夜，听到枪声后急忙起身，但在他瞥见那些人之前，他们已逃之夭夭。纳兰·辛格告诉《回声报》（Echo），他个人没有仇敌，也未与其他印度人发生过争执。

几分钟后，在靠近罗伯逊路（Robertson Road）的槟榔路（Penang Road）250号，日华纺织株式会社（N.W.K.）的工厂宿舍区也被投掷了另外两颗炸弹，均未爆炸。附近刚刚开始热闹起来，但前往上班的工人中无人看到投弹者。

今晨约5时30分，日华纺织株式会社（N. W. K.）第九棉纺厂雇员小林先生（Mr. Kobayashi）乘坐私人黄包车（牌照号8750）沿马克姆路（Markham Road）前往办公室途中，遭到四人伏击，当场被枪杀。黄包车被拦下，四名刺客将致命武器刺入其头部，瞬间完成了刺杀。

据警方从马克姆路801号一家中国店铺雇员处收集的信息称，他们听到一声枪响，声音类似汽车轮胎爆裂。在听到一连串枪声后，他们记得看到的下一件事是远处有四名男子逃跑，但背对着他们，只能说出其中两人未穿鞋。警方还获得了这四人的粗略描述，随后在枪击现场附近发现了四枚空弹壳。

另一名日本受害者，48岁的加野（K. Kano，音译），也是日华纺织株式会社棉纺厂的雇员，今晨约5时20分骑自行车上班途中，在佩里路（Perry Road）和罗伯逊路拐角处转弯时，被不明身份的刺客连开两枪致死。刺客随即逃离，混入早班工厂工人的庞大人群中。

警方还在现场周围发现大量传单。传单敦促中国公众“战斗到底”，并提醒他们“最后胜利属于我们”。

大约在同一时间，澳门路（Macao Road）和西摩路（Seymour Roads）拐角处的日华纺织株式会社工厂宿舍附近也被投掷了另外两颗炸弹，但只有一颗爆炸，且未造成人员伤亡。附近也发现了大量传单和海报。

位于北西藏路（North Tibet Road）靠近阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）的四明公所（Sih Ching Guild）发生了日本军事哨兵向三名疑似投弹者开枪的事件。据日本人称，附近发生了三起炸弹爆炸，随后日本哨兵展开追捕，击倒三名中国人，其中两人死亡，一人受伤。

杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）的公大纱厂（Kung Dah Cotton Mills）大约在同一时间也发生了两起炸弹爆炸，但无人伤亡。

鉴于预计今天恐怖活动会死灰复燃，租界和法租界警方昨天已做好准备，对其辖区进行严密监视。昨晚和今晨派出了多支搜查队，并对可疑行人进行了仔细搜身。日本领事馆警察也被指派与租界巡捕合作。

在这一系列枪击和爆炸事件发生后，租界巡捕在恐怖活动地点周围设置了警戒线，静安寺路、南京路及租界其他地区实行戒严。

（批注：Fic 2/7）

BOMB THROWERS
CREATE INTENSE
REIGN OF TERROR

Two Japanese Killed, Several Chinese Shot
In Many Incidents; Nippon Soldiers
Open Fire; 15 Missiles Thrown

TROOPS PATROLLING STREETS

Chinese bomb-throwers staged a brief but intense reign
of terror in the International Settlement today as part of
the observance of the first anniversary of the start of
hostilities July 7. 1937. at Lukiaochao. ne. Peiping. About
15 bombs were thrown between 5 and 6 a.m. in widely
separated areas of the Settlement, and between these bombs
and shots fired by Japanese troops
and Chinese assassins, several are
dead or wounded.
In a growing crescendo, the
blasts of exploding hand-grenades
and guns provided a grim over-
ture for the anniversary. Two
Japanese were killed, and several
Chinese were shot. Among the
wounded was a Japanese military
police interpreter and a Sikh
watchman of a Japanese cotton
mill.

**Japanese Fire**
The opening burst occurred at
5.05 a.m. at the corner of North
Tibet and Alabaster Roads, when
Japanese sentries opened fire on
a gang of Chinese, killing two and
wounding two. The victims were
sent to the Lester Hospital. The
sentries alleged that the men had
thrown three dud bombs at them
prior to the shooting.
A few minutes later two bombs
were thrown at the Kung Dah
Cotton Mill on Jessfield Road.
This mill is Japanese owned. The
gate was smashed and many
windows broken. There were no
casualties.

**Another Mill Bombed**
Eight minutes after this, two
bombs were thrown at the China-
Japan Cotton Mill staff quarters
(Japanese owned) at 250 Penang
Road. Damage was slight and
there were no casualties.
One minute later Kozaburo
Kano, employee of the No. 1 mill
of the Nagai Wata Kaisha, was
shot and killed by an unidentified
Chinese at Robison and Ferry
Roads while he was walking to
work. Six bullets hit his
head and body from be-
hind, killing him instantly.

**Watchman Hit**
At 5.30 a.m. three bombs were
thrown at the Nagai Wata Kaisha
Mill at Gordon and Penang Roads.
An Indian watchman at the gate
was wounded in the hand and
taken to the Country Hospital.
Fifteen minutes later Yasujiro
Shiraishi, another employee of the
Nagai Wata Kaisha, working at
the No. 9 mill on Gordon Road,
was shot at from behind while
riding in a ricsha at Markham
and Tonkin Roads, and died later
in the Foomin Hospital on North
Szechuen Road. Two Chinese
gunmen made the attack, firing
four shots. His ricsha coolie was
reportedly wounded and also taken
to the Foomin Hospital.

**Bund Bombed**
Several attacks were made about
6 a.m. At 120 Jinkee Road in
the Central District, a grenade
was thrown near the compound
of the Shanghai Land Investment
building. A window was broken
by the missile.

Next two bombs were tossed at
the premises of the Yokohama,
Specie Bank on the Bund. A
Japanese report stated that the
bombs exploded, damaging the
building and fatally wounding an
unidentified Chinese. Police re-
ports did not confirm this, stating
that both bombs were duds.

**Bomb At Ferry**
Then a grenade exploded at
the former City Government Ferry
Restaurant Jetty at Peking Road
and the Bund, now used as a
Japanese Military Water Police
headquarters. Japanese reported
one Japanese military police inter-
preter slightly injured. One un-
named suspect, described as a
motor truck driver, was detained
at the Jetty; a grenade was
allegedly found in the truck.
Japanese sentries opened fire,
killing a Chinese of the coolie
type and wounding another, who
is at the Lester Hospital.
Almost simultaneously a Chin-
ese threw a bomb at two Japanese
sentries on the Szechuen Road
bridge. It did not explode.

**Bombings In Chapei**
Five minutes later a grenade
was tossed at a house near the
corner of Macao and Seymour
Roads. It is understood the house
is occupied by a Japanese official.
Damage was slight.
Two other bombings occurred
about an hour later in Chapel,
outside SMP jurisdiction. Two
Japanese sentries were allegedly
wounded on Haining Road west
of North Tibet Road by a bomb
tossed near the Wusih Guild in
Chinese territory. Another bomb
allegedly exploded in Chapei
about the same time near the
North Tibet Road boundary.
The bombings ceased in the
Settlement about 6 o'clock, and
further attacks had not been re-
ported up to press time.

**Troops to Mills**
Japanese troops were rushed by
truck to various Japanese mills
in the Western District after the
attacks, giving rise to wild rumors
for a time that the area was be-
ing taken over. The troops gar-
risoned the compounds for pro-
tection in Pootoo Road, Gordon
Road, Bubbling Well Road and
other district police station areas.
The Bund from the former
ferry to Nanking Road was very
tense for a period. Japanese
troops being rushed to the area
despite the presence of a large
number of Settlement police,
Russian Regiment men, Volun-
teers, and Highlanders. The area

BOMBS AND
BULLETS

The following attacks oc-
curred in the Settlement this
morning:
5.05 a.m.: At North Tibet
and Alabaster Roads,
West Hongkew, three
bombs thrown at Ja-
panese sentries, who
fired on the Chinese
tossers, killing two,
wounding two.
5.12 a.m.: At the Kung Dah
Cotton Mill, Jessfield
Road, two bombs
thrown, no casualties.
5.20 a.m.: At 250 Penang
Road, the China-Japan
Cotton Mill, two bombs
thrown, no casualties.
5.21 a.m.: At Robison and
Ferry Roads, one Ja-
panese killed by shots.
5.30 a.m.: At Gordon and
Penang Roads, the
Nagai Wata Kaisha
Mill, three bombs
thrown, one Indian
wounded.
5.45 a.m.: At Markham and
Tonkin Road, one Ja-
panese killed by shots,
one ricshaman wound-
ed.
6 a.m.: At 120 Jinkee Road,
one bomb thrown.
6 a.m.: At the Yokohama
Specie Bank on the
Bund, two bombs
thrown, both duds.
6 a.m.: At the former
Government Ferry on
the Bund, one bomb
thrown, one Chinese
killed, one wounded by
Japanese sentries, one
Japanese wounded.
6 a.m.: At the Szechuen
Road Bridge, one bomb
thrown, unexploded.
6.05 a.m.: At Macao and
Seymour Roads, one
bomb thrown.
7 a.m.: In Chapei on Hain-
ing Road west of North
Chekiang Road, one
bomb thrown, two Ja-
panese wounded.
7 a.m.: In Chapei near
North Tibet Road, one
bomb thrown.

投弹者制造
极度恐怖统治

两名日本人被杀，多起事件中数名中国人中枪；
日军开火；投掷15枚爆炸物

军队巡逻街道

今日，作为纪念1937年7月7日北平附近卢沟桥爆发敌对行动一周年活动的一部分，中国投弹者在国际租界上演了一场短暂但激烈的恐怖统治。清晨5时至6时之间，租界各分散区域共投掷了约15颗炸弹，在这些炸弹以及日军和中国刺客发射的枪弹之间，数人死亡或受伤。

随着手榴弹爆炸声和枪声逐渐增强，为这一周年纪念奏响了严峻的序曲。两名日本人被杀，数名中国人中枪。伤者中包括一名日本宪兵翻译和一名日本棉纺厂的锡克教巡夜人。

**日军开火**
第一波爆发发生在凌晨5时05分，地点在北西藏路和阿拉巴斯特路拐角处，当时日本哨兵向一伙中国人开火，击毙两人，击伤两人。受害者被送往雷士德医院（Lester Hospital）。哨兵称，在开枪前，这些人曾向他们投掷了三颗哑弹。

几分钟后，两颗炸弹被掷向杰斯菲尔德路的公大纱厂。该厂为日资。大门被砸坏，许多窗户破碎。无人员伤亡。

**另一家纱厂遭炸**
八分钟后，两颗炸弹被掷向槟榔路250号的中日纺织厂（China-Japan Cotton Mill，日资）职员宿舍。损失轻微，无人员伤亡。

一分钟后，长崎棉业会社（Nagai Wata Kaisha，音译）第一厂雇员鹿子郎·加野（Kozaburo Kano，音译）在罗伯逊路（Robison Road）和费里路（Ferry Road）步行上班途中，被一名身份不明的中国人枪杀。六颗子弹从背后击中其头部和身体，当场死亡。

**巡夜人中弹**
上午5时30分，三颗炸弹被掷向戈登路和槟榔路交叉口的长崎棉业会社工厂。门口的一名印度巡夜人手部受伤，被送往乡村医院（Country Hospital）。

十五分钟后，长崎棉业会社另一名雇员白石康次郎（Yasujiro Shiraishi，音译），在戈登路第九厂工作，乘坐黄包车经过马克姆路和东京路（Tonkin Roads）时从背后遭到枪击，后死于北四川路的福民医院（Foomin Hospital）。两名中国枪手发动了袭击，开了四枪。据报道，他的黄包车夫也受伤，并被送往福民医院。

**外滩遭炸**
上午6点左右发生了几起袭击。在中央区静安寺路120号，一颗手榴弹被掷在上海业广地产大楼的大院附近。一枚投射物打破了一扇窗户。

接着，两颗炸弹被掷向外滩的横滨正金银行 premises。一份日本报告称，炸弹爆炸，损坏了建筑物，并致使一名身份不明的中国人受致命伤。警方报告未证实这一点，称两颗炸弹均为哑弹。

**费里码头炸弹**
随后，一颗手榴弹在北京路和外滩的前市政府轮渡餐厅码头爆炸，该地现用作日本海军陆战队（Military Water Police）总部。日方报告称，一名日本宪兵翻译受轻伤。一名未具名的嫌疑人，据描述为卡车司机，在码头被拘留；据称在卡车内发现了一颗手榴弹。日本哨兵开火，击毙一名苦力类型的中国人，并击伤另一人，后者目前在雷士德医院。

几乎与此同时，一名中国人在四川路桥上向两名日本哨兵投掷了一颗炸弹。炸弹未爆炸。

**闸北的爆炸案**
五分钟后，一颗手榴弹被掷向澳门路和西摩路拐角附近的一所房屋。据悉该房屋由一名日本官员居住。损失轻微。

大约一小时后，在工部局管辖范围之外的闸北（Chapel，原文误植，应为Chapei）发生了另外两起爆炸案。据称，在中国领土无锡公所（Wusih Guild）附近投掷的一颗炸弹，炸伤了北西藏路以西海宁路上的两名日本哨兵。另一颗炸弹据称大约在同一时间在闸北靠近北西藏路边界处爆炸。

租界内的爆炸案在6点左右停止，截至发稿时未报告进一步的袭击。

**军队进驻纱厂**

袭击发生后，日军乘卡车迅速赶往西区各家日本纱厂，一时间引发了该地区被接管的疯狂谣言。部队驻守在大院内进行保护，涉及普陀路（Pootoo Road）、戈登路、静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）及其他各区警署区域。

从前轮渡到南京路的外滩区域在一段时间内气氛非常紧张。尽管有大量租界巡捕、俄国团士兵、万国商团志愿者和高地兵团成员在场，日军仍被紧急调往该区域。该区域

炸弹与
子弹

今晨租界内发生的袭击如下：
上午5:05：在西虹口北西藏路和阿拉巴斯特路，向日本哨兵投掷三颗炸弹，哨兵向中国投弹者开火，击毙两人，击伤两人。
上午5:12：在杰斯菲尔德路公大纱厂，投掷两颗炸弹，无伤亡。
上午5:20：在槟榔路250号中日纺织厂，投掷两颗炸弹，无伤亡。
上午5:21：在罗伯逊路和费里路，一名日本人被枪杀。
上午5:30：在戈登路和槟榔路长崎棉业会社工厂，投掷三颗炸弹，一名印度人受伤。
上午5:45：在马克姆路和东京路，一名日本人被枪杀，一名黄包车夫受伤。
上午6:00：在静安寺路120号，投掷一颗炸弹。
上午6:00：在外滩横滨正金银行，投掷两颗炸弹，均为哑弹。
上午6:00：在外滩前政府轮渡码头，投掷一颗炸弹，一名中国人被日本哨兵击毙，一人受伤，一名日本人受伤。
上午6:00：在四川路桥，投掷一颗炸弹，未爆炸。
上午6:05：在澳门路和西摩路，投掷一颗炸弹。
上午7:00：在闸北海宁路（北浙江路以西），投掷一颗炸弹，两名日本人受伤。
上午7:00：在闸北靠近北西藏路处，投掷一颗炸弹。

pages.en:
was cordoned off for a time, giv-
ing the Bund and lower Nanking
Road the appearance of being
under martial law. The SMP Re-
serve Unit was rushed from one
section of the Settlement to an-
other constantly for about two
hours as reports of further at-
tacks poured in.

**Attack On Bridge**
Two of the boldest bombing at-
tempts were those carried out at
the North Szechuen Road Bridge
and near the Joint Savings Bank
Godown, scene of the stand of
the Chinese "Lost Battalion" last
October.

One hand-grenade was tossed
at the Japanese Naval Landing
Party sentry box on North Sze-
chuen Road Bridge, but failed to
explode. One terrorist suspect
was seized.

**One Shot**
Three hand-grenades were
thrown by as many Chinese at a
Japanese Naval Landing Party
post near the Joint Savings Bank
godown. All went wide of their
mark, but the fire of Japanese
bluejackets downed one of the
men.

The two others fled into the
International Settlement across
Yu Ya Ching Road Bridge.
through which they had ap-
parently gained access to Chapel.
The body of the slain Chinese
was removed by the Japanese
naval authorities.

**Grenade At Station**
One unidentified person tossed
a hand-grenade at the North
Station, allegedly from Boundary
Road in the International Settle-
ment. No casualties were caused.
Comparatively few arrests have
been made today, however. The
French Concession was almost
entirely quiet, no outrages occur-
ring within its boundaries,
though French Police were on the
alert. They arrested one pedes-
trian carrying a hand-grenade.
He told police he was taking it
into the Settlement with the in-
tention of throwing it at Japan-
ese sentries.

**Bund Guarded**
The Bund seemed on a war-
time basis, due to the presence
of many police and troops. The
French Bund was very closely
guarded by armed patrols wear-
ing bullet-proof vests, and there
was plenty of barbed wire and
armored cars in the vicinity.
Special precautions were also
taken in Pootung today. Several
guerillas were reportedly arrested
with Mausers at the ferry land-
ings during the morning. For the
first time since the start of hostili-
ties Chinese police in Pootung
were being armed by the Japanese
with rifles, some 500 being re-
portedly distributed.

**Many Flags**
One enterprising foreigners rid-
ing up Nanking Road counted 148
Kuomintang flags flying between
Szechuen and Yu Ya Ching Roads
in honor of the day.
A persistent report that two
Russians had been shot in the
Gordon Road district this morn-
ing was denied by police.

**City Tense**
All Shanghai was tensely aware
of the significance of this first
anniversary of the Sino-Japanese
undeclared war today, marking 12
months since the outbreak of
fighting at Lukouchiao. The war
has cut a wide swath across
China and brought much devasta-
tion and death, not only to
Shanghai but to almost one-third
of the nation. Property destruc-
tion has been estimated at be-
tween US$350,000,000, and US$1,-
000,000,000.
Memorial services were being
held today throughout China and
Japan for soldiers and civilians
killed in the hostilities. Here
Chinese national flags were much
in evidence and public organiza-
tions were holding memorial
meetings, a joint meet being
staged by delegates of various
local bodies. Amusements and
social functions in the Chinese
community were generally sus-
pended, and many Chinese were
on a vegetarian diet. Chinese had
been asked to observe a three-
minute silence at noon, and
though many thoughtful residents
did observe it, the period was by
no means noticeable in downtown
Shanghai.

**Manifesto Issued**
A manifesto has been issued to
Chinese here emphasizing the
struggle to preserve China's
sovereignty and territorial in-
tegrity, and paying high tribute
to the Chinese troops. Confidence
is expressed that the victory will
ultimately be China's. The mes-
sage asks for donations to the
government war chest and it
urges the people to continue to
rid the city of "traitors".
Various Chinese government
leaders, including General Chiang
Kai-shek, have issued statements
in connection with this anniver-
sary. The Japanese have also is-
sued statements. This morning
General Shunroku Hata, com-
mander in chief of the Japanese
Expeditionary Forces in Central
China, broadcast over the Greater
Shanghai Broadcasting Station
emphasizing the necessity of
"nationwide cooperation of
soldiers and civilians for the at-
tainment of the great objective
of this country." He stated that
in the past year the Japanese
have captured China's capital,
won a victory at Hsuchow, and
now control a "greater half of the
political, economic, traffic, indus-
trial and communication interests
of China." He said that the peo-
ple have supported the army and
the army morale is high. "Of
course," he said, "there may be
some difficulties ahead because of
the peculiarities of Central China,
but we shall put forth our best
efforts . . ."

**Japanese Meet**
At 11 a.m. the Japanese Re-
sidents Corporation met at the
Japanese Club on Bo'ne Road to
mark the anniversary. A one-
minute silence was observed and
services were then held at the
shrine for the war dead. Services
were also held in Buddhist temples
while private Japanese families
contributed funds. Japanese also
ate "one-dish meals" to contribute
money to a national defense fund.
Posters were stuck up in Hong-
kew emphasizing this part of the
program.
A Japanese source has declared
that "secret orders" had been is-
sued by the Chinese authorities
in Hankow "for a nationwide
terroristic campaign, with Shang-
hai as the principal locale of
operations," and added that "all
organs concerned" had been
directed to carry out a series of
"dire plots" in Japanese-occupied
districts throughout China.

**Police On Alert**
For several days the police of
the International Settlement and
French Concession were making
plans to guard against an out-
break of terrorism today. Special
police patrols in the Central and
Louza districts were on duty at 4
a.m. today and search parties
were busy all day yesterday and
up to midnight, beginning again
at dawn this morning. Downtown
Shanghai was very much aware
of the tension due to the pre-
sence on all streets of heavily
reinforced patrols of the Russian
Regiment and Shanghai Volun-
teers. Detachments of the Sea-
forth Highlanders were patrolling
Nanking Road and special patrols
were kept in readiness for
emergencies. Especial care was
taken in the Louza District and
along the Bund, particularly at
Garden Bridge and Soochow Creek
bridges. West Hongkew was
heavily patrolled, the Reserve Unit
was constantly on the alert, and
steel-vested police squads awaited
at all stations for the alarm
signal. This was true at most
stations in the Settlement,
particularly Central, Louza, Bub-
bling Well, West Hongkew and
Hongkew.
In the French Concession the
same precautions were taken to-
day. Police were carefully search-
ing pedestrians along all bound-
aries. French patrols were in-
creased. French military units
were standing by, and armored
cars patrolled the main thorough-
fares. The Settlement boundary
and the French Bund were
specially guarded. Riot squads
were held ready at all French
police posts. Throughout the city
plainclothes squads were standing
by.

**Five Shootings**
There have been up to this
morning five political shootings
here in 19 days, since the killing
of Jen Pao-an, "Reformed Gov-
ernment" official. Seven have
been killed and 12 wounded in
these attacks, and there have been
two gang slayings in addition. A
police record has been set, with
the Louza District as the focal
point. This reign of terror was
expected to reach a crisis today.
In Hongkew, Japanese naval
and military patrols were very
much on the alert, as well as in
Nantao, Pootung and the western
outside roads areas. This morn-
ing many residents were alarmed
by the sound of machine gun fire
but it was ascertained that this
came from the French Rifle
Range, where troops were practic-
ing.
Chinese reports today said that
a large number of guerillas had
appeared in the outer reaches of
the Kiangwan area last night and
that the Japanese army planes
had been busy over the area.
These reports also said that there
had been fighting for the last 48
hours near the city.
pages.zh:
该区域一度被封锁，使得外滩和南京路下段呈现出戒严的景象。约两小时内，随着进一步袭击的报告不断涌入，上海公共租界工部局警务处（SMP）后备队被频繁地从租界的一个区域调往另一个区域。

**袭击桥梁**
两次最大胆的炸弹袭击企图分别发生在北四川路桥以及联合储蓄银行仓库附近，后者是去年十月中国“孤军营”坚守阵地的地点。

一枚手榴弹被扔向北四川路桥上的日本海军陆战队哨亭，但未爆炸。一名恐怖嫌疑分子被抓获。

**开了一枪**
三名中国人向联合储蓄银行仓库附近的日本海军陆战队哨所投掷了三枚手榴弹。所有手榴弹均未击中目标，但日本水兵的火力击倒其中一人。

另外两人逃入国际租界，穿过虞洽卿路桥，他们显然是通过该桥进入教堂区域的。被杀中国人的尸体由日本海军当局移走。

**车站的手榴弹**
一名身份不明的人据称从国际租界的界路向北火车站投掷了一枚手榴弹。未造成伤亡。然而，今天被捕的人数相对较少。法租界几乎完全平静，其境内未发生暴行，尽管法国警察处于警戒状态。他们逮捕了一名携带手榴弹的行人。他告诉警察，他正打算将手榴弹带入租界，意图投向日本哨兵。

**外滩戒备**
由于大量警察和军队驻守，外滩似乎处于战时状态。法外滩由身穿防弹背心的武装巡逻队严密把守，附近部署了大量铁丝网和装甲车。今天浦东也采取了特别预防措施。据报道，上午在渡口码头逮捕了几名携带毛瑟枪的游击队员。自敌对行动开始以来，浦东的中国警察首次由日本人配备步枪，据报道分发了约500支。

**许多旗帜**
一位富有进取心的外国人在南京路上乘车时，数出在四川路和虞洽卿路之间悬挂了148面国民党旗帜，以纪念这一天。
警方否认了今晨戈登路地区有两名俄罗斯人被枪击的持续传言。

**城市紧张**
全上海都紧张地意识到今天是中日不宣而战的第一周年纪念日，标志着卢沟桥事变爆发已过去12个月。战争在中国大片土地上肆虐，不仅给上海，也给全国近三分之一的地区带来了巨大的破坏和死亡。财产损失估计在3.5亿美元至10亿美元之间。
今天，中国和日本各地都在为在敌对行动中丧生的士兵和平民举行追悼活动。在此地，中国国旗随处可见，公共组织正在举行追悼会，各地方团体的代表联合举办了一场会议。华人社区的娱乐和社交活动普遍暂停，许多中国人吃素。华人被要求在中午默哀三分钟，虽然许多深思熟虑的居民确实遵守了这一要求，但在上海市中心，这一时段并不明显。

**发表宣言**
向在沪华人发布了一份宣言，强调为维护中国主权和领土完整而斗争，并向中国军队致以崇高敬意。宣言表示相信胜利最终将属于中国。文告呼吁向政府战争基金捐款，并敦促人民继续清除城市中的“汉奸”。
包括蒋介石将军在内的各位中国政府领导人都就这一周年纪念日发表了声明。日本人也发表了声明。今天上午，华中日军派遣军总司令畑俊六将军在上海大广播电台广播，强调“军民 nationwide cooperation（全国合作）以实现本国伟大目标”的必要性。他表示，在过去一年中，日军攻占了中国首都，在徐州取得胜利，现在控制着“中国政治、经济、交通、工业和通信利益的大半部分”。他说，人民支持军队，军队士气高昂。他说：“当然，由于华中的特殊性，前方可能会有一些困难，但我们将尽最大努力……”

**日本人集会**
上午11时，日本居留民团在波恩路日本俱乐部集会纪念周年纪念日。全体默哀一分钟，随后在靖国神社（原文为shrine，指代供奉战死者之处）举行祭奠战死者的仪式。佛教寺庙也举行了仪式，日本私人家庭捐献了资金。日本人还吃“一菜餐”以为国防基金筹款。虹口张贴了强调该计划这一部分的海报。
一位日本消息人士宣称，汉口中国当局已发出“秘密命令”，开展“以上海为主要行动地点的全国性恐怖运动”，并补充说，“所有有关机构”已受命在中国各地的日占区实施一系列“可怕阴谋”。

**警察警戒**
几天来，国际租界和法租界的警察一直在制定计划，以防今天爆发恐怖主义活动。中央区和老闸区的特别警察巡逻队于今天凌晨4点上岗，搜查队昨天全天忙碌直至午夜，并于今天黎明再次开始工作。由于俄罗斯团和上海义勇队的重兵巡逻队出现在所有街道上，上海市中心非常清楚地感受到了紧张气氛。海福尔高地人团（Seaforth Highlanders）的分遣队在南京路巡逻，特别巡逻队随时待命以应对紧急情况。老闸区和沿外滩，特别是花园桥和苏州河桥梁，受到了特别关照。西虹口地区巡逻密集，后备队始终保持警戒，穿防弹背心的警察小队在各警局等待警报信号。租界内大多数警局都是如此，特别是中央、老闸、静安寺、西虹口和虹口警局。
今天在法租界也采取了同样的预防措施。警察在所有边界仔细搜查行人。增加了法国巡逻队。法国军事单位待命，装甲车在主要干道巡逻。租界边界和法外滩受到特别警卫。所有法国警察岗哨都备有防暴队。全市便衣队随时待命。

**五起枪击案**
自“维新政府”官员任葆安被杀以来，截至今天上午的19天内，此地已发生五起政治枪击案。在这些袭击中，7人死亡，12人受伤，此外还有两起帮派谋杀案。创下了警察记录，以老闸区为焦点。预计这种恐怖统治今天将达到危机时刻。
在虹口，日本海军和军事巡逻队高度警戒，南市、浦东和西部越界筑路地区也是如此。今天上午，许多居民被机枪声惊醒，但经查明，声音来自法国步枪射击场，当时部队正在那里进行演习。
今天的中文报道称，昨晚大量游击队员出现在江湾地区的外围，日本军用飞机在该地区上空频繁活动。这些报道还称，过去48小时在城市附近发生了战斗。

pages.en:
Local Police
Take Rigid
Steps Today

Extra Patrols To Curb
Possible Terrorist
Activities

Fearing an outbreak of trouble, involving bombings, assassinations and other terroristic activities today—the first anniversary of the present war in China—police of both the International Settlement and the French Concession were last night taking precautionary measures, intended to check or prevent incidents involving crime.

Special police patrols for both the Central and Louza Districts have been assigned to commence work at 4 a.m. today. Search parties, functioning throughout the day yesterday, were kept on the job until midnight. They were also scheduled to resume their work at dawn this morning.

In addition to the police patrols it is understood that the Russian Regiment of the Shanghai Volunteer Corps will be kept under stand-by orders throughout the day, prepared for any emergency. Detachments of the Seaforth Highlanders will carry out their patrols along Nanking Road as usual, but it is reported that special patrols of these men will be kept in readiness for emergency duty.

If trouble does occur today, the police are inclined to believe that it will most likely be centered in either the department store district on Nanking Road, or in the Central District along Foochow Road. While the authorities are making no predictions as to what might happen, they are definitely taking no chances and practically every officer, plain-clothes, or uniformed, will get a session of extra duty.

In view of the increase of the number of assassinations occurring in the Settlement during the past few weeks, the authorities feel that most anything can happen. They point out that since the slaying of Jen Pao-an, "Reformed Government" official, 19 days ago, no less than five other shootings, all of a political nature, have taken place in this city.

Seven Killed

Including the Jen Pao-an affair, seven persons have been killed and 12 others wounded in political shootings alone. In addition, two other murders have been reported to the police, one in the French Concession and one in the Settlement. The latter two killings, it is believed, were ordinary gang slayings, possibly prompted by revenge motives.

No matter what the motive, the murder toll in the Settlement and the French Concession during these past 19 days is nine, a record for this city. And among the victims were four prominent Chinese individuals, all persons allegedly connected with the local and Japanese sponsored Reformed Government.

These four people were:

Jen Pao-an, "Reformed Government" Land Bureau chief, shot down on the night of June 18, in a Foochow Road restaurant.

Koo Shing-yi, rice taipan and allegedly a member of the Shanghai Citizens' Civic Federation, a pro-Japanese organization. Koo was assassinated on June 25 in front of his offices in an alleyway off Rue Montauban.

Chen Teh-ming, one-time detective of the Shanghai Municipal Police and chief tax collector of the shipping control bureau of the "Reformed Government". He was shot and killed on Yu Ya Chung Road, June 29.

General Chow Lu-wu, former army officer, and alleged head of a pro-Japanese terrorist organization. He was killed in the Oriental Hotel on Nanking Road, Monday afternoon, July 4.

The two other political shootings occurred on the afternoon and evening of Friday, June 20. Three men were wounded, one fatally, in a shooting in Room 407, Sun Sun Hotel, while two men were wounded, one fatally, in a shooting in the law offices of Mr. Wu Zang-yu, 81 Lloyd Road.
pages.zh:
本地警察
今日采取严厉措施

增派巡逻以遏制
可能的恐怖活动

鉴于担心今天——即中国当前战争第一周年纪念日——会发生涉及炸弹袭击、暗杀和其他恐怖活动的骚乱，国际租界和法租界的警察昨晚采取了预防措施，旨在遏制或防止涉及犯罪的事件发生。

中央区和老闸区的特别警察巡逻队已被指派于今天凌晨4点开始工作。昨天全天运作的搜查队一直工作到午夜。他们还计划于今天黎明恢复工作。

除了警察巡逻外，据悉上海义勇队的俄罗斯团将全天保持待命状态，准备应对任何紧急情况。海福尔高地人团的分遣队将像往常一样沿南京路执行巡逻任务，但有报道称，这些人员的特别巡逻队将保持待命，以备紧急任务之需。

如果今天发生麻烦，警方倾向于认为最可能集中在南京路的百货公司区，或福州路沿线的中央区。虽然当局不对可能发生的情况做出预测，但他们肯定不愿冒险，实际上每名警官，无论是便衣还是制服警察，都将承担额外的勤务。

鉴于过去几周租界内暗杀数量增加，当局觉得任何事情都可能发生。他们指出，自19天前“维新政府”官员任葆安被杀以来，本市至少又发生了五起其他枪击案，均具有政治性质。

七人死亡

包括任葆安一案在内，仅政治枪击案就有7人死亡，12人受伤。此外，警方还接到两起其他谋杀案的报告，一起发生在法租界，另一起发生在租界。据信，后两起杀人案是普通的帮派谋杀，可能是出于报复动机。

无论动机如何，在过去19天里，租界和法租界的谋杀死亡人数达到9人，创下了本市的历史纪录。受害者中有四名显赫的中国人，据称都与当地及日本支持的“维新政府”有关。

这四人分别是：

任葆安，“维新政府”地政局局长，6月18日晚在福州路一家餐馆被枪杀。

顾馨一，米业大亨，据称是亲日组织“上海市民协会”成员。顾于6月25日在其蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）旁小巷的办公室前被暗杀。

陈德明，前上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探，兼“维新政府”航运管制局首席税务官。他于6月29日在虞洽卿路被枪杀。

周鲁武将军，前军官，据称是亲日恐怖组织的头目。他于7月4日星期一下午在南京路汇中饭店被杀。

另外两起政治枪击案发生在6月20日星期五的下午和晚上。在新新旅馆407房间的一次枪击中，三人受伤，其中一人致命；而在劳合路81号吴藏玉先生的律师事务所发生的一次枪击中，两人受伤，其中一人致命。

1702

50 Chinese Students Questioned
About 50 Chinese students who
had congregated in the dining hall
of the Chinese YMCA on Boule-
vard de Montigny to partake of a
vegetable diet in observance of the
first anniversary of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities yesterday, were
taken to French police station for
questioning. When it was explain-
ed to the French police that they
were trying to save up money
thereby for relief purposes, they
were immediately released.

All were of good standing
and subsequently released.

昨日，约50名中国学生聚集在蒙蒂尼大道（Boulevard de Montigny）基督教青年会（YMCA）的餐厅内，为纪念中日敌对行动一周年而食素，随后被带往法国警察局接受讯问。当向法国警方解释称他们此举旨在省钱以用于救济目的时，他们随即获释。

July 17, 1938. Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE RICE SITUATION

Lately, the prices of commodities in Shanghai have heavily increased. Fortunately, the price of rice is firm thanks to the efforts of the authorities of the Foreign Settlements and the Customs as well as of those bodies dealing in provisions.
Owing to the increase in local population, certain local public bodies are paying close attention to the question of food supplies and will probably submit the following suggestions to the authorities of the Foreign Settlements :-
(1) That the authorities of the Foreign Settlements be requested to appropriate a large sum of money for the purchase of rice to be held in stock.
(2) That the exportation of rice be strictly prohibited and if necessary a strict ban be also placed on the exportation of all kinds of cereals.
(3) That the price of rice be limited to $14 a picul.
(4) That fines be imposed on traitorous merchants who hoard rice or who manipulate the price of rice.
(5) That measures be drawn up beforehand to facilitate the purchase of rice by poor people.

Ta Ying Yeh Pao of July 16 :-

160 CHINESE ARRESTED ON JULY 7 BY JAPANESE

On the night of July 7 special precautionary measures were adopted by the Japanese military authorities in Hongkew. As a result of a house-to-house search in Hongkew, which lasted until five o'clock the next morning, about 160 persons were arrested.
According to a Japanese statement, this search was made because information had been received to the effect that undesirable elements had entered Hongkew to create disturbances. It was also said that these arrests were made only after definite proofs had been established. It is learned that half of the arrested persons are still in the custody of the Japanese.
It is to be noted that the residents in Hongkew are all registered with the puppet organizations and are issued with passes. Consequently, undesirable elements are finding it difficult to enter the district without discovery.

News Digest :-

CHINESE TRAITORS TO BE ORGANIZED

In order to organize Chinese traitors, the Japanese authorities are making strenuous efforts to inaugurate an "All People's Party" (全民党) in Central

1938年7月17日。晨间译件

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

米粮局势

近期，上海物价大幅上涨。幸得租界当局、海关以及粮食业同业公会等机构努力，米价尚属稳定。
鉴于本地人口增加，某些本地公共团体正密切关注粮食供应问题，并可能向租界当局提交以下建议：
(1) 请租界当局拨出巨款购买大米作为储备。
(2) 严禁大米出口，如有必要，亦应严格禁止各类谷物出口。
(3) 将米价限制在每担14元。
(4) 对囤积大米或操纵米价的奸商处以罚款。
(5) 预先制定措施，以便贫民购买大米。

7月16日《大英夜报》：

日本人于7月7日逮捕160名中国人

7月7日晚，日本军方当局在虹口采取了特别预防措施。通过对虹口地区进行挨户搜查，直至次日凌晨五时，约160人被捕。
据日方声明，此次搜查是因为收到情报，称有不良分子进入虹口制造骚乱。另称，这些逮捕行动仅在确凿证据成立后才实施。据悉，被捕者中有一半仍由日军拘押。
值得注意的是，虹口居民均在伪组织登记并领取通行证。因此，不良分子难以在不被发现的情况下进入该区。

《新闻摘要》：

拟组织中国汉奸

为了组织中国汉奸，日本当局正竭力在中部地区发起成立一个“全民党”

July 8, 1938.                                      Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE SINO-JAPANESE HOSTILITIES

In accordance with the measures drawn up by
the National Government, local schools, public bodies,
factories and shops hoisted the national flag yesterday,
while all amusements and entertainments were suspended
and the people observed a vegetarian diet to commemorate
the first anniversary of the War of Resistance. A
three-minute silence was observed at noon.
Strict precautionary measures were taken by
the authorities of the two Foreign Settlements. The
Settlement Police, assisted by the S.V.C., patrolled the
streets and made strict searches of all suspicious persons,
especially on The Bund and in the hotels. Many armoured
cars of the French Police stood on guard at the corner of
Avenue Edward VII and The Bund, while policemen on duty at
posts adjacent to Nantao and the Western District searched
pedestrians. At certain places communications were
suspended. The British and American Defence Forces
stood by.
The Sincere's and Sun Sun's Roof Gardens
and other amusement resorts were closed yesterday, while
most of the Chinese radio broadcasting stations were silent.
Few parties were noticed in restaurants and many engagements
were postponed.
Contributions, consisting of money saved by
a vegetarian diet, were sent to benevolent bodies.

Standard and other local newspapers :-

13 Cases of Bombing Outrages and Shooting

(1) The first bombing incident occurred in
the vicinity of North Thibet Road and Alabaster Road,
International Settlement, at 5.05 a.m. yesterday when
3 Chinese youths hurled 3 bombs at a Japanese sentry, but
the missile failed to explode. The Japanese sentry
immediately opened fire indiscriminately, killing two
Chinese and wounding two others, all of whom were ricksha
coolies. The names of the wounded coolies are: Loh Yeu-
fah (隆友發), age 62, injured in the left arm, and
Chen Ching-ya (陳正協), age 42, injured in the right
leg. The names of the dead are unknown. The place
was closed to traffic shortly after the incident.
(2) At 5.18 a.m. two hand grenades were
thrown at the Kung Dah Cotton Mill (公大紗廠), Jessfield
Road, in the extra-Settlement Roads area in the Western
District. Nobody was injured but some damage was done
to windows.
(3) At 5.20 a.m. two hand grenades were
hurled at the dormitory of the employees of the Japan-
China Cotton Mill at No. 250 Penang Road. There were no
casualties.
(4) At 5.21 a.m. a Japanese employee of the
Nagai Wata Kaisha was shot at six times and instantly
killed by persons unknown at Ying Hwa Li (櫻華里) on
Robison Road near Ferry Road.

1938年7月8日。                                      晨间译件。

《大美晚报》及其他本地报纸：

中日敌对行动周年纪念

根据国民政府制定的措施，本地学校、公共团体、工厂和商店昨日悬挂国旗，所有娱乐活动暂停，民众食素以纪念抗战一周年。中午时分默哀三分钟。
两租界当局采取了严格的预防措施。租界巡捕在义勇军（S.V.C.）的协助下巡逻街道，并对所有可疑人员进行严密搜查，尤其是在外滩和旅馆区域。法国警察的多辆装甲车在爱德华七世大道与外滩交界处警戒，而在邻近南市和西区岗位的警察则搜查行人。部分地区通讯中断。英美防务部队待命。
先施公司和永安公司的屋顶花园及其他娱乐场所昨日关闭，大多数中文广播电台停播。餐馆内鲜见聚会，许多宴请推迟。
由食素省下的钱款组成的捐款已送往慈善团体。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

13起炸弹袭击和枪击案件

(1) 第一起炸弹事件发生在昨日凌晨5时05分，地点位于公共租界北西藏路与阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）附近，当时3名中国青年向一名日本哨兵投掷了3枚炸弹，但炸弹未爆炸。该日本哨兵立即随意开火，打死两名中国人，打伤另外两人，死者与伤者均为黄包车夫。受伤车夫姓名为：隆友發，62岁，左臂受伤；陳正協，42岁，右腿受伤。死者姓名不详。事发后不久，该地交通封锁。
(2) 凌晨5时18分，两枚手榴弹被投向西区越界筑路地段极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的公大紗廠。无人受伤，但部分窗户受损。
(3) 凌晨5时20分，两枚手榴弹被投向彭路250号日华纱厂员工宿舍。无伤亡。
(4) 凌晨5时21分，永井棉业公司（Nagai Wata Kaisha）的一名日本雇员在罗便臣道（Robison Road）靠近摆渡路（Ferry Road）处的樱华里（Ying Hwa Li）被身份不明者连开六枪，当场毙命。

pages.en:
July 8, 1938. Morning Translation

(5) At 5.30 a.m. three bombs were hurled at
the Nagai Wata Kaisha Cotton Mill at the junction of Gordon
Road and Penang Road. An Indian watchman was wounded in
the hand and was later removed to the Country Hospital for
treatment.
(6) At 5.45 a.m. another Japanese employee of
the Nagai Wata Kaisha No.9 Cotton Mill, while passing by
the corner of Markham Road and Tonquin Road in a vehicle,
was shot at four times. He was removed to Foo Min Hospital
where he later died of his wounds.
(7) At 6 a.m. a bomb was thrown at the Shanghai
Land Investment Company at No.120 Jinkee Road, damaging some
window frames and panes.
(8) At 6 a.m. two bombs were thrown at the
Yokohama Specie Bank on the Bund. According to a report
made by the Japanese, the two missiles exploded wounding
an unknown Chinese. This report, however, could not be
confirmed.
(9) At 6 a.m. a bomb exploded at the Japanese
Water Police Headquarters at the Peking Road Jetty.
According to the Japanese version, an interpreter was
slightly injured. The Japanese sentry immediately opened
fire, killing one and wounding another Chinese. The latter
was removed to Chinese Lester Hospital for treatment. A
motor truck driver was detained because a hand grenade was
found on his truck.
(10) At 6 a.m. a hand grenade was hurled by
some person unknown at the Japanese sentry on Szechuen Road
Bridge, but the missile failed to explode.
(11) At 6.05 a.m. a bomb was thrown into the
residence of a Japanese army officer on Macao Road. Slight
damage was done.
(12) At 7 a.m. some person or persons unknown
hurled a bomb from the vicinity of the Wusih Fellow Country-
men's Association at two Japanese sentries standing on
Haining Road near North Chekiang Road, Chapel. The sentries
were slightly wounded.
(13) At 7 a.m. a bomb-throwing took place in
the vicinity of North Thibet Road. Another hand grenade
was understood to have been thrown from Boundary Road at
the Shanghai North Station. There were no casualties.

News Digest and other local newspapers :-

Handbills Supporting The War Of Resistance
Distributed Locally

Between 10 p.m. July 6 and 2 p.m. July 7, eleven
cases of distribution of handbills took place in the
International Settlement as follows :-
(1) 10.40 p.m. July 6 on Gordon Road near Pootoo Road.
(2) 5 a.m. July 7. Handbills distributed from a motor car
proceeding on Nanking Road from west to east.
(3) 5.10 a.m. July 7 on Penang Road near Gordon Road.
(4) 5.20 a.m. July 7 on Honan Road near Nanking Road.
(5) 5.40 a.m. July 7. Handbills distributed everywhere
on Pootoo Road.
(6) 8 a.m. July 7 on Avenue Road.
(7) 8.10 a.m. July 7 on Nanking Road near Yu Ya Ching Road.

1938年7月8日。晨间译件

(5) 凌晨5时30分，三枚炸弹被投向戈登路与彭路交界处的永井棉业公司纱厂。一名印度看守手部受伤，后被送往宏恩医院（Country Hospital）治疗。
(6) 凌晨5时45分，永井棉业公司第九纱厂的另一名日本雇员乘车经过马克姆路（Markham Road）与唐昆路（Tonquin Road）转角时，被连开四枪。他被送往福民医院，后因伤重不治身亡。
(7) 上午6时，一枚炸弹被投向金基路120号的上海地产投资公司，损坏了一些窗框和玻璃。
(8) 上午6时，两枚炸弹被投向外滩的横滨正金银行。据日方报告，两枚炸弹爆炸，致一名身份不明的中国人受伤。然而，此报告未能得到证实。
(9) 上午6时，一枚炸弹在北京路码头日本水上警察总部爆炸。据日方说法，一名翻译受轻伤。日本哨兵立即开火，打死一名中国人，打伤另一名中国人。后者被送往华人莱斯德医院（Chinese Lester Hospital）治疗。一名卡车司机因车上发现一枚手榴弹而被扣留。
(10) 上午6时，身份不明者向四川路桥上的日本哨兵投掷了一枚手榴弹，但未爆炸。
(11) 上午6时05分，一枚炸弹被投入澳门路一名日本军官的寓所。造成轻微破坏。
(12) 上午7时，身份不明者从无锡同乡会附近向站在海宁路靠近北浙江路教堂处的两名日本哨兵投掷了一枚炸弹。哨兵受轻伤。
(13) 上午7时，北西藏路附近发生投弹事件。据悉，另一枚手榴弹是从界路向上海北站投掷的。无伤亡。

《新闻摘要》及其他本地报纸：

支持抗战的传单在本地分发

7月6日晚上10时至7月7日下午2时之间，公共租界内发生了11起分发传单事件，具体如下：
(1) 7月6日晚上10时40分，戈登路靠近普陀路处。
(2) 7月7日上午5时。传单从一辆由西向东行驶在南京路上的汽车上分发。
(3) 7月7日上午5时10分，彭路靠近戈登路处。
(4) 7月7日上午5时20分，河南路靠近南京路处。
(5) 7月7日上午5时40分。普陀路上各处分发传单。
(6) 7月7日上午8时，爱文义路（Avenue Road）。
(7) 7月7日上午8时10分，南京路靠近虞洽卿路处。

July 8, 1938. Morning Translation.

(8) 8.20 a.m. July 7 on Moulmein Road.
(9) 8.50 a.m. July 7 at the Jessfield Park.
(10) 11.10 a.m. July 7 on Foochow Road near Yu Ya Ching Road.
(11) 1.40 p.m. July 7. Handbills distributed from a bus
passing Avenue Edward VII near Lungmen Road.
The handbills were of different kinds and were
issued by different organizations. Of all these handbills,
the following five kinds were the most important :-
1) Handbill calling upon local Chinese residents to deal
with traitors.
2) Handbill praising the strength of the Chinese Air Force
and calling on residents to offer their gold to the
government for the purchase of aeroplanes.
3) Handbill praising the Ministry of Finance of the
National Government for its control of foreign exchange
as it is beneficial to China's finance during the period
of the war of resistance and advising residents to render
every assistance to the government.
4) Handbill declaring the unification of China and refuting
reports that disputes had arisen between one clique and
another or that a certain prominent government official
was in disagreement with another, for these reports had
been fabricated by a certain party or traitors.
5) Handbill urging capitalists to develop the interior.

Between 4 and 7 p.m. yesterday, patriotic
pamphlets were discovered on Nanking Road. At 4.30 p.m.
several kinds of handbills were thrown from a No. 2 Route
bus in front of the Sun Company, Nanking Road. Four
passengers were arrested by the Police on suspicion of
having thrown the handbills.

Standard and other local newspapers :-

Search Conducted by Plain-Clothes Japanese

At about 9 p.m. yesterday some 30 Japanese in
civilian clothes appeared at the corner of Avenue Edward VII
and Kingse Road and conducted a search of pedestrians.
On learning of the affair and fearing that it might lead
to disturbances in the Settlement, a company of Scotch
soldiers, with two armoured cars, were immediately
dispatched to the scene to maintain order. When they
perceived the British soldiers coming, the Japanese left
in the direction of the Bund, followed by the British
soldiers and their armoured cars.
At about 10 p.m. Japanese gendarmes searched
pedestrians on Honan Road.

News Digest :-

At about 5 p.m. yesterday, some 30 Japanese
in plain clothes carried out a search of pedestrians on
Szechuen Road and vicinity. When the Municipal Police
learned of this, British soldiers were detailed to the spot
in an armoured car. The plain clothes Japanese then moved
away in the direction of the Bund.
After 10 p.m. yesterday, a large party of armed
Japanese gendarmes searched pedestrians at the corner of
Honan Road and Avenue Edward VII. The authorities of the
International Settlement at once detailed British soldiers
to the place in three armoured cars to maintain peace and
order. The two parties stood against each other and the
situation for a time was critical. At 11 p.m. the
Japanese gendarmes withdrew.
